title: Seasonal dynamics and burden of respiratory syncytial virus, influenza, and COVID-19 in Brazil: a national surveillance study (2019–2023)
abstract: Background: The burden and seasonal patterns of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), influenza, and COVID-19 remain poorly characterised in Brazil and other Latin American countries. Understanding their epidemiological patterns is essential to inform public health interventions and preventive strategies. We aimed to assess respiratory virus seasonality using national surveillance data to guide vaccination timing and strengthen preparedness strategies in Brazil. Methods: We conducted a retrospective, observational, descriptive population-based study using national surveillance data collected through the SIVEP system between 2019 and 2023. We analysed confirmed cases, hospitalisations, and deaths attributed to RSV, influenza, and COVID-19. We performed time-series decomposition and seasonal trend analysis using the multiple seasonal-trend decomposition via locally estimated scatterplot smoothing method. We calculated monthly mean values for each aetiology component to assess their seasonal burden. Results: There were 69,389 RSV, 45,881 influenza, and 2,299,712 COVID-19 cases among the laboratory-confirmed severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) cases reported in SIVEP. Each year, more than 90% of RSV diagnoses were reported in children aged 0-10 years, while influenza and COVID-19 were more common among older adults. The proportion of deaths in children related to RSV increased from 19.2% in 2020 to 62.0% in 2023. Seasonal peaks occurred from March to June for RSV, influenza cases peaked in January, while COVID-19 showed less consistent seasonality. Geographic variation was observed, with higher case concentrations in the Southeast and South regions of Brazil. Conclusions: The burden of respiratory viruses among SARI cases reported in the national surveillance system in Brazil differed by pathogen, age group, region, and season, and may be influenced by variations in testing strategies. Strengthening diagnostic capacity and surveillance is critical, particularly for adult RSV cases, which are likely underreported due to limited testing and reduced diagnostic sensitivity. Seasonal vaccination programmes, such as those for influenza, remain essential and may be further enhanced by integrating new preventive measures, such as RSV vaccination for older adults and maternal immunisation to protect infants.

title_zh: 巴西 呼吸道合胞病毒、流感和 COVID-19 的季节性动态和负担:国家 呼吸道合胞病毒 研究(2019-2023 年)
source_body_en: Background: The burden and seasonal patterns of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), influenza, and COVID-19 remain poorly characterised in Brazil and other Latin American countries. Understanding their epidemiological patterns is essential to inform public health interventions and preventive strategies. We aimed to assess respiratory virus seasonality using national surveillance data to guide vaccination timing and strengthen preparedness strategies in Brazil. Methods: We conducted a retrospective, observational, descriptive population-based study using national surveillance data collected through the SIVEP system between 2019 and 2023. We analysed confirmed cases, hospitalisations, and deaths attributed to RSV, influenza, and COVID-19. We performed time-series decomposition and seasonal trend analysis using the multiple seasonal-trend decomposition via locally estimated scatterplot smoothing method. We calculated monthly mean values for each aetiology component to assess their seasonal burden. Results: There were 69,389 RSV, 45,881 influenza, and 2,299,712 COVID-19 cases among the laboratory-confirmed severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) cases reported in SIVEP. Each year, more than 90% of RSV diagnoses were reported in children aged 0-10 years, while influenza and COVID-19 were more common among older adults. The proportion of deaths in children related to RSV increased from 19.2% in 2020 to 62.0% in 2023. Seasonal peaks occurred from March to June for RSV, influenza cases peaked in January, while COVID-19 showed less consistent seasonality. Geographic variation was observed, with higher case concentrations in the Southeast and South regions of Brazil. Conclusions: The burden of respiratory viruses among SARI cases reported in the national surveillance system in Brazil differed by pathogen, age group, region, and season, and may be influenced by variations in testing strategies. Strengthening diagnostic capacity and surveillance is critical, particularly for adult RSV cases, which are likely underreported due to limited testing and reduced diagnostic sensitivity. Seasonal vaccination programmes, such as those for influenza, remain essential and may be further enhanced by integrating new preventive measures, such as RSV vaccination for older adults and maternal immunisation to protect infants.
abstract_zh: 背景:在巴西和其他拉丁美洲国家,呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV)、流感和 COVID-19 的负担和季节性模式仍然不明确。了解其流行病学模式对于为公共卫生干预措施和预防策略提供信息至关重要。我们的目的是使用国家 监测 数据评估呼吸道病毒的季节性,以指导 疫苗接种 时间安排并加强巴西的准备策略。方法:我们使用 2019 年至 2023 年间通过 SIVEP 系统收集的国家 监测 数据进行了一项回顾性、观察性、描述性人群研究。我们分析了由 RSV、流感和 COVID-19 引起的确诊病例、住院和死亡。我们通过局部估计散点图平滑方法使用多重季节趋势分解进行时间序列分解和季节趋势分析。我们计算了每个病因学组成部分的月平均值,以评估其季节性负担。结果:SIVEP 报告的实验室确诊严重急性呼吸道感染 (SARI) 病例中,有 69,389 例 RSV 病例、45,881 例流感病例和 2,299,712 例 COVID-19 病例。每年,超过 90% 的 RSV 诊断发生在 0-10 岁儿童中,而流感和 COVID-19 在老年人中更为常见。与 RSV 相关的儿童死亡比例从 2020 年的 19.2% 增加到 2023 年的 62.0%。RSV 的季节性高峰出现在 3 月至 6 月,流感病例在 1 月达到高峰,而 COVID-19 的季节性高峰则不太一致。观察到地理差异,巴西东南部和南部地区病例集中度较高。结论:巴西国家 监测 系统报告的 SARI 病例中呼吸道病毒负担因病原体、年龄组、地区和季节而异,并且可能受到检测策略变化的影响。加强诊断能力和 监测 至关重要,特别是对于成人 RSV 病例,由于检测有限和诊断敏感性降低,这些病例可能漏报。季节性 疫苗接种 计划(例如针对流感的计划)仍然至关重要,并且可以通过整合新的预防措施(例如针对老年人的 RSV 疫苗接种 和保护婴儿的孕产妇免疫接种)来进一步加强。

title: Diagnostic accuracy of a molecular-based point-of-care test for rapid detection of respiratory syncytial virus in children admitted to high-dependency care in Nepal
abstract: Background Rapid respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) diagnostics are largely unavailable in low-resource settings. We compared the diagnostic accuracy of a molecular-based point-of-care test (POCT) with standard reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) in children admitted to high-dependency care. Methods We analysed data from a larger study (RSV GOLD - ICU Network study) in two Nepali tertiary hospitals over two respiratory seasons. Children aged ≥4 days and Results We analysed 124 randomly selected stored samples, of whom 70 (56.5%) tested positive with POCT and 74 (59.7%) with RT-PCR. The median cycle threshold (CT) value was 29.1 (interquartile range = 25.1-33.4). All cases with false-negative POCT had low viral loads (CT value >31). The sensitivity (93.2%; 95% confidence interval (CI) = 86.0, 97.5), specificity (98.0%; 95% CI = 91.5, 99.9), positive predictive values (98.6%; 95% CI = 93.9, 99.9), and negative predictive values (90.7%; 95% CI = 81.1, 96.6) of POCT for RSV infection were all satisfactory. Conclusions We conducted the first prospective study showing excellent accuracy of molecular RSV POCT in a poor resource setting. Affordable molecular-based POCT in resource-constrained settings can improve care of children with acute respiratory infections and strengthen surveillance for vaccine effectiveness during rollout of RSV interventions.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估基于分子的现场护理测试 (POCT) 的诊断准确性,该测试可快速检测在资源匮乏地区接受高度依赖护理的儿童中的 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV),而这些地区基本上无法进行快速诊断。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究在尼泊尔两家三级医院进行了两个呼吸季节,分析了一项大型研究(RSV GOLD - ICU 网络研究)的数据,该研究涉及 124 个随机选择的 4 天以上儿童的储存样本。
elements_zh.methods: 使用存储的样本将基于分子的 POCT 的诊断准确性与标准逆转录聚合酶链反应 (RT-PCR) 进行比较。该研究分析了尼泊尔两家三级医院在两个呼吸季节进行的一项更大规模前瞻性研究的数据。
elements_zh.main_results: 在 124 份样本中,70 份(56.5%)经 POCT 检测呈阳性,74 份(59.7%)经 RT-PCR 检测呈阳性。中位周期阈值 (CT) 值为 29.1(四分位数范围 = 25.1-33.4)。所有 POCT 假阴性病例的病毒载量均较低(CT 值 >31)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将研究结果解释为,基于分子的 POCT 在资源有限的环境中对 RSV 检测具有出色的准确性,正如其高灵敏度和特异性所证明的那样。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,负担得起的基于分子的 POCT 可以改善急性呼吸道感染儿童的护理,并在推出 RSV 干预措施期间增强 监测 的 疫苗 有效性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其对存储样本的依赖而受到限制,这可能会引入潜在的偏差,并且分析是基于单个呼吸季节。由于这些限制,证据的强度中等。

title: Respiratory Syncytial Virus Vaccine Effectiveness in Medicare Beneficiaries Residing in Nursing Homes
abstract: IMPORTANCE: Vaccine effectiveness (VE) estimates are needed to determine the effectiveness of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccinations during their first season of availability among populations at high risk for severe RSV. OBJECTIVE: To assess RSV VE against RSV-associated outcomes for nursing home residents. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This retrospective cohort study of Medicare fee-for-service beneficiaries used electronic medical claims data from September 10, 2023, to March 30, 2024. A cohort was created for each outcome: an RSV-associated hospitalization cohort; an RSV-associated death cohort; a severe RSV-associated outcome cohort; and an RSV-associated thromboembolic event cohort. To be eligible for inclusion in a cohort, a Medicare fee-for-service beneficiary must be aged 65 years or older, reside in a US nursing home during the study period for at least 1 day, have continuous enrollment in Medicare Parts A and B (365 days prior to the index date), and have continuous enrollment in Part D (beginning on June 21, 2023). EXPOSURE: RSV vaccination. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Outcomes were RSV-associated hospitalization, RSV-associated death, severe RSV-associated outcomes (intensive care unit or critical care unit admission, medical ventilator use, or RSV-associated death), and RSV-associated thromboembolic event. RSV diagnoses and outcome definitions were based on claims with relevant International Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, Tenth Revision codes. RSV vaccine doses were determined from Medicare Part D claims using the National Drug Code Directory. Hazard ratios (HRs) from multivariable Cox proportional hazards models compared the times to first outcomes among RSV vaccinated beneficiaries and unvaccinated beneficiaries. VE was calculated as (1-HR) × 100%. RESULTS: Of 597 430 included Medicare beneficiaries (66% female; median age, 82 [IQR, 75-88] years), RSV VE against RSV-associated hospitalizations was 73% (95% CI, 65%-79%). Among beneficiaries aged 65 to 74 years VE was 60% (95% CI, 35%-76%), 75% (95% CI, 67%-82%) among beneficiaries 75 years or older, 67% (95% CI, 55%-76%) among short-stay residents (<100 cumulative days), and 80% (95% CI, 68%-87%) among long-stay residents (≥100 cumulative days). VE against RSV-associated death was 56% (95% CI, 39%-69%), VE against severe RSV-associated outcomes was 59% (95% CI, 44%-70%), and VE against RSV-associated thromboembolic events was 66% (95% CI, 44%-79%). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this study, in the first season of availability, RSV vaccines were associated with improved RSV-associated outcomes among US Medicare beneficiaries residing in nursing homes.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the effectiveness of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccines among Medicare beneficiaries residing in nursing homes during their first season of availability. Using electronic medical claims data from September 10, 2023, to March 30, 2024, the researchers created cohorts based on RSV-associated outcomes, including hospitalization, death, severe outcomes, and thromboembolic events. VE against RSV-associated death was 56%, against severe outcomes was 59%, and against thromboembolic events was 66%. The study highlights the potential benefits of RSV vaccination in high-risk populations but notes limitations due to the observational nature of the data and possible confounding factors. These findings may inform future public health strategies for RSV prevention in nursing home settings.

title: Respiratory Syncytial Virus Symptomatic Fraction, Shedding and Detection in Children Aged 6–23 Months in South Africa in 2022
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Accurate detection of RSV infections is important to understand epidemiology. We estimated symptomatic fraction and shedding duration of reverse‐transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT‐PCR)‐confirmed cases and compared RSV detection through molecular and serologic techniques. Methods We enrolled healthy children aged 6–23 months in a prospective cohort study, from May to October 2022, collecting thrice‐weekly mid‐turbinate nasal swabs for RSV RT‐PCR testing. We collected serum at baseline and end of follow‐up and detected anti‐RSV IgG using enzyme‐linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) and multipathogen bead‐based immunoassay (MIA). We ascertained symptoms by twice‐weekly nurse visits, and daily caregiver symptom diaries. We calculated sensitivity, specificity, and positive (PPV) and negative (NPV) predictive value of RT‐PCR, ELISA, and MIA compared to a standard (two or more assays‐positive) among children with paired sera and baseline blood preceding an RT‐PCR–confirmed episode. Results The RSV season started mid‐February 2022. We enrolled 93 participants; 87 (94%) followed to the final study visit. Forty individuals had one or more RT‐PCR–confirmed RSV infection, and six of them had a repeat episode. One‐or‐more symptom was reported from 54% (25/46) of RT‐PCR–confirmed episodes, fever in 26% (12/46), and cough in 37% (17/46). Median RNA shedding duration was 7 days (IQR = 4–11 days). Among 80 children meeting criteria, ELISA and MIA each had > 92% sensitivity, specificity, PPV, and NPV while RT‐PCR had 78% (95% CI = 61%–90%) sensitivity, 98% (95% CI = 88–100%) specificity, 97% (95% CI = 82%–100%) PPV, and 84% (95% CI = 71%–93%) NPV. Discussion Approximately half of RSV episodes were symptomatic. Serology had a high sensitivity and specificity for infection identification.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to estimate the symptomatic fraction and shedding duration of RSV infections in children aged 6–23 months in South Africa in 2022. A prospective cohort study was conducted from May to October 2022, enrolling 93 healthy children and collecting nasal swabs and serum samples for RT-PCR and serologic testing. The RSV season began mid-February 2022, with 54% of RT-PCR–confirmed episodes reporting symptoms, 26% with fever, and 37% with cough. Median RNA shedding duration was 7 days. The study found that ELISA and MIA had high sensitivity and specificity, while RT-PCR had moderate performance. The authors interpreted that about half of RSV episodes were symptomatic, offering new insights into the clinical presentation of RSV in this age group. These findings can inform surveillance and diagnostic strategies. The study's evidence is strong but limited by its small sample size and reliance on self-reported symptoms.

title: Hospital Admissions for Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) Among Elderly: A Retrospective Study From an Italian Southern Region During Years 2018–2023
abstract: ABSTRACT Introduction Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is one of the most common causes of acute respiratory infections in both children and adults over 60. RSV can cause severe lower respiratory tract infections in older adults, leading to an increase of morbidity and mortality. The aim of this study was to assess the incidence of hospitalizations due to RSV infections in the Abruzzo region of Italy among patients aged over 60 years. Methods A retrospective study was performed in the Abruzzo region, evaluating all hospitalizations performed during years 2018–2023. Age‐ and gender‐standardized hospitalization rates for RSV were calculated. Patients' comorbidities and hospitalization‐related outcomes were also assessed. Results During 2018–2023, 42 RSV‐coded hospitalizations were identified among adults aged ≥ 60 years. An additional RSV‐attributable burden was estimated by applying a literature‐derived attributable fraction to hospitalizations for unspecified viral bronchiolitis and pneumonia, resulting in an estimated total of 67 RSV‐attributable admissions. Annual age‐ and sex‐standardized RSV‐coded hospitalization rates showed substantial year‐to‐year variability. Poisson regression with correction for overdispersion identified no statistically significant temporal trend during the study period (IRR per calendar year 1.08, 95% CI 0.86–1.34; p = 0.516). Among patients with RSV‐coded admissions, the median length of stay was 11 days (IQR 6–18), and four patients (9.52%) died during hospitalization. Conclusions RSV was associated with a measurable burden of hospitalization among older adults in Abruzzo. However, substantial year‐to‐year variability and the small number of RSV‐coded admissions warrant cautious interpretation of temporal patterns. No statistically significant temporal trend was identified during the study period.

title_zh: 老年人 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 入院情况:2018-2023 年意大利南部地区的回顾性研究
source_body_en: ABSTRACT Introduction Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is one of the most common causes of acute respiratory infections in both children and adults over 60. RSV can cause severe lower respiratory tract infections in older adults, leading to an increase of morbidity and mortality. The aim of this study was to assess the incidence of hospitalizations due to RSV infections in the Abruzzo region of Italy among patients aged over 60 years. Methods A retrospective study was performed in the Abruzzo region, evaluating all hospitalizations performed during years 2018–2023. Age‐ and gender‐standardized hospitalization rates for RSV were calculated. Patients' comorbidities and hospitalization‐related outcomes were also assessed. Results During 2018–2023, 42 RSV‐coded hospitalizations were identified among adults aged ≥ 60 years. An additional RSV‐attributable burden was estimated by applying a literature‐derived attributable fraction to hospitalizations for unspecified viral bronchiolitis and pneumonia, resulting in an estimated total of 67 RSV‐attributable admissions. Annual age‐ and sex‐standardized RSV‐coded hospitalization rates showed substantial year‐to‐year variability. Poisson regression with correction for overdispersion identified no statistically significant temporal trend during the study period (IRR per calendar year 1.08, 95% CI 0.86–1.34; p = 0.516). Among patients with RSV‐coded admissions, the median length of stay was 11 days (IQR 6–18), and four patients (9.52%) died during hospitalization. Conclusions RSV was associated with a measurable burden of hospitalization among older adults in Abruzzo. However, substantial year‐to‐year variability and the small number of RSV‐coded admissions warrant cautious interpretation of temporal patterns. No statistically significant temporal trend was identified during the study period.

title: Cardiovascular Outcomes and Acute Human Metapneumovirus Infection in Adults: A Systematic Literature Review.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Acute respiratory viral infections, including influenza, RSV, and SARS-CoV-2, are well-recognized as being associated with cardiovascular events (CVEs). In contrast, the cardiovascular impact of human metapneumovirus (HMPV) remains poorly characterized. We aimed to describe the prevalence of pre-existing cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) and the incidence of acute CVEs in adults with laboratory-confirmed HMPV infection. METHODS: PRISMA-guided systematic literature review of MEDLINE, Embase, and Google Scholar (Jan.-2000/Sept.-2025). Observational studies and clinical trials reporting pre-existing CVDs and/or CVEs in adults (≥18 years) were included. RESULTS: Eighteen studies met the inclusion criteria, of which nine underwent critical appraisal. Most involved hospitalized older adults. Pre-existing CVD was reported in 10%-80% of HMPV-infected patients, with chronic heart failure and coronary artery disease being the most common conditions. Acute CVEs, particularly heart failure exacerbations, occurred in 5%-25% of hospitalized patients. Underlying CVD was consistently linked to increased severity of HMPV illness, including higher rates of ICU admission and mortality. CONCLUSIONS: Acute HMPV infection frequently occurs in adults with pre-existing CVD and may be associated with CVEs in older hospitalized populations. However, evidence remains limited and largely observational. These findings highlight the need to increase awareness of the potential CV complications associated with HMPV infection. TRIAL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO [CRD420251164583].

analysis.summary_en: This systematic literature review investigates the cardiovascular impact of human metapneumovirus (HMPV) infection in adults. It highlights that acute HMPV infection frequently occurs in adults with pre-existing cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) and may be associated with cardiovascular events (CVEs), particularly heart failure exacerbations, in hospitalized older populations. Pre-existing CVD was reported in 10%-80% of HMPV-infected patients, with chronic heart failure and coronary artery disease being the most common conditions. Despite these findings, the evidence remains limited and observational, underscoring the need for further research and heightened awareness of HMPV-related cardiovascular complications in clinical practice.

title: Comparative effectiveness of preventive strategies against medically-attended respiratory syncytial virus in U.S. infants during the first six months of life, 2023-2025
abstract: Importance: Maternal vaccination and long-acting monoclonal antibodies are now available in the U.S. Long-acting monoclonal antibody administration in the U.S. commonly occurs after hospital discharge in outpatient settings, leaving some infants unprotected early in life when severe RSV risk is highest. Comparative effectiveness between the two interventions and whether delays affect effectiveness estimates have not been quantified. Objective: To evaluate the effectiveness of infant long-acting monoclonal antibody strategies and a maternal vaccination strategy, each compared to no intervention, and the comparative effectiveness of intervention strategies when accounting for real-world delays in monoclonal antibody receipt. Design: Cohort study using target trial emulation to compare four strategies for prevention of RSV-related outcomes. between 2023 and 2025 using a nationwide database of employer-sponsored commercial insurance claims. Participants: 120,586 commercially insured mother-infants, whose infants were born in the U.S. during the 2023-2024 or 2024-2025 RSV season. Infants who could not be paired with their mother's record, did not enroll in commercial insurance within 75 days from birth, received palivizumab, and had an implausible birth date were excluded. Interventions: Comparison of four RSV prevention strategies: (i) maternal RSVpreF; (ii) long-acting monoclonal antibody given within the first week of life (mAb as intended); (iii) long-acting monoclonal antibody given within a six-month grace period from birth (mAb within grace period); and (iv) a control. Main outcomes and measures: Effectiveness against first RSV-associated hospitalization and medically-attended RSV illness was summarized using adjusted hazard ratios (aHR) and estimated using an inverse propensity weighting approach, with weights accounting for maternal age, maternal comorbidities affecting pregnancy, obstetric and newborn complications, season, region, and birth timing relative to October 1. A weighted Kaplan Meier estimator was used to estimate strategy-specific cumulative incidence of RSV outcomes over time. Results: In the first five weeks of life, the mAb within grace period strategy doubled the hazard of RSV hospitalization (aHR: 2.0 [95% CI: 1.0-4.9]) and increased the hazard of medically-attended RSV (aHR: 1.6 [95% CI: 1.0-2.7]) compared to the maternal RSVpreF strategy. The hazard for RSV hospitalization was similar for the mAb as intended strategy compared to the maternal RSVpreF strategy (aHR = 0.9 [95% CI: 0.3-1.9]). Conclusions and relevance: RSVpreF and monoclonal antibodies were similarly effective when monoclonal antibodies were administered close to birth, but when accounting for real-world delays in monoclonal antibody receipt, the maternal RSVpreF strategy was more effective than the mAb within grace period strategy.

The knowledge gap lies in quantifying how real-world delays affect the effectiveness of these interventions.

analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that RSVpreF and monoclonal antibodies were similarly effective when monoclonal antibodies were administered close to birth, but when accounting for real-world delays, the maternal RSVpreF strategy was more effective than the mAb within grace period strategy. This finding highlights the importance of timing in the effectiveness of monoclonal antibody interventions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform public health strategies for RSV prevention by emphasizing the need for timely administration of monoclonal antibodies and the potential advantages of maternal vaccination in protecting infants during the early period of highest risk.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on commercial insurance claims, which may not capture all cases or represent the entire population. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the observational nature of the study and potential for unmeasured confounding.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the effectiveness of maternal vaccination and long-acting monoclonal antibodies in preventing RSV-related outcomes in U.S. infants during the first six months of life. It compares four strategies: maternal RSVpreF, monoclonal antibody given within the first week of life, monoclonal antibody given within a six-month grace period, and a control. The study uses a nationwide database of commercial insurance claims and employs adjusted hazard ratios and inverse propensity weighting to account for confounding factors. Results show that the mAb within grace period strategy had a higher hazard of RSV hospitalization and medically-attended RSV compared to maternal RSVpreF in the first five weeks of life, while the mAb as intended strategy was similarly effective to maternal RSVpreF. The authors conclude that maternal RSVpreF is more effective when considering real-world delays in monoclonal antibody administration. The study's findings have implications for public health strategies, emphasizing the importance of timely intervention. However, the study's reliance on insurance data and observational design limits the strength of the evidence.

title_zh: 2023-2025 年美国婴儿生命前六个月内就医 呼吸道合胞病毒 的预防策略的有效性比较
source_body_en: Importance: Maternal vaccination and long-acting monoclonal antibodies are now available in the U.S. Long-acting monoclonal antibody administration in the U.S. commonly occurs after hospital discharge in outpatient settings, leaving some infants unprotected early in life when severe RSV risk is highest. Comparative effectiveness between the two interventions and whether delays affect effectiveness estimates have not been quantified. Objective: To evaluate the effectiveness of infant long-acting monoclonal antibody strategies and a maternal vaccination strategy, each compared to no intervention, and the comparative effectiveness of intervention strategies when accounting for real-world delays in monoclonal antibody receipt. Design: Cohort study using target trial emulation to compare four strategies for prevention of RSV-related outcomes. between 2023 and 2025 using a nationwide database of employer-sponsored commercial insurance claims. Participants: 120,586 commercially insured mother-infants, whose infants were born in the U.S. during the 2023-2024 or 2024-2025 RSV season. Infants who could not be paired with their mother's record, did not enroll in commercial insurance within 75 days from birth, received palivizumab, and had an implausible birth date were excluded. Interventions: Comparison of four RSV prevention strategies: (i) maternal RSVpreF; (ii) long-acting monoclonal antibody given within the first week of life (mAb as intended); (iii) long-acting monoclonal antibody given within a six-month grace period from birth (mAb within grace period); and (iv) a control. Main outcomes and measures: Effectiveness against first RSV-associated hospitalization and medically-attended RSV illness was summarized using adjusted hazard ratios (aHR) and estimated using an inverse propensity weighting approach, with weights accounting for maternal age, maternal comorbidities affecting pregnancy, obstetric and newborn complications, season, region, and birth timing relative to October 1. A weighted Kaplan Meier estimator was used to estimate strategy-specific cumulative incidence of RSV outcomes over time. Results: In the first five weeks of life, the mAb within grace period strategy doubled the hazard of RSV hospitalization (aHR: 2.0 [95% CI: 1.0-4.9]) and increased the hazard of medically-attended RSV (aHR: 1.6 [95% CI: 1.0-2.7]) compared to the maternal RSVpreF strategy. The hazard for RSV hospitalization was similar for the mAb as intended strategy compared to the maternal RSVpreF strategy (aHR = 0.9 [95% CI: 0.3-1.9]). Conclusions and relevance: RSVpreF and monoclonal antibodies were similarly effective when monoclonal antibodies were administered close to birth, but when accounting for real-world delays in monoclonal antibody receipt, the maternal RSVpreF strategy was more effective than the mAb within grace period strategy.
abstract_zh: 重要性:母体 疫苗接种 和长效单克隆抗体现已在美国上市。在美国,长效单克隆抗体给药通常发生在出院后的门诊环境中,导致一些婴儿在生命早期严重 RSV 风险最高时得不到保护。两种干预措施之间的有效性比较以及延迟是否影响有效性估计尚未得到量化。目的:评估婴儿长效单克隆抗体策略和母亲 疫苗接种 策略的有效性,分别与无干预进行比较,以及在考虑单克隆抗体接收的实际延迟时干预策略的比较有效性。设计:队列研究 研究使用目标试验模拟来比较四种预防 RSV 相关结果的策略。2023 年至 2025 年间,使用全国范围内雇主资助的商业保险索赔数据库。参与者:120,586 名有商业保险的母婴,其婴儿在 2023-2024 年或 2024-2025 年 RSV 季节期间在美国出生。无法与母亲记录配对、出生后75天内未参加商业保险、接受帕利珠单抗治疗以及出生日期不可信的婴儿被排除在外。干预措施:四种 RSV 预防策略的比较:(i) 母体 RSVpreF;(ii) 在出生后第一周内给予长效单克隆抗体(按预期使用单克隆抗体);(iii) 在出生后六个月的宽限期内给予长效单克隆抗体(宽限期内的单克隆抗体);(iv) 对照。主要结果和措施:使用调整后的风险比(aHR)总结了针对首次 RSV 相关住院和就医 RSV 疾病的有效性,并使用逆倾向加权方法进行了估计,权重考虑了产妇年龄、影响妊娠的孕产妇合并症、产科和新生儿并发症、季节、地区和相对于 10 月 1 日的出生时间。使用加权 Kaplan Meier 估计器来估计 RSV 结果的特定策略累积 发病率时间。结果:在出生后的前五周,与母体 RSVpreF 策略相比,宽限期内使用 mAb 策略使 RSV 住院风险加倍(aHR:2.0 [95% CI:1.0-4.9]),并增加就医 RSV 风险(aHR:1.6 [95% CI:1.0-2.7])。与母体 RSVpreF 策略相比,mAb 预期策略的 RSV 住院风险相似 (aHR = 0.9 [95% CI: 0.3-1.9])。结论和相关性:当临近出生时施用单克隆抗体时,RSVpreF 和单克隆抗体的效果相似,但考虑到单克隆抗体接收的实际延迟时,母体 RSVpreF 策略比宽限期内的 mAb 策略更有效。

title: Impact of respiratory syncytial virus immunization in older adults: the importance of a valid burden estimation
abstract: ABSTRACT Introduction In the province of Québec, Canada, a respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) immunization program restricted to seniors residing in long-term care facilities (LTCF) and those aged ≥75 years from private senior residences (PSR) was implemented in Fall 2024, with approximately 65% vaccine uptake in the targeted populations. Despite high vaccine effectiveness, the real-world impact of the RSV immunization program on population-level averted hospitalizations and the influence that RSV diagnostic test performance might have remains unknown. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of the first season (2024-25) of the intervention among older adults in Québec while accounting for laboratory test performance. Methods A prospective hospital-based surveillance (HospiVir) and health administrative databases were used to assess the intervention impact. Observed to expected approach and before/after ecological design using a difference-in-difference Poisson regression, both accounting for seasonal variations and trends in comparison groups, were used. Hospitalization incidence rate estimates based on hospital-based surveillance were adjusted for the laboratory test performances using Lash equations. Results Based on HospiVir, a 49% (95% confidence interval (CI): -80– -5) decrease in RSV-associated hospitalizations was observed among adults aged ≥75 years residing in PSR. This decrease was 23% (95% CI: -38–66) in the overall population ≥75 years. A smaller decrease for the overall population ≥75 years was observed using health administrative data, but it did not reach statistical significance (10%; 95% CI: -7–23). The impact of the immunization program did not change following adjustment for diagnostic test performance, while the absolute burden of RSV-associated hospitalizations varied according to the proportion of RSV test positivity. Conclusions The 2024-25 RSV immunization program was associated with an almost 50% reduction in hospitalizations in residents of PSR aged ≥75 years. The magnitude of this reduction was roughly twofold lower when considering the overall population aged ≥75 years. Expanding the target population and strengthening vaccine promotion efforts to improve uptake are both essential to enhance the population-level impact of the RSV immunization program.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study was needed to assess the real-world impact of the RSV immunization program on hospitalization rates among older adults and to understand how diagnostic test performance might influence these estimates. The authors aimed to address the lack of knowledge regarding the program's effectiveness in reducing RSV-associated hospitalizations.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A prospective hospital-based surveillance system (HospiVir) and health administrative databases were used to evaluate the impact of the RSV immunization program in Québec, focusing on older adults aged ≥75 years residing in private senior residences and long-term care facilities.
analysis.methods: The study employed an observed to expected approach and a before/after ecological design using a difference-in-difference Poisson regression to assess the intervention impact, while accounting for seasonal variations and trends in comparison groups.
analysis.main_results: Based on HospiVir, there was a 49% (95% confidence interval: -80–-5) decrease in RSV-associated hospitalizations among adults aged ≥75 years in private senior residences. For the overall population ≥75 years, the decrease was 23% (95% confidence interval: -38–66). Using health administrative data, a smaller decrease of 10% (95% confidence interval: -7–23) was observed, but it did not reach statistical significance.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as indicating that the RSV immunization program was associated with a substantial reduction in hospitalizations among residents of private senior residences aged ≥75 years. This reduction was approximately twofold lower when considering the overall population aged ≥75 years.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that expanding the target population and improving vaccine uptake could significantly enhance the population-level impact of the RSV immunization program, particularly in high-risk groups such as those in private senior residences.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's results were based on hospital-based surveillance and health administrative data, which may have limitations in capturing the full burden of RSV. analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the impact of the first season of an RSV immunization program in Québec, targeting older adults in long-term care facilities and those aged ≥75 years in private senior residences. The authors used a prospective hospital-based surveillance system and health administrative databases to assess the program's effectiveness. They observed a 49% decrease in RSV-associated hospitalizations among adults aged ≥75 years in private senior residences, while the overall population showed a smaller reduction of 23%. The study also found that the impact of the program did not change after adjusting for diagnostic test performance. The findings highlight the importance of expanding the target population and improving vaccine uptake to enhance the program's effectiveness. However, the study's reliance on surveillance data and the lack of statistical significance in some comparisons limit the confidence in the results, suggesting a moderate evidence strength.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 这项研究需要评估 RSV 免疫计划对老年人住院率的实际影响,并了解诊断测试性能如何影响这些估计。作者旨在解决对该计划在减少 RSV 相关住院治疗方面的有效性缺乏了解的问题。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 使用基于医院的前瞻性 监测 系统 (HospiVir) 和健康管理数据库来评估魁北克省 RSV 免疫计划的影响,重点关注居住在私人高级住宅和长期护理机构的 75 岁以上老年人。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究采用了观察到预期的方法和前后生态设计,使用双差泊松回归来评估干预影响,同时考虑了对照组的季节变化和趋势。
elements_zh.main_results: 根据 HospiVir 的数据,私人老年住宅中年龄≥75 岁的成年人中与 RSV 相关的住院率下降了 49%(95% 置信区间:-80–-5)。对于 75 岁以上的总人口,下降了 23%(95% 置信区间:-38–66)。使用卫生管理数据,观察到较小的下降 10%(95% 置信区间:-7-23),但未达到统计显着性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将研究结果解释为,RSV 免疫计划与年龄≥75 岁的私人高级住宅居民住院治疗的大幅减少有关。考虑到年龄 ≥ 75 岁的总人口,这一减少量大约低两倍。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,扩大目标人群和提高 疫苗 的吸收率可以显着增强 RSV 免疫计划的人群影响,特别是在私人高级住宅等高危人群中。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的结果基于医院的 监测 和卫生行政数据,这些数据在捕获 RSV 的全部负担方面可能存在局限性。证据强度中等,因为在调整诊断测试性能后,免疫计划的影响没有改变。

title_zh: 呼吸道合胞病毒 免疫接种对老年人的影响:有效负担估计的重要性
source_body_en: ABSTRACT Introduction In the province of Québec, Canada, a respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) immunization program restricted to seniors residing in long-term care facilities (LTCF) and those aged ≥75 years from private senior residences (PSR) was implemented in Fall 2024, with approximately 65% vaccine uptake in the targeted populations. Despite high vaccine effectiveness, the real-world impact of the RSV immunization program on population-level averted hospitalizations and the influence that RSV diagnostic test performance might have remains unknown. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of the first season (2024-25) of the intervention among older adults in Québec while accounting for laboratory test performance. Methods A prospective hospital-based surveillance (HospiVir) and health administrative databases were used to assess the intervention impact. Observed to expected approach and before/after ecological design using a difference-in-difference Poisson regression, both accounting for seasonal variations and trends in comparison groups, were used. Hospitalization incidence rate estimates based on hospital-based surveillance were adjusted for the laboratory test performances using Lash equations. Results Based on HospiVir, a 49% (95% confidence interval (CI): -80– -5) decrease in RSV-associated hospitalizations was observed among adults aged ≥75 years residing in PSR. This decrease was 23% (95% CI: -38–66) in the overall population ≥75 years. A smaller decrease for the overall population ≥75 years was observed using health administrative data, but it did not reach statistical significance (10%; 95% CI: -7–23). The impact of the immunization program did not change following adjustment for diagnostic test performance, while the absolute burden of RSV-associated hospitalizations varied according to the proportion of RSV test positivity. Conclusions The 2024-25 RSV immunization program was associated with an almost 50% reduction in hospitalizations in residents of PSR aged ≥75 years. The magnitude of this reduction was roughly twofold lower when considering the overall population aged ≥75 years. Expanding the target population and strengthening vaccine promotion efforts to improve uptake are both essential to enhance the population-level impact of the RSV immunization program.

title: Extreme weather and high-level PM2.5 co-exposure are associated with elevated respiratory syncytial virus circulating intensity
abstract: Abstract Background Higher temperatures and more frequent heat waves and cold spells due to climate change raise concerns for respiratory health. However, the association of extreme temperature events with RSV epidemics remains unclear. Method We conducted time-series analyses to assess relative risks from exposure to extreme temperatures alone and joint exposure to extreme temperatures and high-level particulate matter [2.5 microns or less in diameter ( $${{{\rm{PM}}}}_{2.5}$$ PM 2.5 )] pollution on RSV circulating strength. Japan and Chile were selected as two contrasting settings with distinct climatic and geographic backgrounds. Weekly data on laboratory-confirmed RSV-positive cases, denominator population, meteorological factors, and air pollutants were collected from 16 Chilean regions (2015–2018) and 47 Japanese prefectures (2013–2019). We fitted quasi-Poisson regression to assess the local-level estimates and used random-effects meta-analyses to obtain national estimates. Results Here we show that heat waves are linked to increased RSV circulating intensity in Japan, with relative risks up to 1.49 (95% confidence interval (CI): 1.29–1.73). Cold spells show weaker but positive effects. Although cold spells demonstrate no consistent effects in Chile, joint exposure to high-level $${{{\rm{PM}}}}_{2.5}$$ PM 2.5 pollution and cold spells increases risks by 32% (95% CI: 1.10–1.58). Joint exposure to high-level $${{{\rm{PM}}}}_{2.5}$$ PM 2.5 pollution and heat waves raises risk by up to 66% (95% CI: 1.27–2.16) in Japan. Conclusions These findings reveal national patterns and regional variations in RSV responses to extreme temperatures, highlighting the need for public health measures targeting modifiable population-level factors amid global climate change.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the association between extreme temperature events and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) circulating intensity, addressing a critical knowledge gap amid climate change concerns. Using time-series analyses of weekly RSV case data from Japan and Chile, the authors quantified the relative risks of RSV cases linked to heat waves, cold spells, and joint exposure to high-level PM2.5 pollution. Heat waves were associated with increased RSV intensity in Japan (RR up to 1.49), while joint exposure to PM2.5 and extreme temperatures further elevated risks (up to 66% for heat waves and 32% for cold spells). elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 由于气候变化,人们对呼吸系统健康的担忧日益加剧,该研究解决了极端温度事件与 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 流行病之间尚不清楚的关联问题。其目的是量化极端温度(单独或与高浓度 PM2.5 污染结合)如何影响 RSV 循环强度。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用智利 16 个地区(2015-2018 年)和日本 47 个都道府县(2013-2019 年)的每周数据进行时间序列分析。它评估了 RSV 循环强度与气象因素和空气污染物的关系,重点关注极端温度事件和 PM2.5 暴露。
elements_zh.methods: 拟合准泊松回归模型来估计与极端温度和高浓度 PM2.5 污染相关的当地 RSV 病例相对风险。然后使用随机效应荟萃分析从当地数据得出国家层面的估计。
elements_zh.main_results: 热浪与日本 RSV 循环强度增加有关,相对风险高达 1.49(95% CI:1.29-1.73)。在日本,同时暴露于高浓度 PM2.5 和热浪会使风险增加高达 66%(95% CI:1.27–2.16),而同时暴露于 PM2.5 和寒流会使风险增加 32%(95% CI:1.10–1.58)。寒潮表现出较弱但积极的影响。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果揭示了 RSV 对极端温度反应的国家模式和区域差异,强调了在气候变化下可能影响 RSV 传播 的可改变的种群水平因素。这是第一项量化极端温度和 PM2.5 对 RSV 循环强度联合影响的研究。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果表明,针对极端温度事件和空气污染的公共卫生措施可以减轻 RSV 负担,特别是在 PM2.5 水平较高且热浪或寒流频繁的地区。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到其生态设计的限制,无法进行因果推断,并且可能受到未测量的混杂因素(例如就医行为和测试实践)的影响。由于依赖汇总数据且缺乏个体层面的控制,证据强度中等。

title: Changes in respiratory virus seasonality across the COVID-19 pandemic: a multicentre comparative study in Leicester, Rotterdam, Hong Kong, and Christchurch.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To describe respiratory virus seasonality before, during, and after coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) using routine hospital diagnostic laboratory data contributed through the International Network for the Sequencing of Respiratory Viruses (INSPIRE). METHODS: We analysed monthly test data from four diagnostic laboratories in Leicester, UK; Rotterdam, the Netherlands; Hong Kong, China; and Christchurch, New Zealand, during 2018-2023. Viruses included influenza A virus, influenza B virus, respiratory syncytial virus, parainfluenza viruses 1-4, human metapneumovirus, adenovirus, and enterovirus/rhinovirus. Monthly test positivity was compared across pre-COVID-19 (2018-2019), COVID-19 disruption (2020-2021), and post-COVID-19 re-emergence (2022-2023) periods. RESULTS: The dataset comprised 3,164,720 tests performed and 84,300 positive detections. During 2020-2021, influenza activity was markedly suppressed: influenza A virus positivity decreased from 7.3% to 1.2%, and influenza B virus positivity from 3.0% to 0.1%. Respiratory syncytial virus showed a smaller overall reduction, whereas enterovirus/rhinovirus remained detectable in all four sites. In 2022-2023, respiratory viruses re-emerged heterogeneously; peak months differed by at least two months between the pre- and post-COVID-19 periods in 21 of 40 site-virus combinations. CONCLUSIONS: Respiratory virus seasonality was substantially altered during and after COVID-19. Post-COVID-19 re-emergence varied by virus and site, supporting continued multi-pathogen surveillance.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在利用常规医院诊断实验室数据来描述 2019 年冠状病毒病 (COVID-19) 大流行之前、期间和之后呼吸道病毒的季节性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是在莱斯特、鹿特丹、香港和基督城的四个诊断实验室进行的多中心比较分析,使用了 2018 年至 2023 年的数据。它包括 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 以及其他病毒,如甲型流感病毒、乙型流感病毒、副流感病毒 1-4、人类偏肺病毒、腺病毒和肠道病毒/鼻病毒。
elements_zh.methods: 比较了三个时期的每月测试阳性率:COVID-19 之前(2018-2019 年)、COVID-19 中断(2020-2021 年)和 COVID-19 重新出现后(2022-2023 年)。该分析使用了国际呼吸道病毒测序网络(INSPIRE)提供的常规诊断实验室数据。

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,在 COVID-19 大流行期间和之后,呼吸道病毒的季节性发生了显着变化,流感活动发生了显着变化,其他病毒的重新出现模式也发生了变化。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果强调了持续使用多病原体 监测 的必要性,因为 COVID-19 后的重新出现模式因病毒和地点而异,可能会影响公共卫生策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于常规诊断数据,在捕获全面的病毒动态方面可能存在局限性。证据是温和的,因为它依赖于没有实验控制的观察数据。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在利用常规医院诊断实验室数据来描述 2019 年冠状病毒病 (COVID-19) 大流行之前、期间和之后呼吸道病毒的季节性。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是在莱斯特、鹿特丹、香港和基督城的四个诊断实验室进行的多中心比较分析,使用了 2018 年至 2023 年的数据。它包括 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 以及其他病毒,如甲型流感病毒、乙型流感病毒、副流感病毒 1-4、人类偏肺病毒、腺病毒和肠道病毒/鼻病毒。
analysis_zh.methods: 比较了三个时期的每月测试阳性率:COVID-19 之前(2018-2019 年)、COVID-19 中断(2020-2021 年)和 COVID-19 重新出现后(2022-2023 年)。该分析使用了国际呼吸道病毒测序网络(INSPIRE)提供的常规诊断实验室数据。
analysis_zh.main_results: 该数据集包括 3,164,720 项测试,其中检测到 84,300 项阳性。2020-2021年间,甲型流感病毒阳性率从7.3%下降至1.2%,乙型流感病毒阳性率从3.0%下降至0.1%。呼吸道合胞病毒 总体减少幅度较小,而肠道病毒/鼻病毒在所有四个位点仍可检测到。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,在 COVID-19 大流行期间和之后,呼吸道病毒的季节性发生了显着变化,流感活动发生了显着变化,其他病毒的重新出现模式也发生了变化。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果强调了持续使用多病原体 监测 的必要性,因为 COVID-19 后的重新出现模式因病毒和地点而异,可能会影响公共卫生策略。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于常规诊断数据,在捕获全面的病毒动态方面可能存在局限性。证据是温和的,因为它依赖于没有实验控制的观察数据。

title: Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV)–An Urgent Priority in Respiratory Disease Prevention
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of lower respiratory tract disease in infants, young children, older adults, and individuals with cardiopulmonary comorbidities or immunocompromised states. Recent advances enable layered prevention through maternal vaccination for infant protection, long-acting monoclonal antibodies for newborns and select toddlers, and vaccines for older adults. However, inequities in surveillance, seasonality-driven timing, and challenges in affordability and delivery—particularly in low- and middle-income countries— impede equitable uptake. This editorial underscores priority populations, synthesizes current evidence and policy directions, and outlines actionable levers in financing, procurement, and integrated maternal–child health delivery to accelerate access, making RSV prevention an urgent and achievable global health priority.

title: Clinical and Analytical Validation of a Novel Switching RT-qPCR Assay for the Simultaneous Detection of Seven Respiratory Viruses.
abstract: Rapid and accurate identification of respiratory viruses is essential for effective clinical management and infection control. However, conventional RT-qPCR methods are time-consuming and require complex workflows. To address these limitations, we developed a novel Switching RT-qPCR assay designed for multiplex detection of respiratory viruses with enhanced efficiency and sensitivity. This study aimed to evaluate the analytical and clinical performance of the switching RT-qPCR assay in the detection of seven major respiratory viruses: Influenza A and B, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) A and B, adenovirus (AdV), human metapneumovirus (hMPV), and SARS-CoV-2 (Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2). Nasopharyngeal swab specimens (n = 808) were collected from patients with respiratory symptoms. RNA was extracted and tested using both a Switching RT-qPCR assay and commercial multiplex RT-qPCR method (Allplex Respiratory Panels and Allplex SARS-CoV-2 Assay). The concordance, sensitivity, specificity, and analytical performances of the two methods were compared. The Switching RT-qPCR assay demonstrated a clinical sensitivity of 93.6% and a specificity of 100%, with an overall concordance rate exceeding 96%, compared with the conventional assay. Analytical sensitivity was comparable or superior across most viral targets, particularly RSV A, AdV, and hMPV. The duplex assay format enabled the efficient simultaneous detection of two targets per reaction, reducing the overall testing time while maintaining analytical accuracy. This Switching RT-qPCR assay offers a reliable, rapid, and efficient alternative for respiratory virus detection. Its simplified duplex format and high concordance with standard molecular diagnostics indicate its potential utility in routine clinical laboratories.

title: An evaluation of the anti-human respiratory syncytial virus activity of sophora alkaloids and the enhanced efficacy by liposomes via intratracheal administration
abstract: Human respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of severe lower respiratory tract infections and related deaths in infants, young children, and the elderly. The clinical management of RSV is challenging due to its high mutation rate and the limited efficacy and safety of existing antiviral drugs. Sophora alkaloids, natural compounds derived from Sophora flavescens, exhibit broad-spectrum antiviral and immunomodulatory activities. Mechanistically, RSV relies on ERK1/2 phosphorylation to facilitate viral replication and spread, while sophora alkaloids inhibit ERK1/2 phosphorylation via regulating MEK/ERK signaling pathway, thereby suppressing viral proliferation and the inflammatory response caused by RSV infection. In vivo studies demonstrated that sophora alkaloids significantly reduced the mortality of RSV-infected mice via intratracheal administration. To further enhance the pulmonary retention of drugs, liposomes were used to improve the therapeutic effects of sophora alkaloids. As the most effective sophora alkaloids against RSV infection, sophocarpine (SC) was encapsulated in liposomes to enhance its anti-RSV infection effect. In vivo studies demonstrate that SC-loaded liposomes outperformed the free SC in suppressing RSV replication and alleviating pulmonary inflammation in murine models of RSV infection. This study not only clarifies the mechanism by which sophora alkaloids counteract RSV-infection but also provides liposomal formulation of SC to improve the anti-RSV therapeutic effects.

title_zh: 槐生物碱的抗人呼吸道合胞病毒活性评价及脂质体气管内给药增强功效的评价
source_body_en: Human respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of severe lower respiratory tract infections and related deaths in infants, young children, and the elderly. The clinical management of RSV is challenging due to its high mutation rate and the limited efficacy and safety of existing antiviral drugs. Sophora alkaloids, natural compounds derived from Sophora flavescens, exhibit broad-spectrum antiviral and immunomodulatory activities. Mechanistically, RSV relies on ERK1/2 phosphorylation to facilitate viral replication and spread, while sophora alkaloids inhibit ERK1/2 phosphorylation via regulating MEK/ERK signaling pathway, thereby suppressing viral proliferation and the inflammatory response caused by RSV infection. In vivo studies demonstrated that sophora alkaloids significantly reduced the mortality of RSV-infected mice via intratracheal administration. To further enhance the pulmonary retention of drugs, liposomes were used to improve the therapeutic effects of sophora alkaloids. As the most effective sophora alkaloids against RSV infection, sophocarpine (SC) was encapsulated in liposomes to enhance its anti-RSV infection effect. In vivo studies demonstrate that SC-loaded liposomes outperformed the free SC in suppressing RSV replication and alleviating pulmonary inflammation in murine models of RSV infection. This study not only clarifies the mechanism by which sophora alkaloids counteract RSV-infection but also provides liposomal formulation of SC to improve the anti-RSV therapeutic effects.

title: Clinician-Reported Respiratory Viral Testing and Intended Management of Community-Acquired Respiratory Viral Infections in Haematology and Haematopoietic Cell Transplantation: An International Exploratory Survey
abstract: Background: Community-acquired respiratory viruses (CARVs) cause significant morbidity and mortality in patients with haematological malignancies and those undergoing haematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT). Despite this, clinical management remains variable. This study evaluated clinicians’ awareness, diagnostic practices, and treatment approaches to major respiratory viruses in this high-risk population. Methods: An international electronic survey using non-probability convenience sampling was conducted among haematology, oncology, intensive care and emergency medicine physicians. Four real-life clinical cases were converted into standardised vignettes covering human metapneumovirus (HMPV), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), human parainfluenza virus (HPIV) and influenza A virus (IAV). The questionnaire assessed reported testing strategies and intended management, including antiviral and immunoprophylactic interventions. Responses were analysed descriptively; no inferential between-group comparisons were performed. Results: Ninety-eight clinicians from 26 countries responded. Diagnostic approaches, including testing indications and panel selection, varied among respondents. For HMPV and HPIV, respondents mainly reported supportive care, immunoglobulin replacement, and infection-control measures in the absence of established pathogen-specific interventions. RSV practice was heterogeneous: systemic ribavirin was considered by 45/96 (46.9%) respondents, including 34/96 (35.4%) when guided by an immunodeficiency score. IAV management was more consistent, with reported availability of vaccination and antiviral therapy and frequent use of post-exposure prophylaxis. Conclusions: Within this international convenience sample, clinicians reported variation in respiratory viral testing and in how results informed intended management. Because sampling was non-probability-based and respondent groups were small and unevenly distributed, the findings should not be interpreted as representative estimates of international practice. IAV testing was most consistently linked to established treatment and prevention, RSV showed greater therapeutic and preventive heterogeneity, and HMPV/HPIV testing primarily informed infection control, monitoring and antimicrobial stewardship.

Four real-life clinical cases were converted into standardised vignettes covering respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), human metapneumovirus (HMPV), human parainfluenza virus (HPIV) and influenza A virus (IAV).
elements_en.methods: The questionnaire assessed reported testing strategies and intended management, including antiviral and immunoprophylactic interventions. Responses were analysed descriptively; no inferential between-group comparisons were performed.
elements_en.main_results: Ninety-eight clinicians from 26 countries responded. Diagnostic approaches, including testing indications and panel selection, varied among respondents. elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the need for standardised diagnostic and management protocols for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in high-risk populations. elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study used non-probability convenience sampling, which may limit the generalisability of the findings. title_zh: 临床医生报告的血液学和造血细胞移植中社区获得性呼吸道病毒感染的呼吸道病毒检测和预期管理:一项国际探索性调查
source_body_en: Background: Community-acquired respiratory viruses (CARVs) cause significant morbidity and mortality in patients with haematological malignancies and those undergoing haematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT). Despite this, clinical management remains variable. This study evaluated clinicians’ awareness, diagnostic practices, and treatment approaches to major respiratory viruses in this high-risk population. Methods: An international electronic survey using non-probability convenience sampling was conducted among haematology, oncology, intensive care and emergency medicine physicians. Four real-life clinical cases were converted into standardised vignettes covering human metapneumovirus (HMPV), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), human parainfluenza virus (HPIV) and influenza A virus (IAV). The questionnaire assessed reported testing strategies and intended management, including antiviral and immunoprophylactic interventions. Responses were analysed descriptively; no inferential between-group comparisons were performed. Results: Ninety-eight clinicians from 26 countries responded. Diagnostic approaches, including testing indications and panel selection, varied among respondents. For HMPV and HPIV, respondents mainly reported supportive care, immunoglobulin replacement, and infection-control measures in the absence of established pathogen-specific interventions. RSV practice was heterogeneous: systemic ribavirin was considered by 45/96 (46.9%) respondents, including 34/96 (35.4%) when guided by an immunodeficiency score. IAV management was more consistent, with reported availability of vaccination and antiviral therapy and frequent use of post-exposure prophylaxis. Conclusions: Within this international convenience sample, clinicians reported variation in respiratory viral testing and in how results informed intended management. Because sampling was non-probability-based and respondent groups were small and unevenly distributed, the findings should not be interpreted as representative estimates of international practice. IAV testing was most consistently linked to established treatment and prevention, RSV showed greater therapeutic and preventive heterogeneity, and HMPV/HPIV testing primarily informed infection control, monitoring and antimicrobial stewardship.

title: Analiza hematoloških parametara u djece s bronhiolitisom uzrokovanim respiratornim sincicijskim virusom The analysis of haematological parameters in children with bronchiolitis caused by respiratory syncytial virus
abstract: Cilj: Cilj je ovog presječnog istraživanja ispitati povezanost hematoloških parametara u djece s bronhiolitisom uzrokovanim respiratornim sincicijskim virusom s kliničkim karakteristikama bolesti te analizirati njihovu moguću prediktivnu vrijednost. Ispitanici i metode: Istraživanje je presječno, provedeno na uzorku od 100 djece hospitalizirane na Odjelu pedijatrije Opće županijske bolnice u Požegi od 2010. godine zbog bronhiolitisa uzrokovanog respiratornim sincicijskim virusom. Podatci o pacijentima i tijeku bolesti prikupljeni su iz medicinske dokumentacije. Svim pacijentima s kliničkom slikom bronhiolitisa kojima je iz brisa nazofarinksa izoliran respiracijski sincicijski virus, učinjena je kompletna krvna slika i C-reaktivni protein. U statističkoj obradi korišteni su test 2, Mann-Whitneyev test, Spearmanov koeficijent korelacije (Rho) te binarna logistička regresija. Rezultati: S obzirom na ovisnost o kisiku, utvrđene su statistički značajno niže vrijednosti eritrocita (p = 0,030) te značajno više ispitanika s vrijednostima trombocita iznad referentnog raspona (p = 0,030) u skupini koja je ovisna o kisiku, u odnosu na ispitanike koji nisu ovisni o kisiku. C-reaktivni protein nije povezan s prisutnošću pneumonije i ovisnosti o kisiku. Što su više vrijednosti trombocita, a niže vrijednosti MPV-a, to je i dulje trajanje bolesti. Zaključak: Djeca koja tijekom hospitalizacije zbog akutnog bronhiolitisa uzrokovanog respiratornim sincicijskim virusom imaju niže vrijednosti eritrocita i više vrijednosti trombocita iz periferne krvi, imaju veći rizik za ovisnost o kisiku tijekom liječenja, a samim time i za teži tijek bolesti. C-reaktivni protein nije statistički značajno povezan s težinom ili trajanjem bolesti.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to investigate the association between haematological parameters and clinical characteristics in children with bronchiolitis caused by respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). It was a cross-sectional study conducted on 100 children hospitalized at the Department of Pediatrics in Požega General Hospital in 2010 due to RSV bronchiolitis. Complete blood count and C-reactive protein were performed on all patients with clinical features of bronchiolitis confirmed by RSV isolation from nasal swabs. The results showed statistically significant lower erythrocyte counts and higher platelet counts in children dependent on oxygen therapy compared to those not dependent. The authors interpreted these findings as indicating a higher risk of oxygen dependency and more severe disease progression in children with lower erythrocyte counts and higher platelet counts. The study suggests potential utility in identifying children at risk for severe RSV bronchiolitis. However, the analysis relied on data from medical records, which may limit precision and generalizability. The evidence is moderate due to the observational nature and potential for confounding factors.

title: PREVENCIÓN DE LAS INFECCIONES SEVERAS POR VIRUS SINCITIAL RESPIRATORIO EN LACTANTES EN EL PERÚ: RECOMENDACIONES BASADAS EN LA METODOLOGÍA GRADE PREVENTION OF SEVERE RESPIRATORY SYNCYTIAL VIRUS INFECTIONS IN INFANTS IN PERU: RECOMMENDATIONS BASED ON THE GRADE METHODOLOGY
abstract: Introducción: El virus sincitial respiratorio (VSR) es la principal causa de infección respiratoria aguda baja en lactantes y representa una importante carga de morbilidad, hospitalización y mortalidad, especialmente durante los primeros meses de vida en países de ingresos bajos y medianos como el Perú. Objetivo: Desarrollar recomendaciones basadas en evidencia para prevenir la enfermedad grave por VSR en lactantes en el Perú. Métodos: Se elaboró una guía de práctica clínica utilizando la metodología GRADE. Se formularon cinco preguntas clínicas estructuradas en formato PICO y se realizó una revisión sistemática de la evidencia en bases de datos biomédicas. La certeza de la evidencia se evaluó considerando el riesgo de sesgo, la consistencia, la precisión y la aplicabilidad. Se utilizó un marco de la Evidencia a la Decisión (EtD) para formular recomendaciones. Resultados: Se recomienda la vacunación materna entre las 32 y 36 semanas de gestación para reducir la enfermedad grave y las hospitalizaciones por VSR en lactantes (recomendación fuerte a favor, evidencia alta). En lactantes no protegidos por vacunación materna, se recomienda administrar nirsevimab (recomendación fuerte a favor, evidencia alta). En prematuros y en poblaciones de alto riesgo, nirsevimab se considera la estrategia preferida, con recomendaciones fuertes o condicionales según el subgrupo y la disponibilidad de evidencia directa. Conclusión: Las estrategias de inmunoprofilaxis contra el VSR, basadas en la vacunación materna y el uso de un anticuerpo monoclonal (nirsevimab), tienen el potencial de reducir sustancialmente la carga de enfermedad en lactantes en el Perú, y su implementación programada debe considerarse una prioridad de salud pública.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop evidence-based recommendations for preventing severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infections in infants in Peru. Using the GRADE methodology, five structured PICO clinical questions were formulated, and a systematic review of biomedical databases was conducted. The results indicated that maternal vaccination between 32 and 36 weeks of gestation is strongly recommended to reduce severe RSV disease and hospitalizations in infants, with high-quality evidence. Additionally, nirsevimab is strongly recommended for infants not protected by maternal vaccination, and it is considered the preferred strategy for preterm infants and high-risk populations, with strong or conditional recommendations based on subgroup availability. The authors interpreted these findings as having significant potential to reduce the disease burden in Peruvian infants, highlighting the importance of implementing these strategies as a public health priority. The evidence strength was assessed as high, with the certainty of evidence evaluated based on bias risk, consistency, precision, and applicability. However, the study is limited by its reliance on abstract-only evidence and the absence of detailed statistical or methodological procedures.

source_body_en: Introducción: El virus sincitial respiratorio (VSR) es la principal causa de infección respiratoria aguda baja en lactantes y representa una importante carga de morbilidad, hospitalización y mortalidad, especialmente durante los primeros meses de vida en países de ingresos bajos y medianos como el Perú. Objetivo: Desarrollar recomendaciones basadas en evidencia para prevenir la enfermedad grave por VSR en lactantes en el Perú. Métodos: Se elaboró una guía de práctica clínica utilizando la metodología GRADE. Se formularon cinco preguntas clínicas estructuradas en formato PICO y se realizó una revisión sistemática de la evidencia en bases de datos biomédicas. La certeza de la evidencia se evaluó considerando el riesgo de sesgo, la consistencia, la precisión y la aplicabilidad. Se utilizó un marco de la Evidencia a la Decisión (EtD) para formular recomendaciones. Resultados: Se recomienda la vacunación materna entre las 32 y 36 semanas de gestación para reducir la enfermedad grave y las hospitalizaciones por VSR en lactantes (recomendación fuerte a favor, evidencia alta). En lactantes no protegidos por vacunación materna, se recomienda administrar nirsevimab (recomendación fuerte a favor, evidencia alta). En prematuros y en poblaciones de alto riesgo, nirsevimab se considera la estrategia preferida, con recomendaciones fuertes o condicionales según el subgrupo y la disponibilidad de evidencia directa. Conclusión: Las estrategias de inmunoprofilaxis contra el VSR, basadas en la vacunación materna y el uso de un anticuerpo monoclonal (nirsevimab), tienen el potencial de reducir sustancialmente la carga de enfermedad en lactantes en el Perú, y su implementación programada debe considerarse una prioridad de salud pública.

title: Epidemiology of SARS-CoV-2, Influenza, RSV, and Human Metapneumovirus Across the COVID-19 Era: An Eight-Year Tertiary-Center Study in Saudi Arabia
abstract: Background: Respiratory tract infections (RTIs) caused by viruses are a public health problem, contributing to hospital admissions and morbidity worldwide. The COVID-19 pandemic substantially altered the detection patterns of respiratory viruses through public health interventions. Longitudinal data on these changes and viral seasonality remain limited in Saudi Arabia. This eight-year study evaluated epidemiological and seasonal patterns of major respiratory viruses across the COVID-19 era at a major Saudi tertiary care center. Methods: A retrospective observational study was conducted at King Khalid University Hospital, Riyadh, from October 2017 to December 2025. PCR-confirmed detections for SARS-CoV-2, Influenza A, Influenza B, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and human metapneumovirus (HMPV) were extracted from the hospital Laboratory Information System. Demographics, co-detection, seasonality, and length of stay (LOS) were analyzed across four eras spanning the pre-COVID-19, lockdown, restriction, and post-restriction periods using descriptive statistics, the Kruskal–Wallis test, and multivariable negative binomial regression. Results: Among 5708 confirmed respiratory viral detection episodes, SARS-CoV-2 was the most frequently detected (52.5%), followed by Influenza A (19.1%), RSV (16.4%), Influenza B (8.4%), and HMPV (3.6%). Before the pandemic, Influenza A accounted for the largest proportion of detected episodes (71.1%), with detections clustering particularly during autumn and winter seasons, whereas SARS-CoV-2 accounted for the majority of detected episodes during the lockdown and restriction eras (97.4% and 93.2%). The post-restriction era became more diverse, with RSV being detected in substantial proportions (28.3%), showing prominent winter activity. RSV and HMPV predominantly affected children aged 0–5 years, whereas SARS-CoV-2 was more frequently detected among older adults. Among adults, older age was associated with prolonged LOS; Influenza A and HMPV were associated with shorter stays compared to SARS-CoV-2. Among children, no virus was independently associated with LOS after adjustment for age and sex; however, older age was associated with longer hospital stays. Conclusion: The observed detection patterns of major respiratory viruses shifted substantially across the COVID-19 eras, with notable post-restriction diversification among observed positive detections. LOS was associated with age in both adults and children and with virus type among adults, supporting continued surveillance to guide preventive and clinical strategies.

title_zh: COVID-19 时代的 SARS-CoV-2、流感、RSV 和人类偏肺病毒的 流行病学:沙特阿拉伯三级中心为期八年的研究
source_body_en: Background: Respiratory tract infections (RTIs) caused by viruses are a public health problem, contributing to hospital admissions and morbidity worldwide. The COVID-19 pandemic substantially altered the detection patterns of respiratory viruses through public health interventions. Longitudinal data on these changes and viral seasonality remain limited in Saudi Arabia. This eight-year study evaluated epidemiological and seasonal patterns of major respiratory viruses across the COVID-19 era at a major Saudi tertiary care center. Methods: A retrospective observational study was conducted at King Khalid University Hospital, Riyadh, from October 2017 to December 2025. PCR-confirmed detections for SARS-CoV-2, Influenza A, Influenza B, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and human metapneumovirus (HMPV) were extracted from the hospital Laboratory Information System. Demographics, co-detection, seasonality, and length of stay (LOS) were analyzed across four eras spanning the pre-COVID-19, lockdown, restriction, and post-restriction periods using descriptive statistics, the Kruskal–Wallis test, and multivariable negative binomial regression. Results: Among 5708 confirmed respiratory viral detection episodes, SARS-CoV-2 was the most frequently detected (52.5%), followed by Influenza A (19.1%), RSV (16.4%), Influenza B (8.4%), and HMPV (3.6%). Before the pandemic, Influenza A accounted for the largest proportion of detected episodes (71.1%), with detections clustering particularly during autumn and winter seasons, whereas SARS-CoV-2 accounted for the majority of detected episodes during the lockdown and restriction eras (97.4% and 93.2%). The post-restriction era became more diverse, with RSV being detected in substantial proportions (28.3%), showing prominent winter activity. RSV and HMPV predominantly affected children aged 0–5 years, whereas SARS-CoV-2 was more frequently detected among older adults. Among adults, older age was associated with prolonged LOS; Influenza A and HMPV were associated with shorter stays compared to SARS-CoV-2. Among children, no virus was independently associated with LOS after adjustment for age and sex; however, older age was associated with longer hospital stays. Conclusion: The observed detection patterns of major respiratory viruses shifted substantially across the COVID-19 eras, with notable post-restriction diversification among observed positive detections. LOS was associated with age in both adults and children and with virus type among adults, supporting continued surveillance to guide preventive and clinical strategies.
abstract_zh: 背景:由病毒引起的呼吸道感染(RTI)是一个公共卫生问题,导致全世界住院和发病。COVID-19 大流行通过公共卫生干预措施极大地改变了呼吸道病毒的检测模式。沙特阿拉伯有关这些变化和病毒季节性的纵向数据仍然有限。这项为期八年的研究评估了沙特阿拉伯一家主要三级护理中心在整个 COVID-19 时代主要呼吸道病毒的流行病学和季节性模式。方法:2017 年 10 月至 2025 年 12 月在利雅得哈立德国王大学医院进行了一项回顾性观察研究。从医院实验室信息系统中提取了 SARS-CoV-2、甲型流感、乙型流感、呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和人类偏肺病毒 (HMPV) 的 PCR 确诊检测结果。使用描述性统计、Kruskal-Wallis 检验和多变量负二项式回归,对跨越 COVID-19 之前、封锁、限制和限制后四个时期的人口统计、共同检测、季节性和住院时间 (LOS) 进行了分析。结果:在 5708 例确诊的呼吸道病毒检测事件中,SARS-CoV-2 检测频率最高(52.5%),其次是甲型流感(19.1%)、RSV(16.4%)、乙型流感(8.4%)和 HMPV(3.6%)。在大流行之前,甲型流感占检测到的病例的最大比例(71.1%),检测集中在秋冬季节,而SARS-CoV-2占封锁和限制时期检测到的病例的大部分(97.4%和93.2%)。后限制时代变得更加多样化,RSV 检测到的比例很高(28.3%),显示出冬季活动突出。RSV 和 HMPV 主要影响 0-5 岁儿童,而 SARS-CoV-2 在老年人中更常见。在成年人中,年龄较大与 LOS 延长有关;与 SARS-CoV-2 相比,甲型流感和 HMPV 的停留时间较短。在儿童中,调整年龄和性别后,没有病毒与 LOS 独立相关;然而,年龄越大,住院时间越长。结论:在 COVID-19 时代,观察到的主要呼吸道病毒的检测模式发生了很大变化,观察到的阳性检测在限制后出现了显着的多样化。LOS 与成人和儿童的年龄以及成人的病毒类型相关,支持持续的 监测 来指导预防和临床策略。

title: Morbidity and mortality of respiratory syncytial virus versus influenza virus infections in hospitalized older adults: an adjusted comparative analysis
abstract: Abstract Pneumonia is diagnosed based on clinical symptoms and radiological features. It can be caused by a variety of pathogens including bacterial, mycobacterial, viral, fungal, and other atypical organisms. Most bacterial community-acquired pneumonia is due to Streptococcus pneumoniae, which is normally treated with penicillin and can be risk stratified using the CURB-65 score. Atypical organisms require macrolides. Hospital-acquired pneumonia involves Gram-negative or resistant organisms and treatment depends on local sensitivities. Viral pneumonias can include influenza and COVID-19, with antivirals used only in specific cases. Immunocompromised patients may develop invasive fungal infections such as Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia or invasive aspergillosis requiring targeted antifungals.

source_body_en: Abstract Pneumonia is diagnosed based on clinical symptoms and radiological features. It can be caused by a variety of pathogens including bacterial, mycobacterial, viral, fungal, and other atypical organisms. Most bacterial community-acquired pneumonia is due to Streptococcus pneumoniae, which is normally treated with penicillin and can be risk stratified using the CURB-65 score. Atypical organisms require macrolides. Hospital-acquired pneumonia involves Gram-negative or resistant organisms and treatment depends on local sensitivities. Viral pneumonias can include influenza and COVID-19, with antivirals used only in specific cases. Immunocompromised patients may develop invasive fungal infections such as Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia or invasive aspergillosis requiring targeted antifungals.

title: Clinical Characteristics and Outcomes of Respiratory Viral Infections in Pediatric Cancer Patients, Single center experience
abstract: Abstract Background Respiratory viral (RV) infections cause morbidity and mortality in immunocompromised pediatric patients undergoing cancer treatment. The burden of RV infections in pediatric oncology populations from low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) remain limited. We aimed to detect the prevalence of viruses causing respiratory infections among pediatric patients with cancer and guide empiric therapy and improve patient outcomes. Methods Retrospectively we collected nasopharyngeal swabs and clinical and demographic data from pediatric patients under cancer treatment with respiratory symptoms at Children’s Cancer Hospital Egypt-57357 from September 2023 until March 2025. Samples were tested using multiplex PCR for 16 respiratory viruses. Results A total of 1710 samples were collected from 784 patients with a median age of 7 years and a male-to-female ratio of 1.26:1. Viral pathogens were detected in 1037 swabs (60.6%). The most frequently identified virus was human rhinovirus (HRV) (51.3%), followed by parainfluenza virus (PIV) (9%), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) (8%), SARS-CoV-2 (6.4%), and human metapneumovirus (HmpV) (5.8%). Co-infections were observed in 13% of samples, commonly involving RSV, PIV, and adenovirus. The main symptoms were fever (85.7%), lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) (59.4%), and cough (57.7%). HRV were associated with fever (p=0.01), cough (p=0.02), and hospital admission (p=0.006). PIV infection were associated with increased hospital admission (p=0.04) and need for inotropes (p=0.02), while HmpV was significantly related to LRTI (p=0.01). There was no statistically significant association between virus type and mortality (p=0.64). When correlating patient characteristics with clinical symptoms and outcomes, several significant associations were found. Lower neutrophil count (<500) correlated with rhinorrhea (p<0.001), oxygen need (p=0.01), hospital admission (p=0.001) and intensive care unit (ICU) admission (p=0.04). Female sex was significantly associated with oxygen requirement (p=0.03) and ICU admission (p=0.02); and patients with hematologic malignancies were more likely to require oxygen support (p=0.01). Conclusion RV infections are common among pediatric cancer patients presenting with respiratory symptoms, with predominance of HRV and linked to key clinical manifestations and hospital admission. Host factors such as female sex, hematology tumors, and profound neutropenia were also associated with increased illness severity and need for supportive care. However, mortality did not significantly differ among virus types, suggesting that while RV infections contribute substantially to morbidity, mortality in immunocompromised children likely depends on multifactorial host and disease-related factors.
