title_zh: 小儿癌症患者呼吸道病毒感染的临床特征和结果,单中心经验
source_body_en: Abstract Background Respiratory viral (RV) infections cause morbidity and mortality in immunocompromised pediatric patients undergoing cancer treatment. The burden of RV infections in pediatric oncology populations from low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) remain limited. We aimed to detect the prevalence of viruses causing respiratory infections among pediatric patients with cancer and guide empiric therapy and improve patient outcomes. Methods Retrospectively we collected nasopharyngeal swabs and clinical and demographic data from pediatric patients under cancer treatment with respiratory symptoms at Children’s Cancer Hospital Egypt-57357 from September 2023 until March 2025. Samples were tested using multiplex PCR for 16 respiratory viruses. Results A total of 1710 samples were collected from 784 patients with a median age of 7 years and a male-to-female ratio of 1.26:1. Viral pathogens were detected in 1037 swabs (60.6%). The most frequently identified virus was human rhinovirus (HRV) (51.3%), followed by parainfluenza virus (PIV) (9%), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) (8%), SARS-CoV-2 (6.4%), and human metapneumovirus (HmpV) (5.8%). Co-infections were observed in 13% of samples, commonly involving RSV, PIV, and adenovirus. The main symptoms were fever (85.7%), lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) (59.4%), and cough (57.7%). HRV were associated with fever (p=0.01), cough (p=0.02), and hospital admission (p=0.006). PIV infection were associated with increased hospital admission (p=0.04) and need for inotropes (p=0.02), while HmpV was significantly related to LRTI (p=0.01). There was no statistically significant association between virus type and mortality (p=0.64). When correlating patient characteristics with clinical symptoms and outcomes, several significant associations were found. Lower neutrophil count (<500) correlated with rhinorrhea (p<0.001), oxygen need (p=0.01), hospital admission (p=0.001) and intensive care unit (ICU) admission (p=0.04). Female sex was significantly associated with oxygen requirement (p=0.03) and ICU admission (p=0.02); and patients with hematologic malignancies were more likely to require oxygen support (p=0.01). Conclusion RV infections are common among pediatric cancer patients presenting with respiratory symptoms, with predominance of HRV and linked to key clinical manifestations and hospital admission. Host factors such as female sex, hematology tumors, and profound neutropenia were also associated with increased illness severity and need for supportive care. However, mortality did not significantly differ among virus types, suggesting that while RV infections contribute substantially to morbidity, mortality in immunocompromised children likely depends on multifactorial host and disease-related factors.
abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 呼吸道病毒 (RV) 感染会导致患有癌症 治疗 的免疫功能低下儿科患者发病和 死亡率。低收入和中等收入国家 (LMIC) 儿童肿瘤人群的 RV 感染负担仍然有限。我们的目的是检测引起儿科癌症患者呼吸道感染的病毒的 患病率,并指导经验性治疗和改善患者的治疗结果。方法 回顾性收集了 2023 年 9 月至 2025 年 3 月埃及 57357 儿童癌症医院有呼吸道症状的 治疗 癌症儿童患者的鼻咽拭子以及临床和人口统计数据。使用多重 PCR 对样本进行了 16 种呼吸道病毒检测。结果共收集784例患者1710份样本,中位年龄7岁,男女比例1.26:1。在 1037 份拭子(60.6%)中检测到病毒病原体。最常见的病毒是人鼻病毒 (HRV) (51.3%),其次是副流感病毒 (PIV) (9%)、呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) (8%)、SARS-CoV-2 (6.4%) 和人偏肺病毒 (HmpV) (5.8%)。13% 的样本中观察到混合感染,通常涉及 RSV、PIV 和腺病毒。主要症状为发热(85.7%)、下呼吸道感染(LRTI)(59.4%)和咳嗽(57.7%)。HRV 与发烧 (p=0.01)、咳嗽 (p=0.02) 和入院 (p=0.006) 相关。PIV 感染与入院率增加 (p=0.04) 和正性肌力药物需求增加 (p=0.02) 相关,而 HmpV 与 LRTI 显着相关 (p=0.01)。病毒类型和 死亡率 之间没有统计学上的显着关联 (p=0.64)。当将患者特征与临床症状和结果关联起来时,发现了一些显着的关联。中性粒细胞计数较低(<500)与鼻漏(p<0.001)、需氧量(p=0.01)、入院(p=0.001)和入院重症监护病房(p=0.04)相关。女性性别与需氧量 (p=0.03) 和入住 ICU (p=0.02) 显着相关;患有血液系统恶性肿瘤的患者更有可能需要氧气支持(p=0.01)。结论 RV 感染在有呼吸道症状的儿童癌症患者中很常见,以 HRV 为主,且与关键临床表现和入院情况相关。宿主 因素(例如女性、血液肿瘤和严重中性粒细胞减少症)也与疾病严重程度增加和支持性护理需求增加相关。然而,死亡率 在病毒类型之间没有显着差异,这表明虽然 RV 感染对发病率有很大影响,但免疫功能低下儿童的 死亡率 可能取决于多因素 宿主 和疾病相关因素。

title: Maternal vaccination with RSVpreF and risk of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Background A bivalent respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prefusion F protein–based vaccine (RSVpreF) was approved in the United States in August 2023 for use during pregnancy to prevent infant RSV-associated lower respiratory tract disease. The pivotal phase 3 trial identified a numerical imbalance in hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) that did not reach statistical significance; postmarketing observational studies have since reported inconsistent findings. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to assess this association. Methods We searched MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, Scopus, ClinicalTrials.gov , and WHO ICTRP from inception to Jan 26, 2026, for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational studies comparing HDP outcomes in RSVpreF-vaccinated versus unvaccinated or placebo-receiving pregnant individuals. Unadjusted risk ratios (RRs) were pooled using a random-effects model; adjusted estimates from observational studies were pooled separately by inverse variance methods. This study is registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251026835). Results Nine studies were included (3 RCTs, 6 retrospective cohort studies; n = 148,267). RSVpreF vaccination was associated with a small but statistically significant increase in overall HDP risk (RR 1·08, 95% CI 1·02–1·13; p = 0·004; I 2 = 44%), driven by the observational studies group (1·08, 1·02–1·14; I 2 = 61%); RCTs showed a directionally consistent but non-significant RR (1·12, 0·87–1·43; I 2 = 0%). The association was attributable to gestational hypertension, with no significant association for preeclampsia/eclampsia. Conclusion Maternal RSVpreF vaccination was associated with a small increase in HDP attributable to gestational hypertension and driven primarily by observational studies, in which residual confounding remains possible. The benefits of infant RSV prevention remain substantial, and these findings support continued postmarketing surveillance and informed shared decision-making.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the association between maternal vaccination with RSVpreF and the risk of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP). The target pathogen is respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), specifically RSV-A and RSV-B. The central question is whether RSVpreF vaccination during pregnancy increases the risk of HDP, with a particular emphasis on gestational hypertension.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a systematic review and meta-analysis. The evidence base includes randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational studies. The search was conducted across MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, Scopus, ClinicalTrials.gov, and WHO ICTRP from inception to January 26, 2026. Unadjusted risk ratios (RRs) were pooled using a random-effects model, while adjusted estimates from observational studies were pooled separately using inverse variance methods.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Maternal RSVpreF vaccination was associated with a small but statistically significant increase in overall HDP risk (RR 1·08, 95% CI 1·02–1·13; p = 0·004; I 2 = 44%). This association was primarily driven by observational studies (RR 1·08, 95% CI 1·02–1·14; I 2 = 61%), with RCTs showing a directionally consistent but non-significant RR (1·12, 0·87–1·43; I 2 = 0%). The association was attributed to gestational hypertension, with no significant link to preeclampsia/eclampsia.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The pivotal phase 3 trial found a numerical imbalance in HDP that did not reach statistical significance, and postmarketing observational studies reported inconsistent findings. The association observed in observational studies may be influenced by residual confounding, highlighting methodological limitations. There is a lack of clarity on the mechanisms underlying the increased risk of gestational hypertension and the potential role of other factors.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The benefits of infant RSV prevention through maternal vaccination remain substantial. These findings support continued postmarketing surveillance to monitor the safety profile of RSVpreF vaccination during pregnancy and informed shared decision-making between healthcare providers and pregnant individuals.

title_zh: 患有 RSVpreF 的母亲 疫苗接种 和妊娠期高血压疾病的风险:系统评价和荟萃分析。
source_body_en: Background A bivalent respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prefusion F protein–based vaccine (RSVpreF) was approved in the United States in August 2023 for use during pregnancy to prevent infant RSV-associated lower respiratory tract disease. The pivotal phase 3 trial identified a numerical imbalance in hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) that did not reach statistical significance; postmarketing observational studies have since reported inconsistent findings. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to assess this association. Methods We searched MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, Scopus, ClinicalTrials.gov , and WHO ICTRP from inception to Jan 26, 2026, for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational studies comparing HDP outcomes in RSVpreF-vaccinated versus unvaccinated or placebo-receiving pregnant individuals. Unadjusted risk ratios (RRs) were pooled using a random-effects model; adjusted estimates from observational studies were pooled separately by inverse variance methods. This study is registered with PROSPERO (CRD420251026835). Results Nine studies were included (3 RCTs, 6 retrospective cohort studies; n = 148,267). RSVpreF vaccination was associated with a small but statistically significant increase in overall HDP risk (RR 1·08, 95% CI 1·02–1·13; p = 0·004; I 2 = 44%), driven by the observational studies group (1·08, 1·02–1·14; I 2 = 61%); RCTs showed a directionally consistent but non-significant RR (1·12, 0·87–1·43; I 2 = 0%). The association was attributable to gestational hypertension, with no significant association for preeclampsia/eclampsia. Conclusion Maternal RSVpreF vaccination was associated with a small increase in HDP attributable to gestational hypertension and driven primarily by observational studies, in which residual confounding remains possible. The benefits of infant RSV prevention remain substantial, and these findings support continued postmarketing surveillance and informed shared decision-making.

title: An Appraisal of the Potential Downstream Benefits of RSV Vaccination in Older Adults
abstract: ABSTRACT Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) has long been underrecognized as a significant pathogen in older adults, despite accumulating evidence of its substantial morbidity and mortality burden in this population. While RSV vaccination is now well established as an effective intervention for preventing lower respiratory tract disease, this narrative review examines whether its public health value may extend beyond these primary clinical endpoints. A targeted search of Scopus and Web of Science from database inception to May 2026 was conducted to identify biological, epidemiological, observational, interventional, and modelling evidence relevant to potential downstream vaccine effects. The available evidence potentially supports hypotheses concerning possible reductions in cardiovascular complications and secondary bacterial infections, possible decreases in transmission to younger household contacts, and potential preservation of functional status and independence. However, the strength of evidence varies substantially across these outcomes. Cardiovascular protection has not been independently demonstrated in randomized trials, bacterial and antimicrobial‐use outcomes have rarely been prespecified, real‐world household transmission studies are unavailable, and functional trajectories may be strongly modified by baseline frailty and pre‐existing disability. RSV vaccination in older adults therefore remains a well‐validated strategy for preventing acute respiratory disease, whereas its proposed broader effects should be regarded as biologically plausible but incompletely demonstrated benefits. Future studies should incorporate prespecified cardiovascular, bacterial, transmission, geriatric, and functional outcomes, with particular attention to frailty, antimicrobial use, and longer‐term follow‐up.

title: Eligibility-Identification Difficulty and Self-Reported Preventive Care Implementation Among Japanese Primary Care Physicians.
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Primary care is an important setting for prevention, but implementation gaps may arise before clinicians can identify patients eligible for preventive services. We described self‐reported preventive care implementation among Japanese primary care physicians and examined whether lower implementation co‐occurred with eligibility‐identification difficulty. Methods We conducted a nationwide web‐based cross‐sectional survey of physician members of the Japan Primary Care Association from May to June 2025. Respondents reported recommendation consistency for 30 preventive services, difficulty identifying eligible patients, and perceived barriers. Service‐level implementation and eligibility‐identification difficulty were summarized in a two‐axis map. Results Among 258 respondents, 56.2% reported structured preventive care training and 53.9% used outpatient reminders. “Mostly achieved” recommendation was relatively high for hypertension, diabetes, and dyslipidaemia screening and influenza vaccination, but low for screening for domestic violence, chlamydia/gonorrhea, abdominal aortic aneurysm, anxiety, and depression, respiratory syncytial virus vaccination, and folic acid counseling. Difficulty identifying eligible patients was highest for domestic violence screening (14.0%), chlamydia/gonorrhea screening (13.6%), hepatitis C screening (10.5%), and respiratory syncytial virus vaccination (7.8%). Common barriers were time constraints, insufficient knowledge or skills, low patient interest, and financial or reimbursement issues. Conclusions Self‐reported implementation varied substantially across services. Some low‐implementation services also involved eligibility‐identification difficulty, suggesting an upstream implementation problem. Japanese primary care may need systems that make eligibility visible through training, reminders, prompts, registries, and team‐based workflows.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the implementation of preventive care for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) among Japanese primary care physicians. It examines the difficulty in identifying eligible patients for RSV-related preventive services and the self-reported implementation of these services by clinicians.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a nationwide web-based cross-sectional survey conducted among physician members of the Japan Primary Care Association from May to June 2025. It collects data on self-reported preventive care implementation and eligibility-identification difficulty for RSV-related services.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that self-reported implementation of RSV preventive care varies substantially across services. Specifically, services such as RSV bronchiolitis and respiratory syncytial virus vaccination show lower implementation rates and higher difficulty in identifying eligible patients.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights that some low-implementation services also involve difficulty in identifying eligible patients, suggesting potential upstream implementation problems. However, the evidence does not provide detailed mechanisms or solutions for these challenges.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that Japanese primary care may need systems to make eligibility for RSV preventive services more visible, such as training, reminders, prompts, registries, and team-based workflows.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本次审查的重点是日本初级保健医生对 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 预防性护理的实施情况。它研究了确定符合 RSV 相关预防服务资格的患者的困难以及临床医生自我报告的这些服务的实施情况。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该审查是 2025 年 5 月至 6 月在日本初级保健协会的医生成员中进行的一项全国性网络横断面调查。它收集了有关自我报告的预防性护理实施情况以及 RSV 相关服务的资格识别难度的数据。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 审查得出的结论是,各服务部门自我报告的 RSV 预防护理实施情况存在很大差异。具体而言,RSV 毛细支气管炎 和 呼吸道合胞病毒 疫苗接种 等服务的实施率较低,识别合格患者的难度较高。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 审查强调,一些实施程度较低的服务还难以识别符合条件的患者,这表明潜在的上游实施问题。然而,证据并未提供应对这些挑战的详细机制或解决方案。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 审查表明,日本初级保健可能需要系统来使 RSV 预防服务的资格更加明显,例如培训、提醒、提示、登记和基于团队的工作流程。

abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 初级保健是预防的重要场所,但在临床医生识别出符合预防性服务资格的患者之前,可能会出现实施差距。我们描述了日本初级保健医生自我报告的预防保健实施情况,并检查了较低的实施情况是否与资格识别困难同时发生。方法 我们于 2025 年 5 月至 6 月对日本初级保健协会的医生成员进行了一项全国性的网络横断面调查。受访者报告了 30 种预防性服务的推荐一致性、识别合格患者的困难以及感知到的障碍。服务水平实施和资格识别难度总结在双轴图中。结果 在 258 名受访者中,56.2% 的受访者表示接受了结构化的预防护理培训,53.9% 的受访者使用了门诊提醒。高血压、糖尿病、血脂异常筛查和流感 疫苗接种 的“基本达到”建议相对较高,但家庭暴力、衣原体/淋病、腹主动脉瘤、焦虑和抑郁、呼吸道合胞病毒 疫苗接种 和叶酸咨询的筛查建议较低。家庭暴力筛查 (14.0%)、衣原体/淋病筛查 (13.6%)、丙型肝炎筛查 (10.5%) 和 呼吸道合胞病毒 疫苗接种 (7.8%) 筛选合格患者的难度最高。常见的障碍是时间限制、知识或技能不足、患者兴趣低以及财务或报销问题。结论 不同服务的自我报告实施情况差异很大。一些低实施服务还涉及资格识别困难,表明存在上游实施问题。日本初级保健可能需要通过培训、提醒、提示、登记和基于团队的工作流程使资格可见的系统。

title: A cavity-reduced prefusion RSV F bivalent vaccine elicits durable and protective immunity
abstract: Abstract Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remains a major cause of severe respiratory disease, and stabilization of the prefusion (preF) conformation of the F glycoprotein is central for vaccine development. Here, we report a structure-guided engineering strategy that enhances preF stability by reducing the hydrophobic cavity within the trimeric F protein. Targeted modifications at metastability-associated sites generated RVF-88, a disulfide-free stabilized preF immunogen that preserves key neutralizing epitopes, including antigenic site Ø, while exhibiting improved structural integrity and long-term storage stability. Formulated as an unadjuvanted bivalent vaccine, RVF-88 elicited potent neutralizing antibody responses and durable immune protection lasting up to 5 months in mice. Vaccination also protected both mice and cotton rats against RSV challenge. Structural analyses confirmed the intended cavity-reduction design, revealing a reduced apical hydrophobic cavity volume and surface area while maintaining the prefusion architecture. Together, these findings establish hydrophobic cavity reduction as a rational strategy for stabilizing prefusion RSV F and provide a promising next-generation vaccine candidate with improved stability and immunogenicity for further clinical development.

The vaccine was developed using structure-guided engineering and demonstrated potent neutralizing antibody responses and durable immune protection in mice, lasting up to 5 months. abstract_zh: 摘要 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 仍然是严重呼吸道疾病的主要原因,F 糖蛋白预融合 (preF) 构象的稳定对于 疫苗 的发展至关重要。在这里,我们报告了一种结构引导的工程策略,该策略通过减少三聚体 F 蛋白内的疏水空腔来增强 preF 稳定性。对亚稳定性相关位点进行靶向修饰生成了 RVF-88,这是一种不含二硫键的稳定 preF 免疫原,可保留关键中和表位,包括抗原位点 Ø,同时表现出改善的结构完整性和长期储存稳定性。RVF-88 采用无佐剂二价 疫苗 配方,在小鼠体内引发有效的中和抗体反应和持久的免疫保护,可持续长达 5 个月。疫苗接种 还保护小鼠和棉鼠免受 RSV 攻击。结构分析证实了预期的空腔减少设计,揭示了顶端疏水空腔体积和表面积的减少,同时保持了预融合结构。总之,这些发现确立了疏水腔减少作为稳定预灌 RSV F 的合理策略,并为进一步的临床开发提供了具有改进的稳定性和免疫原性的有前途的下一代 疫苗 候选药物。

title: Quality Improvement Initiative to Increase Newborn RSV Immunization
abstract: Background: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of respiratory illness in infants. In 2023, the Food and Drug Administration approved 2 methods of RSV prevention: birthing parent bivalent RSVpreF vaccine and infant nirsevimab monoclonal antibody. During the 2023–2024 RSV season, 57.8% of newborns at Montefiore Medical Center Wakefield Division were immunized. This single-center quality improvement initiative aimed to increase RSV immunization rates by 10% in the following season. Methods: Multidisciplinary teams implemented targeted interventions across preconception, prenatal, and postnatal periods. Strategies included posting RSV educational flyers, conducting staff education meetings, and incorporating mandatory RSV-related phrases into newborn discharge summaries. Weekly monitoring enabled real-time tracking and adjustments. Immunization rates were tracked using maternal records and newborn discharge data; engagement with educational materials was measured using quick-response code analytics. Results: The average newborn RSV immunization rate increased to 75.9% during the 2024–2025 season. Maternal RSVpreF uptake significantly increased from 10.9 to 33.5% within the first month. The nirsevimab administration remained stable at 57.1% in the second season. Required documentation in the electronic medical record ensured that all newborns were assessed for immunization before discharge. Quick-response code flyers had moderate engagement, with higher click-through rates for Spanish-language materials. Conclusions: This quality improvement initiative exceeded its target, improving newborn RSV protection through provider education, documentation standardization, and patient outreach. These interventions streamlined workflow and advanced equitable immunization practices. Continued refinements and provider awareness will be essential to sustain high immunization rates amid evolving vaccine guidance and hesitancy.

title_zh: 提高新生儿 RSV 免疫接种质量的举措
source_body_en: Background: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of respiratory illness in infants. In 2023, the Food and Drug Administration approved 2 methods of RSV prevention: birthing parent bivalent RSVpreF vaccine and infant nirsevimab monoclonal antibody. During the 2023–2024 RSV season, 57.8% of newborns at Montefiore Medical Center Wakefield Division were immunized. This single-center quality improvement initiative aimed to increase RSV immunization rates by 10% in the following season. Methods: Multidisciplinary teams implemented targeted interventions across preconception, prenatal, and postnatal periods. Strategies included posting RSV educational flyers, conducting staff education meetings, and incorporating mandatory RSV-related phrases into newborn discharge summaries. Weekly monitoring enabled real-time tracking and adjustments. Immunization rates were tracked using maternal records and newborn discharge data; engagement with educational materials was measured using quick-response code analytics. Results: The average newborn RSV immunization rate increased to 75.9% during the 2024–2025 season. Maternal RSVpreF uptake significantly increased from 10.9 to 33.5% within the first month. The nirsevimab administration remained stable at 57.1% in the second season. Required documentation in the electronic medical record ensured that all newborns were assessed for immunization before discharge. Quick-response code flyers had moderate engagement, with higher click-through rates for Spanish-language materials. Conclusions: This quality improvement initiative exceeded its target, improving newborn RSV protection through provider education, documentation standardization, and patient outreach. These interventions streamlined workflow and advanced equitable immunization practices. Continued refinements and provider awareness will be essential to sustain high immunization rates amid evolving vaccine guidance and hesitancy.

title: Sociodemographic and Clinical Factors Associated With Nirsevimab Receipt Among Children Aged Younger Than 20 Months in the New Vaccine Surveillance Network in 2023 to 2025.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: We aim to evaluate the association of sociodemographic and clinical factors with nirsevimab receipt among children with medically attended acute respiratory illness (ARI) across multiple seasons and beyond birth hospitalization. PATIENTS AND METHODS: We included nirsevimab-eligible children aged younger than 8 months and 8 to 19 months with ARI enrolled in the New Vaccine Surveillance Network during the 2023 to 2024 and 2024 to 2025 respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) seasons (October 1 to March 31). A mixed-effects logistic regression model was used to evaluate the association between sociodemographic and clinical factors with the likelihood of nirsevimab receipt among enrolled children aged younger than 8 months. RESULTS: Of the 2151 nirsevimab-eligible children with ARI enrolled in the 2023 to 2024 RSV season and 1819 in the 2024 to 2025 RSV season, 96% were aged younger than 8 months and in their first RSV season. Fourteen percent and 36% of eligible children aged younger than 8 months received nirsevimab in the 2023 to 2024 and 2024 to 2025 seasons, respectively. Among infants aged younger than 8 months, those born during the RSV season and those with an underlying medical condition were more likely to receive nirsevimab in both RSV seasons; infant female sex and maternal education were also associated with nirsevimab receipt during 2023 to 2024 but not 2024 to 2025. CONCLUSION: Most nirsevimab-eligible children with medically attended ARI in this analysis did not receive nirsevimab during the first 2 seasons of nirsevimab availability. Factors such as birth before the RSV season were associated with a decreased likelihood of nirsevimab receipt, emphasizing the need for tailored interventions following birth hospitalization to increase nirsevimab uptake for this group of children.

title: The new UK RSV maternal vaccination programme and ethnic disparities in uptake in a diverse urban population: A Retrospective Study
abstract: Abstract Introduction: RSV is the leading cause of bronchiolitis and acute lower respiratory tract infections in infants under 6 months of age. In the UK, the RSV vaccine was introduced in the National Health System from September 2024, recommended antenatally from 28 weeks of gestation. This retrospective observational study examines maternal uptake of the RSV vaccine across two hospital sites in the UK Aim: To analyse ethnic variations in antenatal RSV Vaccine uptake Method: Data was collected between the months of 15 September 2024 to 29 April 2025 on vaccine uptake from electronic patient records, as well as infants admitted with lower respiratory tract infections to the hospital (N = 5,757). Results: 2,931 women received the antenatal RSV vaccine (51% uptake). Vaccine uptake varied by ethnicity: highest amongst White British (62%), Bangladeshi (59%); lowest in Pakistani women (30%). Among 67 infants admitted with LRTI, 15 were RSV-positive (1 with a vaccinated mother) and 52 RSV-negative (14 with vaccinated mothers). Discussion: Overall vaccine uptake was 51%, indicating moderate early acceptance during the first RSV season following national implementation. However, variations in uptake was observed across ethnic groups, highlighting emerging inequalities that warrant attention as the programme becomes established. Infant admission data in this cohort suggest a potential protective association between maternal vaccination and RSV-related hospitalisation, although sample size was small. Conclusion: Findings demonstrates moderate uptake with significant ethnic variation. Addressing these disparities will be vital to maximise the public health impact against RSV-related morbidity in infancy.

abstract_zh: 摘要:RSV 是导致 6 个月以下婴儿 毛细支气管炎 和急性下呼吸道感染的主要原因。在英国,RSV 疫苗 自 2024 年 9 月起被引入国家卫生系统,建议从妊娠 28 周起进行产前接种。这项回顾性观察研究检查了英国两家医院的母亲对 RSV 疫苗 的摄取情况 目的:分析产前 RSV 疫苗 摄取的种族差异 方法:从 2024 年 9 月 15 日至 2025 年 4 月 29 日期间从电子病历以及因下呼吸道感染入院的婴儿中收集 疫苗 摄取数据(N = 5,757)。结果:2,931 名女性接受了产前 RSV 疫苗(51% 的接受率)。疫苗 的使用率因种族而异:最高的是英国白人 (62%)、孟加拉国人 (59%);巴基斯坦女性比例最低(30%)。在 67 名因 LRTI 入院的婴儿中,15 名 RSV 阳性(1 名接种疫苗的母亲),52 名 RSV 阴性(14 名接种疫苗的母亲)。讨论:疫苗 的总体采用率为 51%,表明在全国实施后第一个 RSV 季节期间有适度的早期接受。然而,不同种族群体的接受情况存在差异,凸显了随着该计划的建立,值得关注的新出现的不平等现象。本 队列研究 中的婴儿入院数据表明,尽管样本量较小,但母亲 队列研究 与 RSV 相关住院治疗之间存在潜在的保护性关联。结论:研究结果表明,接受程度适中,但存在显着的种族差异。解决这些差异对于最大限度地减少婴儿期呼吸道合胞病毒相关发病率的公共卫生影响至关重要。

title: Arp2/3 complex-dependent actin remodeling is required for efficient RSV uncoating in A549 cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Productive human respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) cell entry requires coordinated interactions between viral proteins and host-cell factors at the plasma membrane-actin cortex interface. Branched actin networks remodel this interface, but their precise contribution to the early stages of RSV infection remains unclear. Here, we interfered with Arp2/3 complex-dependent actin filament branching by generating A549 cell lines disrupted for expression of the essential Arp2 subunit by CRISPR/Cas9. Permanent loss of Arp2 reduced the infection of the RSV long GFP reporter virus, as quantified over the first 24 h post-infection. Compromised infection efficiency in Arp2 knockout cells persisted at later time points, and also resulted in reduced syncytia formation. Arp2 re-expression restored Arp2/3 complex-dependent actin remodeling and rescued RSV infection in Arp2 KO cells. Notably, impaired RSV infection was not accompanied by obvious changes in viral host cell attachment. Moreover, photoactivated localization microscopy (PALM) studies revealed comparable receptor diffusion and clustering in cells stably expressing mEos3.2-tagged insulin-like growth factor I receptor (IGF1R). title_zh: A549 细胞中 RSV 高效脱壳需要 Arp2/3 复合物依赖性肌动蛋白重塑
source_body_en: ABSTRACT Productive human respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) cell entry requires coordinated interactions between viral proteins and host-cell factors at the plasma membrane-actin cortex interface. Branched actin networks remodel this interface, but their precise contribution to the early stages of RSV infection remains unclear. Here, we interfered with Arp2/3 complex-dependent actin filament branching by generating A549 cell lines disrupted for expression of the essential Arp2 subunit by CRISPR/Cas9. Permanent loss of Arp2 reduced the infection of the RSV long GFP reporter virus, as quantified over the first 24 h post-infection. Compromised infection efficiency in Arp2 knockout cells persisted at later time points, and also resulted in reduced syncytia formation. Arp2 re-expression restored Arp2/3 complex-dependent actin remodeling and rescued RSV infection in Arp2 KO cells. Notably, impaired RSV infection was not accompanied by obvious changes in viral host cell attachment. Moreover, photoactivated localization microscopy (PALM) studies revealed comparable receptor diffusion and clustering in cells stably expressing mEos3.2-tagged insulin-like growth factor I receptor (IGF1R). Although Arp2/3-deficient cells displayed fewer, albeit larger, macropinosomes compared with WT cells, no changes were observed for internalized RSV genome levels. In contrast, Arp2-deficient cells appeared suppressed in RSV-F mediated virus-like particle uncoating efficiency. Consequently, viral mRNA expression and the cellular type III interferon response were reduced. Together, these data reveal that Arp2/3 complex-dependent, branched actin networks contribute to the efficiency of RSV uncoating. These findings define Arp2/3 complex-dependent branched actin networks as a host determinant of RSV-F-mediated uncoating and provide a practical approach to quantify uncoating without engineering the RSV genome.
abstract_zh: 摘要 有效的人类 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 细胞进入需要病毒蛋白和 宿主 细胞因子在质膜-肌动蛋白皮质界面处的协调相互作用。分支肌动蛋白网络重塑了该界面,但它们对 RSV 感染早期阶段的确切贡献仍不清楚。在这里,我们通过生成 A549 细胞系来干扰 Arp2/3 复合物依赖性肌动蛋白丝分支,该细胞系被 CRISPR/Cas9 破坏以表达必需的 Arp2 亚基。根据感染后 24 小时内的量化结果,Arp2 的永久缺失减少了 RSV 长 GFP 报告病毒的感染。Arp2 敲除细胞的感染效率在以后的时间点持续存在,并且还导致合胞体形成减少。Arp2 重新表达可恢复 Arp2/3 复合物依赖性肌动蛋白重塑,并挽救 Arp2 KO 细胞中的 RSV 感染。值得注意的是,RSV 感染受损并不伴随病毒 宿主 细胞附着的明显变化。此外,光激活定位显微镜 (PALM) 研究揭示了稳定表达 mEos3.2 标记的胰岛素样生长因子 I 受体 (IGF1R) 的细胞中类似的受体扩散和聚集。尽管与 WT 细胞相比,Arp2/3 缺陷细胞显示出较少但较大的巨脂质体,但未观察到内化 RSV 基因组 水平的变化。相比之下,Arp2缺陷细胞的RSV-F介导的病毒样颗粒脱壳效率似乎受到抑制。因此,病毒 mRNA 表达和细胞 III 型干扰素反应降低。总之,这些数据表明 Arp2/3 复合物依赖性分支肌动蛋白网络有助于 RSV 脱壳的效率。重要性 人类 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 是严重呼吸道疾病的主要原因。感染始于质膜-肌动蛋白皮质界面,但肌动蛋白在高效 RSV 进入中的作用仍不清楚。使用 CRISPR/Cas9 破坏 A549 细胞中必需的 Arp2/3 复合体亚基 Arp2,我们发现分支肌动蛋白网络是有效 RSV 感染所必需的。尽管肌动蛋白网络重塑,光激活定位显微镜显示 RSV 受体 IGF1R 的扩散和聚集没有变化。尽管 Arp2 缺陷细胞中的巨胞饮作用受到影响,但 RSV 的附着和内化并未受到影响。相比之下,基于β-内酰胺酶病毒样颗粒的测定显示RSV-F介导的脱壳缺陷,随后病毒基因表达减少和III型干扰素反应较弱。这些发现将 Arp2/3 复合物依赖性分支肌动蛋白网络定义为 RSV-F 介导的脱壳的 宿主 决定因素,并提供了一种无需设计 RSV 基因组 即可量化脱壳的实用方法。

title: The airway microbiome in asthma.
abstract: TOPIC IMPORTANCE: Asthma is a heterogenous airways disease characterized by variable airflow limitation, airway inflammation and bronchial hyperresponsiveness. There is evidence to suggest that the airway microbiome plays an important role in asthma pathophysiology. Most microbiome studies have investigated the bacterial constituents of the microbiome and further studies are needed to investigate the role of the airway virome and mycobiome in asthma. REVIEW FINDINGS: Airway microbiome dysbiosis is associated with asthma development, disease severity and inflammatory endotypes. However, it remains unclear whether dysbiosis drives inflammation or is a result of inflammation. Haemophilus and Moraxella alongside rhinovirus and respiratory syncytial virus have been shown to be associated with the development of asthma in children. In established asthma, airway microbiome dysbiosis is associated with severity and risk of exacerbation. Distinct airway microbiome profiles are observed for the different inflammatory endotypes. Asthmatic patients with eosinophilic inflammation have higher microbial diversity similar to healthy individuals while neutrophilic inflammation is associated with reduced microbial diversity, higher bacterial load and a pathogen-dominated microbiome profile suggesting an important role for dysbiosis in asthma that is currently refractory to anti-T2 biologic therapy. SUMMARY: To understand the role of the microbiome in asthma, microbiome data must be integrated with other 'omic approaches' such as proteomics. Recent studies have used a multi-omic approach to investigate the microbiome and host interaction as well as identifying asthma endotypes and potential therapeutic targets. Antibiotics, probiotics, monoclonal antibodies, and diet could theoretically be used to therapeutically target the airway and gut microbiome in asthma.

title_original: The airway microbiome in asthma.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the role of the airway microbiome in asthma, particularly examining how microbial dysbiosis may influence asthma development, severity, and inflammatory endotypes. The central question is whether airway microbiome dysbiosis drives inflammation or is a consequence of it.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of existing literature, with no explicit mention of systematic search methods, databases, or meta-analysis. It includes general observations and interpretations from various studies on the microbiome and asthma.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that airway microbiome dysbiosis is associated with asthma development, disease severity, and inflammatory endotypes. It highlights that distinct microbiome profiles are observed for different endotypes, with eosinophilic inflammation showing higher microbial diversity and neutrophilic inflammation associated with reduced diversity and a pathogen-dominated microbiome.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There is uncertainty regarding whether microbiome dysbiosis is a cause or a result of inflammation in asthma. The review also notes that most studies have focused on bacterial components, with limited investigation into the virome and mycobiome. Additionally, the role of specific viruses like rhinovirus and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in asthma pathophysiology remains underexplored.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests integrating microbiome data with other 'omic approaches' to better understand asthma mechanisms. It also highlights the potential for therapeutic interventions targeting the microbiome, such as antibiotics, probiotics, monoclonal antibodies, and dietary modifications, particularly in refractory asthma cases.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the role of the airway microbiome in asthma, emphasizing its association with disease development, severity, and inflammatory endotypes. While there is evidence linking microbiome dysbiosis to asthma, the causative relationship remains unclear. The review highlights the need for further studies on the virome and mycobiome, as well as the integration of microbiome data with other 'omic approaches' to identify therapeutic targets. It also suggests potential interventions, including antibiotics, probiotics, and dietary changes, to modulate the microbiome in asthma management.

elements_en.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the role of the airway microbiome in asthma, particularly examining how microbial dysbiosis may influence asthma development, severity, and inflammatory endotypes. The central question is whether airway microbiome dysbiosis drives inflammation or is a consequence of it.
elements_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of existing literature, with no explicit mention of systematic search methods, databases, or meta-analysis. It includes general observations and interpretations from various studies on the microbiome and asthma.
elements_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that airway microbiome dysbiosis is associated with asthma development, disease severity, and inflammatory endotypes. It highlights that distinct microbiome profiles are observed for different endotypes, with eosinophilic inflammation showing higher microbial diversity and neutrophilic inflammation associated with reduced diversity and a pathogen-dominated microbiome.
elements_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There is uncertainty regarding whether microbiome dysbiosis is a cause or a result of inflammation in asthma. The review also notes that most studies have focused on bacterial components, with limited investigation into the virome and mycobiome. Additionally, the role of specific viruses like rhinovirus and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in asthma pathophysiology remains underexplored.
elements_en.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests integrating microbiome data with other 'omic approaches' to better understand asthma mechanisms. It also highlights the potential for therapeutic interventions targeting the microbiome, such as antibiotics, probiotics, monoclonal antibodies, and dietary modifications, particularly in refractory asthma cases.

title_zh: 哮喘患者的气道微生物组
source_body_en: TOPIC IMPORTANCE: Asthma is a heterogenous airways disease characterized by variable airflow limitation, airway inflammation and bronchial hyperresponsiveness. There is evidence to suggest that the airway microbiome plays an important role in asthma pathophysiology. Most microbiome studies have investigated the bacterial constituents of the microbiome and further studies are needed to investigate the role of the airway virome and mycobiome in asthma. REVIEW FINDINGS: Airway microbiome dysbiosis is associated with asthma development, disease severity and inflammatory endotypes. However, it remains unclear whether dysbiosis drives inflammation or is a result of inflammation. Haemophilus and Moraxella alongside rhinovirus and respiratory syncytial virus have been shown to be associated with the development of asthma in children. In established asthma, airway microbiome dysbiosis is associated with severity and risk of exacerbation. Distinct airway microbiome profiles are observed for the different inflammatory endotypes. Asthmatic patients with eosinophilic inflammation have higher microbial diversity similar to healthy individuals while neutrophilic inflammation is associated with reduced microbial diversity, higher bacterial load and a pathogen-dominated microbiome profile suggesting an important role for dysbiosis in asthma that is currently refractory to anti-T2 biologic therapy. SUMMARY: To understand the role of the microbiome in asthma, microbiome data must be integrated with other 'omic approaches' such as proteomics. Recent studies have used a multi-omic approach to investigate the microbiome and host interaction as well as identifying asthma endotypes and potential therapeutic targets. Antibiotics, probiotics, monoclonal antibodies, and diet could theoretically be used to therapeutically target the airway and gut microbiome in asthma.
abstract_zh: 主题重要性:哮喘是一种异质性气道疾病,其特征是可变的气流受限、气道炎症和支气管高反应性。有证据表明气道微生物群在哮喘病理生理学中发挥重要作用。大多数微生物组研究已经调查了微生物组的细菌成分,需要进一步研究来调查气道病毒组和真菌组在哮喘中的作用。综述结果:气道微生物群失调与哮喘发展、疾病严重程度和炎症内型相关。然而,目前尚不清楚生态失调是导致炎症还是炎症的结果。嗜血杆菌和莫拉氏菌以及鼻病毒和 呼吸道合胞病毒 已被证明与儿童哮喘的发生有关。在已确诊的哮喘中,气道微生物群失调与严重程度和恶化风险相关。不同的炎症内型观察到不同的气道微生物组特征。患有嗜酸性粒细胞性炎症的哮喘患者与健康个体相似,具有较高的微生物多样性,而中性粒细胞性炎症与微生物多样性降低、细菌负荷较高和病原体主导的微生物组特征相关,表明生态失调在目前抗 T2 生物治疗难治性哮喘中发挥着重要作用。摘要:为了了解微生物组在哮喘中的作用,微生物组数据必须与蛋白质组学等其他“组学方法”相结合。最近的研究使用多组学方法来研究微生物组和 宿主 相互作用,并确定哮喘内型和潜在的治疗靶点。理论上,抗生素、益生菌、单克隆抗体和饮食可以用于针对哮喘气道和肠道微生物组进行治疗。

title: Prenatal RSVpreF Vaccination Uptake Associated with Non-English Primary Language During Its First Season at a Federally Qualified Health Center
abstract: Abstract Background RSV and bronchiolitis are major causes of hospitalizations and death among infants. The RSVpreF vaccine was approved and released in 2023 for pregnant women to prevent severe RSV in infants during their first RSV season. This is the first prenatal vaccine recommended since the COVID-19 vaccine was approved. However, other prenatal vaccination rates have remained low with a rise in overall vaccine hesitancy in recent years. Our cross-sectional study describes and compares the sociodemographic characteristics and health behaviors associated with first-season receipt of the RSVpreF vaccine among women receiving prenatal care at a federally qualified health center (FQHC). Methods Medical records of pregnant women with prenatal care visits at an Indianapolis, IN FQHC between 9/26/2023 and 3/31/2024 were reviewed and screened for RSVpreF vaccine eligibility. Vaccination status (RSVpreF, TDaP, influenza, and COVID-19), demographic information, obstetric history, adequacy of prenatal care, preferred language, and social determinants of health were collected. Corresponding infant charts were reviewed for nirsevimab and 2-month immunizations and breastfeeding status. Women who received the RSVpreF vaccine were compared to those who did not get the vaccine using statistical analyses. Results Of 344 women eligible for the RSVpreF vaccine, 78 (23%) received the vaccine and 266 (77%) did not. Nine (2.6%) infants received nirsevimab. More women who received the RSVpreF vaccine spoke a preferred language other than English (81%) compared to those who did not receive the vaccine (66%) (P=0.0138). More women received adequate prenatal care (53%) in the RSVpreF vaccinated group compared to the unvaccinated group (37%) (P=0.0128) and had 0.88 more prenatal care visits (P=0.0241). The RSVpreF vaccinated group also received the TDaP and influenza vaccines more often, but both groups were above national average vaccination rates. There were no significant differences in race/ethnicity, age, gravida/parity, health insurance, transportation barriers, food insecurity, and housing instability. There were no differences in infant immunization and breastfeeding. Conclusion The presence of a language barrier often limits navigation of the healthcare system due to logistical difficulties, including requiring interpreter services. Likewise, immigration status influences seeking medical care and health insurance coverage. However, our study shows the opposite effect that those who primarily spoke languages other than English were more likely to receive the new RSVpreF vaccine than those who spoke English. Whether cultural factors have a larger influence than expected on pregnant women receiving new vaccines compared to logistical constraints from other social determinants of health requires further investigation.
journal: Journal of the Pediatric Infectious Diseases Society

abstract_original: Abstract Background RSV and bronchiolitis are major causes of hospitalizations and death among infants. The RSVpreF vaccine was approved and released in 2023 for pregnant women to prevent severe RSV in infants during their first RSV season. This is the first prenatal vaccine recommended since the COVID-19 vaccine was approved. However, other prenatal vaccination rates have remained low with a rise in overall vaccine hesitancy in recent years. Our cross-sectional study describes and compares the sociodemographic characteristics and health behaviors associated with first-season receipt of the RSVpreF vaccine among women receiving prenatal care at a federally qualified health center (FQHC). Methods Medical records of pregnant women with prenatal care visits at an Indianapolis, IN FQHC between 9/26/2023 and 3/31/2024 were reviewed and screened for RSVpreF vaccine eligibility. Vaccination status (RSVpreF, TDaP, influenza, and COVID-19), demographic information, obstetric history, adequacy of prenatal care, preferred language, and social determinants of health were collected. Corresponding infant charts were reviewed for nirsevimab and 2-month immunizations and breastfeeding status. Women who received the RSVpreF vaccine were compared to those who did not get the vaccine using statistical analyses. Results Of 344 women eligible for the RSVpreF vaccine, 78 (23%) received the vaccine and 266 (77%) did not. Nine (2.6%) infants received nirsevimab. More women who received the RSVpreF vaccine spoke a preferred language other than English (81%) compared to those who did not receive the vaccine (66%) (P=0.0138). More women received adequate prenatal care (53%) in the RSVpreF vaccinated group compared to the unvaccinated group (37%) (P=0.0128) and had 0.88 more prenatal care visits (P=0.0241). The RSVpreF vaccinated group also received the TDaP and influenza vaccines more often, but both groups were above national average vaccination rates. There were no significant differences in race/ethnicity, age, gravida/parity, health insurance, transportation barriers, food insecurity, and housing instability. There were no differences in infant immunization and breastfeeding. Conclusion The presence of a language barrier often limits navigation of the healthcare system due to logistical difficulties, including requiring interpreter services. Likewise, immigration status influences seeking medical care and health insurance coverage. However, our study shows the opposite effect that those who primarily spoke languages other than English were more likely to receive the new RSVpreF vaccine than those who spoke English. Whether cultural factors have a larger influence than expected on pregnant women receiving new vaccines compared to logistical constraints from other social determinants of health requires further investigation.

abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 RSV 和 毛细支气管炎 是婴儿住院和死亡的主要原因。RSVpreF 疫苗 于 2023 年获得批准并发布,适用于孕妇,以预防婴儿在第一个 RSV 季节感染严重 RSV。这是自 COVID-19 疫苗 获得批准以来第一个推荐的产前 疫苗。然而,其他产前 疫苗接种 率仍然较低,近年来总体 疫苗 犹豫不决的情况有所增加。我们的横断面研究描述并比较了在联邦合格健康中心 (FQHC) 接受产前护理的妇女中与第一季收到 RSVpreF 疫苗 相关的社会人口特征和健康行为。方法 对 2023 年 9 月 26 日至 2024 年 3 月 31 日期间在 IN FQHC 印第安纳波利斯市进行产前护理的孕妇的病历进行审查,并筛选其 RSVpreF 疫苗 资格。收集了 疫苗接种 状态(RSVpreF、TDaP、流感和 COVID-19)、人口统计信息、产科史、产前护理的充分性、首选语言和健康的社会决定因素。审查了相应婴儿图表的 尼塞韦单抗 和 2 个月免疫接种和母乳喂养状态。使用统计分析将接受 RSVpreF 疫苗 的女性与未接受 疫苗 的女性进行比较。结果 在 344 名符合 RSVpreF 疫苗 资格的女性中,78 名 (23%) 接受了 疫苗,266 名 (77%) 没有接受。九名 (2.6%) 婴儿接受了 尼塞韦单抗。与未接受 疫苗 的女性 (66%) 相比,接受 RSVpreF 疫苗 的女性使用英语以外的首选语言 (81%) 的人数较多 (P=0.0138)。与未接种疫苗组 (37%) 相比,RSVpreF 疫苗接种组中有更多女性 (53%) 接受了充分的产前护理 (P=0.0128),并且产前护理就诊次数增加了 0.88 次 (P=0.0241)。RSVpreF 疫苗接种组也更频繁地接受 TDaP 和流感 疫苗,但两组的 疫苗 率均高于全国平均水平。种族/民族、年龄、妊娠/胎次、健康保险、交通障碍、粮食不安全和住房不稳定方面没有显着差异。婴儿免疫接种和母乳喂养没有差异。结论 由于后勤困难(包括需要口译服务),语言障碍的存在常常限制医疗保健系统的导航。同样,移民身份也会影响寻求医疗护理和健康保险。然而,我们的研究显示了相反的效果,即主要讲英语以外的语言的人比讲英语的人更有可能收到新的 RSVpreF 疫苗。与其他健康社会决定因素的后勤限制相比,文化因素对接受新 疫苗 的孕妇的影响是否比预期更大,需要进一步调查。

title: A Systematic Review of Respiratory Viral Infections Outcomes in Immunocompromised Pediatric Patients
abstract: Abstract Background Respiratory Viral Infections (RVI) pose a significant challenge in high-risk pediatric patients with cancer and Hematopoietic Cell Transplant (HCT). Although reports have documented its burden, few studies have systematically analyzed data on outcomes of RVI in immunocompromised patients. Methods A systematic review was undertaken to describe respiratory viral infections outcome in immunocompromised pediatrics patients with febrile neutropenia (FN), HCT recipients, and solid organ transplant recipients (SOT) from published data between January 1, 2019 and October 1, 2025. Twenty-eight studies were included based on the presence of quantified effect estimates specifically Odds Ratio (OR), Hazards Ratio (HR), clinical burden statistics (median fever duration), and viral co-infection patterns. The results were analyzed using a narrative approach, organizing findings by outcome category to ensure comprehensive reporting of descriptive statistics and quantified risk estimates. Results Of the twenty-eight studies analyzed, RVIs were highly prevalent in 76.5% of febrile neutropenia cases versus 48.6% in controls. While Rhinovirus (HRV/HRE) was the most frequently identified pathogen across multiple studies (36.8%, 33.1%, 61%, 47%), Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) was strongly linked with severe outcomes, including Lower Respiratory Tract Infection (LRTI) progression and bacteremia. A high proportion of RVIs were nosocomial (79% in one study of HCT patients), and viral co-infections were common, occurring in up to 55% of cases and often involving RSV. Furthermore, antibiotic exposure prior to RVI onset was identified as a risk factor for LRTI progression in HCT recipients, and Pre-HSCT RVI was significantly associated with ICU transfer(OR = 3.45) and increased Treatment-Related Mortality (OR = 5.57). Human Parainfluenza Virus type 3 (PIV-3) URTIs were significantly associated with Air Flow Obstruction (HR 1.87), while RSV URTIs exhibited a stronger association with Bronchiolitis Obliterans Syndrome (HR 2.65). RVIs significantly impacted clinical management, resulting in chemotherapy delays for 22%-33% of patients, alongside considerable resource utilization including 16% hospitalization, 50% parenteral antibiotic use, and 18.6% PICU admission. Finally, a significant gap in care was noted as only 22% of pediatric cancer patients with influenza received oseltamivir. Conclusion Respiratory Viral Infections impose a substantial burden on immunocompromised children, leading to significant morbidity, mortality, resource use, and long-term complications. RSV, PIV-3, and influenza significantly increase mortality, highlighting the need for stricter infection control and prevention.

title_zh: 免疫功能低下儿科患者呼吸道病毒感染结果的系统评价
source_body_en: Abstract Background Respiratory Viral Infections (RVI) pose a significant challenge in high-risk pediatric patients with cancer and Hematopoietic Cell Transplant (HCT). Although reports have documented its burden, few studies have systematically analyzed data on outcomes of RVI in immunocompromised patients. Methods A systematic review was undertaken to describe respiratory viral infections outcome in immunocompromised pediatrics patients with febrile neutropenia (FN), HCT recipients, and solid organ transplant recipients (SOT) from published data between January 1, 2019 and October 1, 2025. Twenty-eight studies were included based on the presence of quantified effect estimates specifically Odds Ratio (OR), Hazards Ratio (HR), clinical burden statistics (median fever duration), and viral co-infection patterns. The results were analyzed using a narrative approach, organizing findings by outcome category to ensure comprehensive reporting of descriptive statistics and quantified risk estimates. Results Of the twenty-eight studies analyzed, RVIs were highly prevalent in 76.5% of febrile neutropenia cases versus 48.6% in controls. While Rhinovirus (HRV/HRE) was the most frequently identified pathogen across multiple studies (36.8%, 33.1%, 61%, 47%), Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) was strongly linked with severe outcomes, including Lower Respiratory Tract Infection (LRTI) progression and bacteremia. A high proportion of RVIs were nosocomial (79% in one study of HCT patients), and viral co-infections were common, occurring in up to 55% of cases and often involving RSV. Furthermore, antibiotic exposure prior to RVI onset was identified as a risk factor for LRTI progression in HCT recipients, and Pre-HSCT RVI was significantly associated with ICU transfer(OR = 3.45) and increased Treatment-Related Mortality (OR = 5.57). Human Parainfluenza Virus type 3 (PIV-3) URTIs were significantly associated with Air Flow Obstruction (HR 1.87), while RSV URTIs exhibited a stronger association with Bronchiolitis Obliterans Syndrome (HR 2.65). RVIs significantly impacted clinical management, resulting in chemotherapy delays for 22%-33% of patients, alongside considerable resource utilization including 16% hospitalization, 50% parenteral antibiotic use, and 18.6% PICU admission. Finally, a significant gap in care was noted as only 22% of pediatric cancer patients with influenza received oseltamivir. Conclusion Respiratory Viral Infections impose a substantial burden on immunocompromised children, leading to significant morbidity, mortality, resource use, and long-term complications. RSV, PIV-3, and influenza significantly increase mortality, highlighting the need for stricter infection control and prevention.
abstract_zh: 摘要背景 呼吸道病毒感染 (RVI) 对患有癌症和造血细胞移植 (HCT) 的高危儿科患者构成了重大挑战。尽管有报告记录了其负担,但很少有研究系统分析免疫功能低下患者 RVI 结果的数据。方法 根据 2019 年 1 月 1 日至 2025 年 10 月 1 日发表的数据,对患有发热性中性粒细胞减少症 (FN) 的免疫功能低下儿科患者、HCT 接受者和实体器官移植接受者 (SOT) 的呼吸道病毒感染结果进行系统评价。根据量化效果估计的存在,特别是比值比 (OR)、风险比 (HR)、临床负担统计(中位发热),纳入了 28 项研究。持续时间)和病毒共感染模式。使用叙述性方法对结果进行分析,按结果类别组织调查结果,以确保描述性统计数据和量化风险估计的综合报告。结果 在所分析的 28 项研究中,RVI 在发热性中性粒细胞减少症病例中的发生率为 76.5%,而对照组为 48.6%。虽然鼻病毒 (HRV/HRE) 是多项研究中最常见的病原体 (36.8%、33.1%、61%、47%),但 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 与严重后果密切相关,包括下呼吸道感染 (LRTI) 进展和菌血症。很大一部分 RVI 是院内感染(一项针对 HCT 患者的研究中为 79%),并且病毒合并感染很常见,发生率高达 55%,并且通常涉及 RSV。此外,RVI 发病前的抗生素暴露被确定为 HCT 受者 LRTI 进展的危险因素,HSCT 前 RVI 与 ICU 转移(OR = 3.45)和 治疗 相关 死亡率 增加显着相关(OR = 5.57)。人类副流感病毒 3 型 (PIV-3) URTI 与气流阻塞 (HR 1.87) 显着相关,而 RSV URTI 与 毛细支气管炎 闭塞症候群 (HR 2.65) 表现出更强的相关性。RVI 显着影响临床管理,导致 22%-33% 的患者化疗延迟,同时资源利用率很高,包括 16% 住院、50% 肠外抗生素使用和 18.6% 入​​院 PICU。最后,护理方面存在显着差距,因为只有 22% 的流感儿科癌症患者接受了奥司他韦治疗。结论 呼吸道病毒感染给免疫功能低下的儿童带来了沉重负担,导致显着的发病率、死亡率、资源使用和长期并发症。RSV、PIV-3 和流感显着增加 死亡率,突出表明需要更严格的感染控制和预防。

title: Wastewater and Environmental Surveillance in Cities with Sewered and Non-sewered Sanitation: Evidence from Kampala, Uganda
abstract: Summary Background: Wastewater and environmental surveillance (WES) enables community-level monitoring of infectious diseases. Most progress has focused on sewer-based surveillance, yet nearly half of the global population relies on non-sewered sanitation. In non-sewered settings, urban drainage channels have been used for poliovirus environmental surveillance, but their potential for a multi-pathogen WES with spatially defined catchments, and comparability to sewer-based surveillance, remains under-explored. Methods: Ten drainage channel sampling points with delineated micro-catchments (0.95-3.83 km2 with 12,885-44,146 people) were selected within Kampala. A total of 255 drainage channel and 54 wastewater treatment plant (WWTP) influent samples were collected during two campaigns in March and September-October 2025. A multi-target panel was quantified by digital PCR, including enteric viruses (Norovirus GI and GII, Rotavirus), respiratory viruses (SARS-CoV-2, Influenza A and B viruses, Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV)), non-O1/O139 Vibrio cholerae (V. cholerae), and Pepper Mild Mottle Virus (PMMoV) as a fecal indicator. Findings: Enteric viruses, non-O1/O139 V. cholerae, and PMMoV were consistently detected across all drainage channels and WWTP influents. Concentrations were generally lower in drainage than WWTP influents, except for non-O1/O139 V. When normalized by PMMoV, concentrations across most drainage channels were comparable to WWTP influents, although comparability varied by target and location. Both concentrations and PMMoV-normalized concentrations varied across sampling locations. Trends between campaigns varied by pathogen target and were not explained by any single micro-catchment characteristic. Influenza A virus was the most frequently detected respiratory virus (8-23% in drainage channels; 3-10% in WWTP influents), while SARS-CoV-2, Influenza B, and RSV were rarely detected. Interpretation: PMMoV-normalized concentrations across most micro-catchments were comparable to WWTP influents, with spatial heterogeneity implying neighborhood-level differences in disease prevalence. Catchment-delineated drainage surveillance has potential to offer spatially resolved public health information in non-sewered settings comparable to sewer-based wastewater monitoring. Funding: Eawag Discretionary Funding

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore the potential of urban drainage channels for multi-pathogen wastewater and environmental surveillance in non-sewered settings, addressing the gap in understanding their utility compared to sewer-based systems.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in Kampala, Uganda, with ten drainage channel sampling points and 54 wastewater treatment plant influent samples collected during two campaigns in March and September-October 2025.
analysis.methods: A multi-target panel was quantified using digital PCR, including respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) among other pathogens, and samples were normalized by Pepper Mild Mottle Virus (PMMoV) as a fecal indicator.
analysis.main_results: Respiratory syncytial virus was rarely detected in both drainage channels and wastewater treatment plant influents, with concentrations varying across sampling locations.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The low detection rates of RSV suggest that it may not be as prevalent in the sampled non-sewered settings compared to other pathogens, but the study highlights the potential of drainage surveillance to provide spatially resolved public health data.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that drainage-based surveillance could be a valuable tool for monitoring RSV in non-sewered urban areas, offering insights into disease prevalence at the neighborhood level.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's results are limited by the low detection rates of RSV, and the comparability of drainage and wastewater surveillance varied by location and pathogen, indicating the need for further targeted research.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the feasibility of using urban drainage channels for multi-pathogen wastewater and environmental surveillance in non-sewered settings, focusing on respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in Kampala, Uganda. It collected 255 drainage channel and 54 wastewater treatment plant influent samples during two campaigns in 2025. RSV was rarely detected in both sample types, with concentrations varying across locations. The low detection rates suggest limited prevalence in the sampled areas, but the study highlights the potential of drainage surveillance to provide spatially resolved public health data. The findings imply that drainage-based monitoring could be useful for tracking RSV in non-sewered urban environments, though further research is needed to confirm these results. The study's limitations include the variability in comparability between drainage and wastewater samples, which may affect the reliability of surveillance data.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在探索城市排水沟在非污水收集环境中用于多病原体废水和环境监测的潜力,以填补其在效用方面相较于污水收集系统的认知缺口。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 研究在乌干达坎帕拉市进行,共设置10个排水沟采样点,并在2025年3月及9-10月两个时段收集了54份废水治疗厂进水样本。
elements_zh.methods: 采用数字PCR技术对多靶标面板进行定量分析,其中包括呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)等病原体,并以辣椒轻斑驳病毒(PMMoV)作为粪便指示剂对样本进行标准化处理。
elements_zh.main_results: 呼吸道合胞病毒 在排水沟和废水 治疗 工厂进水中很少检测到,不同采样地点的浓度各不相同。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: RSV 的低检出率表明,与其他病原体相比,它在采样的非下水道环境中可能并不那么普遍,但该研究强调了排水 监测 提供空间解析公共卫生数据的潜力。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,基于排水系统的 监测 可能是监测无下水道城市地区 RSV 的宝贵工具,可提供对社区层面疾病 患病率 的深入了解。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的结果受到RSV检出率低的限制,并且排水和废水监测的可比性因地点和病原体而异,表明需要进一步开展有针对性的研究。

title_zh: 有下水道和无下水道卫生设施的城市中的废水和环境 监测:来自乌干达坎帕拉的证据
source_body_en: Summary Background: Wastewater and environmental surveillance (WES) enables community-level monitoring of infectious diseases. Most progress has focused on sewer-based surveillance, yet nearly half of the global population relies on non-sewered sanitation. In non-sewered settings, urban drainage channels have been used for poliovirus environmental surveillance, but their potential for a multi-pathogen WES with spatially defined catchments, and comparability to sewer-based surveillance, remains under-explored. Methods: Ten drainage channel sampling points with delineated micro-catchments (0.95-3.83 km2 with 12,885-44,146 people) were selected within Kampala. A total of 255 drainage channel and 54 wastewater treatment plant (WWTP) influent samples were collected during two campaigns in March and September-October 2025. A multi-target panel was quantified by digital PCR, including enteric viruses (Norovirus GI and GII, Rotavirus), respiratory viruses (SARS-CoV-2, Influenza A and B viruses, Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV)), non-O1/O139 Vibrio cholerae (V. cholerae), and Pepper Mild Mottle Virus (PMMoV) as a fecal indicator. Findings: Enteric viruses, non-O1/O139 V. cholerae, and PMMoV were consistently detected across all drainage channels and WWTP influents. Concentrations were generally lower in drainage than WWTP influents, except for non-O1/O139 V. When normalized by PMMoV, concentrations across most drainage channels were comparable to WWTP influents, although comparability varied by target and location. Both concentrations and PMMoV-normalized concentrations varied across sampling locations. Trends between campaigns varied by pathogen target and were not explained by any single micro-catchment characteristic. Influenza A virus was the most frequently detected respiratory virus (8-23% in drainage channels; 3-10% in WWTP influents), while SARS-CoV-2, Influenza B, and RSV were rarely detected. Interpretation: PMMoV-normalized concentrations across most micro-catchments were comparable to WWTP influents, with spatial heterogeneity implying neighborhood-level differences in disease prevalence. Catchment-delineated drainage surveillance has potential to offer spatially resolved public health information in non-sewered settings comparable to sewer-based wastewater monitoring. Funding: Eawag Discretionary Funding

title: Anellovirus-mediated interferon dysregulation enhances virus-induced lung injury.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To characterize the lung virome after lung transplantation and test whether anelloviruses modulate innate immune responses that influence susceptibility to respiratory viral-associated allograft injury. RATIONALE: The lung virome (LV) and its interactions with the host immune system leading to allograft injury after lung -transplantation are not well characterized. METHODS: Shotgun metagenomics and qPCR was performed on a multicenter BAL/serum cohort from lung transplant recipients (LTRs). Viral constructs from a Betatorquevirus clade (BTV) and group 2 torque teno viruses were transfected in primary bronchial epithelial cells (PBECs) or airways of C57BL/6 mice with and without exposure to influenza A virus (IAV) or respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: LV in LTRs was dominated by viruses from the family Anelloviridae. Chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD) LV was characterized by the enrichment of BTV. Validation in an independent cohort confirmed BTV abundance in CLAD BAL fluid, serum, and lung tissues. BTV ORF1 protein (kV1) suppressed PBEC IFN-α and IFN-γ responses by preventing intranuclear STAT translocation. Co-culture of IAV or RSV in kV1-transfected PBECs significantly augmented replication of RSV and IAV and increased cellular injury. Likewise, in vivo transfection of kV1 increased replication and lung injury associated with IAV. CONCLUSIONS: Our work illuminates a novel virus-associated dysregulation of host interferon responses that promote lung injury associated with respiratory viral infections and, in part, explain differential host responses to viral infections after lung transplantation.
journal: American journal of respiratory cell and molecular biology

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the role of anelloviruses in modulating innate immune responses and their impact on susceptibility to respiratory viral-associated allograft injury after lung transplantation. Using shotgun metagenomics and qPCR, the research characterizes the lung virome in transplant recipients and identifies anelloviruses as dominant. Further, viral constructs from Betatorquevirus clade (BTV) and group 2 torque teno viruses were transfected in bronchial epithelial cells and mice models, revealing that BTV suppresses interferon responses. Co-culture experiments showed that BTV enhances replication and cellular injury of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and influenza A virus (IAV). The study concludes that anellovirus-mediated interferon dysregulation may contribute to lung injury associated with viral infections, potentially explaining differential host responses post-transplant. source_body_en: OBJECTIVES: To characterize the lung virome after lung transplantation and test whether anelloviruses modulate innate immune responses that influence susceptibility to respiratory viral-associated allograft injury. RATIONALE: The lung virome (LV) and its interactions with the host immune system leading to allograft injury after lung -transplantation are not well characterized. METHODS: Shotgun metagenomics and qPCR was performed on a multicenter BAL/serum cohort from lung transplant recipients (LTRs). Viral constructs from a Betatorquevirus clade (BTV) and group 2 torque teno viruses were transfected in primary bronchial epithelial cells (PBECs) or airways of C57BL/6 mice with and without exposure to influenza A virus (IAV) or respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: LV in LTRs was dominated by viruses from the family Anelloviridae. Chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD) LV was characterized by the enrichment of BTV. Validation in an independent cohort confirmed BTV abundance in CLAD BAL fluid, serum, and lung tissues. BTV ORF1 protein (kV1) suppressed PBEC IFN-α and IFN-γ responses by preventing intranuclear STAT translocation. Co-culture of IAV or RSV in kV1-transfected PBECs significantly augmented replication of RSV and IAV and increased cellular injury. Likewise, in vivo transfection of kV1 increased replication and lung injury associated with IAV. CONCLUSIONS: Our work illuminates a novel virus-associated dysregulation of host interferon responses that promote lung injury associated with respiratory viral infections and, in part, explain differential host responses to viral infections after lung transplantation.

title: Understanding RSV Resurgence Following COVID-19 in Ontario, Canada: Evaluating the Roles of Contact Patterns and Maternal Immunity
abstract: Background: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remains a leading cause of hospitalization in infancy, with severe outcomes influenced by both contact patterns and passive immunity. Non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) during the COVID-19 pandemic suppressed RSV circulation and reduced opportunities for maternal immune boosting, potentially altering protection among newborns. We evaluated whether incorporating time-varying maternal immunity improves the ability of an age-structured transmission model to predict post-pandemic RSV hospitalization patterns in infants. Methods: We analyzed population-based RSV hospitalizations among Ontario (Canada) infants (<1 year) from July 2, 2017 to June 25, 2024, using linked administrative databases. A deterministic compartmental model across seven age classes was calibrated against pre-pandemic data using Latin Hypercube Sampling. We compared a model incorporating time-varying contact rates alone against a specification that additionally included time-varying maternal immunity. Results: Both specifications accurately reproduced pre-pandemic seasonality and macro-level post-pandemic resurgence features. The constant maternal immunity model showed slightly better accuracy in capturing the 2021/22 peak compared to the time-varying maternal immunity specification. However, both qualitatively captured the continued near-absence of RSV and the observed peak was captured within the 95% credible intervals. While both models precisely captured the timing and overwhelming surge of admissions that occurred in 2022/23, they failed to capture the premature peak timing and magnitude in 2023/24. Conclusions: Incorporating time-varying maternal immunity did not improve model accuracy post-pandemic. While maternal protection is essential for evaluating infant immunizations, population-level contact shifts primarily shaped post-pandemic RSV seasonality, indicating that models must account for these mechanisms of RSV transmission dynamics.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the resurgence of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in Ontario, Canada, following the COVID-19 pandemic, focusing on the roles of contact patterns and maternal immunity. The research question centers on whether incorporating time-varying maternal immunity into an age-structured transmission model improves predictions of post-pandemic RSV hospitalization patterns in infants. The study design involves analyzing population-based RSV hospitalization data from 2017 to 2024 and comparing two models: one with time-varying contact rates and another with time-varying maternal immunity. The methods include deterministic compartmental modeling across seven age classes, calibrated using Latin Hypercube Sampling. The main results show that both models accurately reproduced pre-pandemic seasonality and macro-level post-pandemic resurgence features, with the constant maternal immunity model slightly better at capturing the 2021/22 peak. However, both models failed to capture the premature peak timing and magnitude in 2023/24. The authors interpret these findings to indicate that population-level contact shifts, rather than maternal immunity, primarily shaped post-pandemic RSV seasonality. This has implications for public health modeling and suggests that future studies should account for contact dynamics in predicting RSV outbreaks. The evidence is moderate in strength due to its reliance on abstract-only data and model outputs.

title: Editorial: Viral co-infections: challenges and therapeutic approaches
abstract: While influenza virus co-infections may be infrequent, combined bacterial or mycoplasma infections are much more commonplace and may give rise to increased symptomology and clinical outcomes. https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/microbiology/articles/10.3389/fmicb.2025.1719387/full carried out a retrospective cohort study utilising data from the Fourth Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University. Panton-Valentine Leukocidin (PVL)-positive, methicillin-susceptible ST22 strains were found to cause fatal outcomes in patients co-infected with influenza A or SARS-CoV-2, associated with severe leukopenia. Similarly, co-infection with Mycoplasma pneumoniae (Mp) is frequently documented. To examine this important but understudied coinfection, Ma et al. https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/microbiology/articles/10.3389/fmicb.2026.1787294/full? established a model in hamsters with H1NI (swine flu) which demonstrated that H1N1 infected animals which received a follow up Mp challenge exhibited significantly more severe histopathological lesions, higher pathogen loads, and dysregulated cytokine responses compared to other infection groups. A comprehensive review by Lei and colleagues discussed primary mechanisms of Influenza-mediated susceptibility to bacterial infection, with particular focus on epithelial barrier damage, immune cell dysfunction and the roles of specific immune cells, and their effector pathways in inducing hyperinflammatory responses aa well as treatment options. https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/microbiology/articles/10.3389/fmicb.2025.1673643/full . The authors emphasise that an in depth understanding of the interactions between the pathogens and the host will assist in the development of therapeutics for the prevention and treatment of post-influenza bacterial infection.Co-infections are a well, established fundamental area of research for Human Immunodeficiency virus (HIV) over many years. The importance of both genomic and immunological approaches to understanding HIV strain recombination, co-infections and vaccine efficacy in HIV infected individuals, are emphasised in 2 articles in this issue. A study by Ling and colleagues https://research-topic-management-app.frontiersin.org/manage/66895/manuscript shows that circulating recombinant forms (CRFs) play a critical role in the global transmission of HIV-1 with further second-generation recombinant viruses, derived from the original CRFs, continually emerging. Furthermore, these CRFs are associated with critical changes in co-receptor tropism. title_original: Editorial: Viral co-infections: challenges and therapeutic approaches

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on co-infections involving respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), particularly in the context of interactions with bacterial pathogens, other viruses, and immune responses. It examines the clinical implications, mechanisms, and therapeutic approaches for managing RSV co-infections, with an emphasis on RSV-A and RSV-B subtypes. The central question is how co-infections affect disease severity and immune responses in RSV-infected individuals.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is based on a combination of studies, including a retrospective cohort study conducted at the Fourth Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University. It also references a study on hamsters with H1N1 infection and a subsequent challenge with Mycoplasma pneumoniae, which demonstrated severe histopathological lesions and dysregulated cytokine responses. The review includes a systematic analysis of herbal agents in traditional Chinese medicine for treating Tianxing fever, which is closely related to dengue virus, and a review of monoclonal antibodies and small-molecule antivirals for RSV.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review highlights that co-infections with RSV and bacterial pathogens can significantly worsen clinical outcomes. It also underscores the importance of genomic surveillance, immunological studies, and experimental models in understanding pathogen interactions and immune responses. analysis.summary_en: This editorial explores the challenges and therapeutic approaches for managing co-infections involving respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), particularly in the context of interactions with bacterial pathogens and other viruses. It highlights the clinical significance of RSV co-infections, especially in high-risk populations, and discusses the role of genomic surveillance, immunological studies, and experimental models in understanding these interactions. The review also emphasizes the need for targeted therapies and the potential of traditional Chinese medicine in treating RSV-related conditions. Despite some progress, there remain unresolved questions about the specific mechanisms of RSV co-infections and the effectiveness of current interventions, underscoring the importance of continued research and surveillance.

elements_en.scope_and_question: The review focuses on co-infections involving respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), particularly in the context of interactions with bacterial pathogens, other viruses, and immune responses. It examines the clinical implications, mechanisms, and therapeutic approaches for managing RSV co-infections, with an emphasis on RSV-A and RSV-B subtypes. The central question is how co-infections affect disease severity and immune responses in RSV-infected individuals.
elements_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is based on a combination of studies, including a retrospective cohort study conducted at the Fourth Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University. It also references a study on hamsters with H1N1 infection and a subsequent challenge with Mycoplasma pneumoniae, which demonstrated severe histopathological lesions and dysregulated cytokine responses. The review includes a systematic analysis of herbal agents in traditional Chinese medicine for treating Tianxing fever, which is closely related to dengue virus, and a review of monoclonal antibodies and small-molecule antivirals for RSV.
elements_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review highlights that co-infections with RSV and bacterial pathogens can significantly worsen clinical outcomes. It also underscores the importance of genomic surveillance, immunological studies, and experimental models in understanding pathogen interactions and immune responses. The findings suggest that RSV co-infections are a critical area for research, particularly in high-risk populations and for developing targeted therapies.
elements_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that while co-infections are well-documented in some contexts, there is limited evidence on the specific mechanisms of RSV co-infections with other viruses. Additionally, the role of traditional Chinese medicine in RSV treatment remains understudied, and there is a need for more research on the interactions between RSV and other pathogens in different host populations.
elements_en.research_and_practice_implications: The review calls for further research into the mechanisms of RSV co-infections, especially with bacterial and other viral pathogens. It also emphasizes the need for improved surveillance, development of specific antiviral therapeutics, and exploration of alternative treatments such as traditional Chinese medicine. These efforts are crucial for managing RSV-related diseases and improving outcomes in vulnerable populations.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述的重点是涉及 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 的合并感染,特别是在与细菌病原体、其他病毒和 免疫应答 相互作用的情况下。它研究了管理 RSV 合并感染的临床意义、机制和治疗方法,重点是 RSV-A 和 RSV-B 亚型。核心问题是合并感染如何影响 RSV 感染者的疾病严重程度和 免疫应答。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该评价基于多项研究的结合,包括在苏州大学第四附属医院进行的回顾性 队列研究 研究。它还引用了一项针对感染 H1N1 的仓鼠以及随后受到肺炎支原体攻击的研究,该研究显示出严重的组织病理学病变和细胞因子反应失调。该综述包括对治疗与登革热病毒密切相关的天星热的中药中草药的系统分析,以及针对 RSV 的单克隆抗体和小分子 抗病毒药物 的综述。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述强调,RSV 和细菌病原体的共同感染会显着恶化临床结果。它还强调了 基因组监测、免疫学研究和实验模型在理解病原体相互作用和 免疫应答 方面的重要性。研究结果表明,RSV 合并感染是研究的一个关键领域,特别是在高危人群中,以及开发靶向治疗。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 审查指出,虽然在某些情况下混合感染有详细记录,但有关 RSV 与其他病毒混合感染的具体机制的证据有限。此外,中药在RSV 治疗中的作用仍有待研究,并且需要对不同宿主人群中RSV与其他病原体之间的相互作用进行更多研究。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该综述呼吁进一步研究 RSV 联合感染的机制,特别是细菌和其他病毒病原体的联合感染。它还强调需要改进监测、开发特定的抗病毒药物疗法以及探索替代治疗(例如中药)。这些努力对于管理 RSV 相关疾病和改善弱势群体的治疗效果至关重要。
