title_zh: 社论:病毒合并感染:挑战和治疗方法
source_body_en: While influenza virus co-infections may be infrequent, combined bacterial or mycoplasma infections are much more commonplace and may give rise to increased symptomology and clinical outcomes. https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/microbiology/articles/10.3389/fmicb.2025.1719387/full carried out a retrospective cohort study utilising data from the Fourth Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University. Panton-Valentine Leukocidin (PVL)-positive, methicillin-susceptible ST22 strains were found to cause fatal outcomes in patients co-infected with influenza A or SARS-CoV-2, associated with severe leukopenia. Similarly, co-infection with Mycoplasma pneumoniae (Mp) is frequently documented. To examine this important but understudied coinfection, Ma et al. https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/microbiology/articles/10.3389/fmicb.2026.1787294/full? established a model in hamsters with H1NI (swine flu) which demonstrated that H1N1 infected animals which received a follow up Mp challenge exhibited significantly more severe histopathological lesions, higher pathogen loads, and dysregulated cytokine responses compared to other infection groups. A comprehensive review by Lei and colleagues discussed primary mechanisms of Influenza-mediated susceptibility to bacterial infection, with particular focus on epithelial barrier damage, immune cell dysfunction and the roles of specific immune cells, and their effector pathways in inducing hyperinflammatory responses aa well as treatment options. https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/microbiology/articles/10.3389/fmicb.2025.1673643/full . The authors emphasise that an in depth understanding of the interactions between the pathogens and the host will assist in the development of therapeutics for the prevention and treatment of post-influenza bacterial infection.Co-infections are a well, established fundamental area of research for Human Immunodeficiency virus (HIV) over many years. The importance of both genomic and immunological approaches to understanding HIV strain recombination, co-infections and vaccine efficacy in HIV infected individuals, are emphasised in 2 articles in this issue. A study by Ling and colleagues https://research-topic-management-app.frontiersin.org/manage/66895/manuscript shows that circulating recombinant forms (CRFs) play a critical role in the global transmission of HIV-1 with further second-generation recombinant viruses, derived from the original CRFs, continually emerging. Furthermore, these CRFs are associated with critical changes in co-receptor tropism. This study strongly supports the importance of sustained genomic surveillance for prevention strategies. https://research-topic-management-app.frontiersin.org/manage/66895/manuscript examined whether there was cross-protection from the humoral immune response of immunocompromised populations of people living with HIV to both infection with existing covid sub-lineages and subsequent covid vaccines. The study highlighted the crucial need for regular monitoring of immune responses to new covid vaccines targeting emerging variants in this category of individuals. Another immunologically challenged group are patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) receiving maintenance haemodialysis who are predisposed to anaemia. A study by Özsoy and colleagues https://research-topic-management-app.frontiersin.org/manage/66895/manuscript raised and examined concerns that prior B19V Parvovirus infection may contribute to anaemia severity or resistance to erythropoiesisstimulating agents (ESAs).In addition to study of co-infections in human populations, research on co-infection in animal species is an important area for veterinary medicine, understanding and utilising natural virus models and for surveillance and protection against zoonotic diseases. Bats are natural reservoirs for many viruses but with information on hepatitis viruses limited. https://research-topic-management-app.frontiersin.org/manage/66895/manuscript examined the diversity and evolution of bat hepatitis B viruses (BtHBVs) and their co-infection with bat hepatitis D virus (BtHDV) in bats in China and showed that they are natural hosts for both viruses.Advances in genomic surveillance, immunological studies, and experimental models reveal how pathogen interactions, immune responses, and infection timing shape disease progression. In addition, there remains an urgent need for specific antiviral therapeutics, as exemplified by 3 papers in this issue. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) is of interest to identify and target new substances not currently used for conventional pharmaceutical treatments. A systematic review by Zeng and colleagues https://research-topic-management-app.frontiersin.org/manage/66895/manuscript examined herbal agents documented in classical TCM texts for the treatment of Tianxing fever (closely related to dengue virus) with the aim of guiding clinical practice and modern drug development for dengue prevention and treatment. A further review by Liu et al. https://research-topic-management-app.frontiersin.org/manage/66895/manuscript comprehensively summarises the current status of Respiratory Syncytial Virus monoclonal antibodies and small-molecule antivirals. A third experimental study by Liang and team https://research-topic-management-app.frontiersin.org/manage/66895/manuscript examined an alternative therapeutic approach to vaccines for porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus (PRRSV). Mogroside V, a triterpenoid compound (derived from Siraitia grosvenorii) which has previously been shown to exhibit diverse biological activities including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anti-cancer properties, with the capacity to scavenge free radicals and mitigate oxidative stress was assessed in vitro. This compound not only directly inhibited PRRSV replication but also significantly upregulated the gene expression of immunomodulatory cytokines.• Co-infections are generally uncommon but can significantly worsen disease severity, particularly in viral-bacterial combinations or high-risk populations.• Pathogen interactions and infection order play a critical role in clinical outcomes and immune responses.• Ongoing surveillance, vaccination strategies, and development of targeted therapies are essential to address the evolving complexity of co-infections.Overall, the research underscores the need for continued monitoring, integrated prevention strategies, and improved therapeutic approaches to manage complex co-infections.

是一种三萜化合物(源自罗汉果),此前已被证明具有多种生物活性,包括抗氧化、抗炎和抗癌特性,并具有清除自由基和减轻氧化应激的能力,并在体外进行了评估。该化合物不仅直接抑制 PRRSV 复制,而且显着上调免疫调节细胞因子的基因表达。• 合并感染通常不常见,但会显着恶化疾病严重程度,特别是在病毒-细菌组合或高危人群中。• 病原体相互作用和感染顺序在临床结果和 免疫应答 中发挥着关键作用。• 持续的 analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该评价基于多项研究的结合,包括在苏州大学第四附属医院进行的回顾性 队列研究 研究。它还引用了一项针对感染 H1N1 的仓鼠以及随后受到肺炎支原体攻击的研究,该研究显示出严重的组织病理学病变和细胞因子反应失调。该综述包括对治疗与登革热病毒密切相关的天星热的中药中草药的系统分析,以及针对 RSV 的单克隆抗体和小分子 抗病毒药物 的综述。

title: Anticipating the Next Week: Calibrated Prediction of State-Level Respiratory Illness Escalation from Public Surveillance Data
abstract: Abstract Background Respiratory-virus surveillance teams need early, credible, and low-burden signals of worsening activity. Current dashboards describe recent activity well, but they are less directly designed to rank jurisdictions that are already at moderate influenza-like illness (ILI) activity and may cross into high activity in the next reporting week. Methods We conducted a retrospective state-week prediction study using public U.S. outpatient ILI surveillance from CDC ILINet, accessed through Delphi Epidata FluView, and regional RSV and SARS-CoV-2 nucleic-acid test positivity from CDC NREVSS. The target was transition from moderate state-specific ILI activity at week t to high activity at week t + 1. State-specific thresholds, preprocessing, hyperparameter tuning, probability calibration, and alert-threshold selection were estimated from development data only. Candidate models were selected by rolling-origin cross-validation and evaluated once on a later chronological holdout. Held-out uncertainty was quantified with state-cluster bootstrap confidence intervals. Results The modelling cohort contained 4,232 moderate state-weeks from 51 jurisdictions. The holdout period contained 943 state-weeks and 127 moderate-to-high transitions. The selected calibrated logistic regression model achieved AUROC 0.877, average precision 0.529, F1 0.594, precision 0.589, recall 0.598, and specificity 0.935. It issued 129 alerts and identified 76 of 127 transitions, whereas an alert-all-moderate baseline identified all transitions but required 943 alerts. The most useful signals were proximity to the state-specific high-activity threshold, seasonal timing, recent ILI history, reporting volume, and lagged RSV/SARS-CoV-2 positivity. Conclusions A simple calibrated surveillance model reduced alert burden while retaining most short-horizon escalations. The study should be interpreted as a transparent benchmark for respiratory-surveillance triage research, not as a deployed public health decision rule. Its contribution is an evaluation framework that combines temporal cross-validation, independent temporal testing, bootstrap uncertainty, calibration, threshold analysis, and explicit reporting that true external validation remains unavailable.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop a low-burden surveillance model to predict respiratory illness escalation at the state level. Using public U.S. data from CDC ILINet and NREVSS, the model focused on transitions from moderate to high influenza-like illness (ILI) activity. The calibrated logistic regression model achieved moderate performance metrics, including an AUROC of 0.877 and F1 score of 0.594, while significantly reducing the number of alerts needed compared to a baseline approach. The model's most useful signals included proximity to high-activity thresholds, seasonal timing, and lagged RSV/SARS-CoV-2 positivity. The study emphasizes the importance of calibrated models in improving surveillance efficiency but notes that true external validation remains unavailable. These findings offer a framework for future research in respiratory virus surveillance and triage systems.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 呼吸道病毒 监测 团队需要早期、可靠且低负担的活动恶化信号。目前的仪表板很好地描述了近期的活动,但它们的设计不太直接地对已经处于中度流感样疾病 (ILI) 活动的辖区进行排名,并且可能在下一个报告周进入高活动度。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们利用来自 CDC ILINEt 的美国公立门诊 ILI 监测(通过 Delphi Epidata FluView 访问)以及来自 CDC NREVSS 的区域 RSV 和 SARS-CoV-2 核酸检测阳性结果,进行了一项回顾性州周预测研究。目标是从 t 周的中度州特定 ILI 活动过渡到 t + 1 周的高活动。
elements_zh.methods: 仅根据开发数据估计特定于状态的阈值、预处理、超参数调整、概率校准和警报阈值选择。通过滚动源交叉验证来选择候选模型,并在稍后按时间顺序保留时进行一次评估。保留的不确定性通过状态簇引导置信区间进行量化。
elements_zh.main_results: 建模 队列研究 包含来自 51 个司法管辖区的 4,232 个中等州周。坚持期包含 943 个状态周和 127 个中度到高度的转换。所选校准逻辑回归模型的 AUROC 0.877、平均精度 0.529、F1 0.594、精度 0.589、召回率 0.598 和特异性 0.935。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 简单的校准 监测 模型减轻了警报负担,同时保留了大多数短期升级。最有用的信号是接近州特定的高活动阈值、季节性时间、近期流感样病例历史、报告量以及滞后的 RSV/SARS-CoV-2 阳性率。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该研究为呼吸道 监测 分类研究提供了透明的基准,可以为开发更有效的呼吸道病毒 监测 系统提供信息。它强调了校准模型在减轻警报负担、同时保持预测活动升级的准确性方面的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究应被解释为呼吸系统 监测 分类研究的透明基准,而不是部署的公共卫生决策规则。它的贡献是一个评估框架,结合了时间交叉验证、独立时间测试、引导不确定性、校准、阈值分析和明确报告真正的外部验证仍然不可用。

title: Effectiveness of RSV Prevention Strategies in US Infants: 2024-2025.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: In 2023, 2 products, a long-acting monoclonal antibody (nirsevimab) and maternal respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccination, were recommended in the United States to prevent severe RSV disease among infants in their first RSV season. Low uptake during the 2023 to 2024 RSV season limited effectiveness estimates. We estimated nirsevimab and maternal RSV vaccine effectiveness against RSV-associated emergency department (ED) encounters and hospitalization among US infants during the 2024 to 2025 RSV season, when uptake was higher. METHODS: We used electronic health record data from 5 health care systems in test-negative analyses of ED encounters and hospitalizations with RSV-like illness during October 1, 2024 to March 31, 2025, among infants in their first RSV season. Nirsevimab and maternal RSV vaccine effectiveness were estimated by comparing RSV-positive with RSV-negative encounters with respect to immunization status in separate logistic regression models adjusted for age, race and ethnicity, sex, calendar day, and geographic region. RESULTS: Among 3531 ED encounters and 470 hospitalizations included in the nirsevimab analyses, nirsevimab effectiveness against RSV-associated ED encounters and hospitalization was 62% (95% CI: 54-68) and 77% (95% CI: 61-87), respectively. Among 810 ED encounters and 187 hospitalizations included in the maternal RSV vaccine analyses, vaccine effectiveness against RSV-associated ED encounters and hospitalization was 49% (95% CI: 26-65) and 82% (95% CI: 54-93), respectively. CONCLUSION: Nirsevimab and maternal RSV vaccination were effective against RSV-associated ED encounters and hospitalization among infants in their first RSV season. As uptake increases and additional products are recommended, monitoring infant RSV immunization effectiveness remains important.

analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted using electronic health record data from 5 healthcare systems during the 2024 to 2025 RSV season, focusing on infants in their first RSV season. Logistic regression models were used, adjusting for age, race and ethnicity, sex, calendar day, and geographic region.
analysis.main_results: Nirsevimab effectiveness against RSV-associated ED encounters was 62% (95% CI: 54-68), and against hospitalization was 77% (95% CI: 61-87). Maternal RSV vaccine effectiveness against ED encounters was 49% (95% CI: 26-65), and against hospitalization was 82% (95% CI: 54-93).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these results as evidence of the effectiveness of both nirsevimab and maternal RSV vaccination in preventing RSV-associated ED encounters and hospitalizations among infants in their first RSV season, with nirsevimab showing higher effectiveness against ED encounters compared to the maternal vaccine.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings inform the importance of monitoring infant RSV immunization effectiveness as uptake increases and additional products are recommended, providing critical data for public health strategies and clinical decision-making.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on electronic health record data, which may have biases or missing information. However, the evidence is strong given the use of test-negative analyses and adjustment for key demographic and temporal factors, supporting a moderate confidence assessment.

The authors concluded that both interventions are effective, emphasizing the need for ongoing monitoring as uptake increases. The study's reliance on electronic health records introduces potential biases, but the methods and results provide a moderate level of confidence in the effectiveness of these RSV prevention strategies.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)预防策略的有效性,具体包括尼塞韦单抗(尼塞韦单抗)和孕妇呼吸道合胞病毒疫苗(maternal RSV 疫苗),以减少美国婴儿在首个RSV流行季期间因RSV相关急诊就诊和住院的发生率。背景部分强调,这两种产品于2023年被推荐使用,但在2023至2024流行季期间的采用率有限,影响了对其有效性的评估能力。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用 2024 年至 2025 年 RSV 季节期间来自 5 个医疗保健系统的电子健康记录数据进行,重点关注第一个 RSV 季节的婴儿。该人群包括 3531 例急诊科就诊病例和 470 例因 RSV 类疾病住院的病例,并对 尼塞韦单抗 和孕产妇 RSV 疫苗 有效性进行了单独分析。
elements_zh.methods: 通过对急诊科就诊和因 RSV 样疾病住院治疗的测试阴性分析,根据免疫状态比较 RSV 阳性和 RSV 阴性病例来评估有效性。使用逻辑回归模型,调整年龄、种族和民族、性别、日历日和地理区域。
elements_zh.main_results: 尼塞韦单抗 对 RSV 相关 ED 患者的有效率为 62% (95% CI: 54-68),对住院治疗的有效率为 77% (95% CI: 61-87)。母亲 RSV 疫苗 对抗 ED 的有效性为 49% (95% CI: 26-65),对抗住院治疗的有效性为 82% (95% CI: 54-93)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些结果解释为尼塞韦单抗和母体RSV 疫苗接种在预防第一个RSV季节婴儿中与RSV相关的ED遭遇和住院治疗方面的有效性的证据,与母体疫苗相比,尼塞韦单抗在预防ED遭遇方面表现出更高的有效性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,随着吸收率的增加和推荐其他产品,监测婴儿 RSV 免疫效果的重要性,为公共卫生策略和临床决策提供关键数据。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受限于对电子健康记录数据的依赖,可能存在偏倚或缺失信息。然而,由于采用了检测阴性分析并针对关键人口统计学和时间因素进行了调整,证据强度较高,支持中等置信度评估。

abstract_zh: 目标:2023年,美国推荐长效单克隆抗体(尼塞韦单抗)和母体呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)疫苗接种这2种产品在婴儿第一个RSV季节预防严重RSV疾病。2023 年至 2024 年 RSV 季节期间使用率较低,限制了有效性估计。我们估计了 2024 年至 2025 年 RSV 季节期间,尼塞韦单抗 和母体 RSV 疫苗 对美国婴儿与 RSV 相关的急诊室 (ED) 接触和住院治疗的有效性,当时的摄入量较高。方法:我们使用来自 5 个医疗保健系统的电子健康记录数据,对 2024 年 10 月 1 日至 2025 年 3 月 31 日期间,在第一个 RSV 季节的婴儿中,对 ED 遭遇和因 RSV 样疾病住院的情况进行测试阴性分析。尼塞韦单抗 和母亲 RSV 疫苗 的有效性是通过比较 RSV 阳性和 RSV 阴性的情况来估计的,这些情况是在单独的逻辑回归模型中针对年龄、种族和民族、性别、日历日和地理区域进行调整后的免疫状态。结果:在 尼塞韦单抗 分析中纳入的 3531 例急诊就诊和 470 例住院治疗中,尼塞韦单抗 针对 RSV 相关急诊就诊和住院的有效性分别为 62%(95% CI:54-68)和 77%(95% CI:61-87)。在母体 RSV 疫苗 分析中纳入的 810 例 ED 就诊和 187 例住院治疗中,疫苗 针对 RSV 相关 ED 就诊和住院的有效性分别为 49% (95% CI: 26-65) 和 82% (95% CI: 54-93)。结论:尼塞韦单抗 和母体 RSV 疫苗接种 对于第一个 RSV 季节婴儿中与 RSV 相关的 ED 事件和住院治疗有效。随着吸收量的增加和其他产品的推荐,监测婴儿 RSV 免疫效果仍然很重要。

title: Anakinra in Severe RSV-Associated Autoinflammatory Encephalopathy With Delayed ADEM-Like Changes.
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)-associated encephalopathy is an uncommon but potentially devastating complication in children. Increasing evidence suggests that infection-triggered neuroinflammation rather than direct viral invasion underlies neurologic injury in a subset of patients. We describe 2 previously healthy, unrelated children who developed rapidly progressive encephalopathy after RSV infection. Initial brain magnetic resonance imaging scan results were normal, but follow-up imaging results showed multifocal white matter lesions consistent with an acute disseminated encephalomyelitis-like pattern. Both patients were given refractory to high-dose corticosteroids, intravenous immunoglobulin, and interleukin (IL)-6 blockade. Markedly elevated serum IL-1β levels were documented in one patient. Treatment with the IL-1 receptor antagonist, anakinra, was temporally associated with neurologic and radiologic recovery in both cases. These observations suggest that an IL-1-driven autoinflammatory phenotype may contribute to disease severity in selected children with RSV-associated encephalopathy and highlight the importance of repeat neuroimaging and consideration of targeted immunomodulation in refractory cases.

elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据仅限于两个 病例报告,这排除了概括性并且无法建立因果关系。由于缺乏对照、样本量小以及对时间关联的依赖,证据的强度较低。

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究为一份病例报告,描述了两名此前健康且无血缘关系的儿童在感染RSV后出现快速进展性脑病。两名患者对包括高剂量皮质类固醇、静脉免疫球蛋白及白细胞介素(IL)-6阻断剂在内的标准治疗均无反应。
analysis_zh.methods: 作者记录了一名患者血清 IL-1β 水平显着升高,并给予 IL-1 受体拮抗剂阿那白滞素作为靶向免疫调节剂。治疗 后监测神经系统和放射学恢复情况。
analysis_zh.main_results: 最初的脑磁共振成像扫描结果正常,但后续成像显示多灶性白质病变,与急性播散性脑脊髓炎样模式一致。在这两种情况下,治疗 联合阿那白滞素与神经系统和放射学恢复均暂时相关。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为,IL-1 驱动的自身炎症表型可能会导致特定患有 RSV 相关脑病的儿童的疾病严重程度。他们强调了重复神经影像学检查的重要性以及在难治性病例中考虑靶向免疫调节的重要性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些观察结果表明,用阿那白滞素阻断 IL-1 可能是患有严重、难治性 RSV 相关脑病的儿童的一种治疗选择。研究结果强调需要警惕监测迟发性神经炎症并发症。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据仅限于两个 病例报告,这排除了概括性并且无法建立因果关系。由于缺乏对照、样本量小以及对时间关联的依赖,证据的强度较低。

title: Perspectives on an Intervention to Increase Confidence in Newborn RSV Immunoprophylaxis.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) immunoprophylaxis is efficacious, yet uptake is low in comparison with other recommended newborn interventions. We aimed to identify barriers to and enablers of implementation of an intervention in the well newborn unit to increase parental confidence in newborn RSV immunoprophylaxis. PATIENTS AND METHODS: We conducted individual, semi-structured interviews of purposively sampled clinicians and parents at an urban, quaternary-care hospital well newborn unit between August 13, 2025, and October 22, 2025. Interviews elicited clinicians' and parents' perceptions of RSV immunoprophylaxis, the counseling process, barriers and facilitators, and their perspectives on the design and implementation of an intervention to increase parental confidence. Using both deductive and inductive approaches, 4 investigators independently coded the first 2 transcripts in each stakeholder group to identify themes. Two investigators then applied codes to the remaining transcripts, resolving discrepancies by consensus. RESULTS: We interviewed 18 clinicians (5 hospitalists, 3 general pediatricians, 3 obstetricians, 7 nurses/nurse managers) and 24 parents. We identified several themes related to an intervention to increase parental confidence, including barriers and facilitators: (1) trust and mistrust of information; (2) differentiation of RSV immunoprophylaxis from a vaccine; and (3) value of providing both data and personal experiences. We also identified themes related to implementation: (1) support for a tool to augment, but not replace, clinician counseling; (2) use of visuals; (3) accessibility for parents of varying health literacy and languages; and (4) importance of timing. CONCLUSIONS: The identified themes can inform the design and implementation of an intervention to increase parental confidence in newborn RSV immunoprophylaxis.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on understanding barriers and enablers to implementing an intervention in the well newborn unit to increase parental confidence in newborn RSV immunoprophylaxis. The target is respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), specifically RSV-A and RSV-B, with the central question being how to improve parental confidence in RSV immunoprophylaxis for newborns.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is based on individual, semi-structured interviews conducted with purposively sampled clinicians and parents at an urban, quaternary-care hospital well newborn unit between August 13, 2025, and October 22, 2025. Four investigators independently coded the first 2 transcripts in each stakeholder group using deductive and inductive approaches to identify themes, and then two investigators applied the codes to the remaining transcripts, resolving discrepancies by consensus.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review identified several themes related to increasing parental confidence in newborn RSV immunoprophylaxis, including trust and mistrust of information, differentiation of RSV immunoprophylaxis from a vaccine, and the value of providing both data and personal experiences. It also highlighted implementation themes such as support for a tool to augment, but not replace, clinician counseling, use of visuals, accessibility for parents of varying health literacy and languages, and the importance of timing.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not report controversies or evidence gaps directly. However, it notes that the findings are based on qualitative interviews, which may not capture the full scope of implementation challenges or provide quantitative data on the effectiveness of the proposed intervention.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The identified themes can inform the design and implementation of an intervention to increase parental confidence in newborn RSV immunoprophylaxis. This includes developing tools that support clinician counseling, incorporating visuals, ensuring accessibility for diverse populations, and timing the intervention appropriately.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores barriers and enablers to increasing parental confidence in newborn RSV immunoprophylaxis through qualitative interviews with clinicians and parents. The study identifies key themes such as trust in information, distinguishing RSV immunoprophylaxis from vaccines, and the importance of combining data with personal experiences. Implementation considerations include supporting clinician counseling with tools, using visuals, ensuring accessibility for diverse populations, and timing the intervention effectively. The findings suggest that these themes can guide the development of targeted interventions to improve uptake of RSV immunoprophylaxis in newborns.

elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该评价基于2025年8月13日至2025年10月22日期间对城市四级护理医院新生儿病房有目的地抽样的临床医生和家长进行的个人、半结构化访谈。四名研究人员使用演绎和归纳方法对每个利益相关者组中的前2份记录进行独立编码,以确定主题,然后两名研究人员将代码应用于其余记录,通过协商一致解决差异。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述识别出多个与提升新生儿呼吸道合胞病毒免疫预防信心相关的主题,包括对信息的信任与不信任、呼吸道合胞病毒免疫预防与抗病毒药物的区分,以及提供数据与个人经验的价值。综述还强调了实施层面的主题,如支持使用工具辅助(但不替代)临床医师咨询、视觉化呈现、满足不同健康素养水平及语言背景父母的可及性,以及时机选择的重要性。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该审查不直接报告争议或证据差距。然而,它指出,调查结果基于定性访谈,可能无法捕捉实施挑战的全部范围或提供有关拟议干预措施有效性的定量数据。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 确定的主题可以为干预措施的设计和实施提供信息,以提高父母对新生儿 RSV 免疫预防的信心。这包括开发支持临床医生咨询的工具、纳入视觉效果、确保不同人群的可及性以及适当地安排干预时间。

abstract_zh: 目标:呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 免疫预防是有效的,但与其他推荐的新生儿干预措施相比,采用率较低。我们的目的是确定在健康新生儿病房实施干预措施的障碍和推动因素,以提高家长对新生儿 RSV 免疫预防的信心。患者和方法:我们于 2025 年 8 月 13 日至 2025 年 10 月 22 日期间,对城市四级护理医院新生儿病房有目的地抽样的临床医生和家长进行了单独的半结构化访谈。访谈引出了临床医生和家长对 RSV 免疫预防、咨询过程、障碍和促进因素的看法,以及他们对设计和实施干预措施的看法。增加父母的信心。4 位研究人员使用演绎和归纳方法独立编码每个利益相关者组中的前 2 个记录,以确定主题。然后,两名研究人员将代码应用于剩余的转录本,通过协商一致解决了差异。结果:我们采访了 18 名临床医生(5 名住院医生、3 名普通儿科医生、3 名产科医生、7 名护士/护士长)和 24 名家长。我们确定了与增强父母信心的干预相关的几个主题,包括障碍和促进因素:(1)对信息的信任和不信任;(2) RSV免疫预防与疫苗的区别;(3) 提供数据和个人经验的价值。我们还确定了与实施相关的主题:(1) 支持一种工具来增强而不是取代临床医生咨询;(2) 视觉效果的使用;(3) 不同健康素养和语言的父母均可获得帮助;(4)时机的重要性。结论:确定的主题可以为干预措施的设计和实施提供信息,以提高父母对新生儿 RSV 免疫预防的信心。

analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该评价基于2025年8月13日至2025年10月22日期间对城市四级护理医院新生儿病房有目的地抽样的临床医生和家长进行的个人、半结构化访谈。四名研究人员使用演绎和归纳方法对每个利益相关者组中的前2份记录进行独立编码,以确定主题,然后两名研究人员将代码应用于其余记录,通过协商一致解决差异。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述识别出多个与提升新生儿呼吸道合胞病毒免疫预防信心相关的主题,包括对信息的信任与不信任、呼吸道合胞病毒免疫预防与抗病毒药物的区分,以及提供数据与个人经验的价值。综述还强调了实施层面的主题,如支持使用工具辅助(但不替代)临床医师咨询、视觉化呈现、满足不同健康素养水平及语言背景父母的可及性,以及时机选择的重要性。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该审查不直接报告争议或证据差距。然而,它指出,调查结果基于定性访谈,可能无法捕捉实施挑战的全部范围或提供有关拟议干预措施有效性的定量数据。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 确定的主题可以为干预措施的设计和实施提供信息,以提高父母对新生儿 RSV 免疫预防的信心。这包括开发支持临床医生咨询的工具、纳入视觉效果、确保不同人群的可及性以及适当地安排干预时间。

title: Impact of Human Adenovirus Co-detection on Disease Severity in Children with Medically Attended Acute Respiratory Infections
abstract: Abstract Background Human Adenovirus (HAdV) is frequently identified as a cause of acute respiratory infections (ARIs) in children and often co-detected with other common respiratory viruses. However, the effect of co-detection on disease severity is not well understood. This study aimed to describe the spectrum and frequency of other respiratory viruses co-detected with HAdV and define the impact of co-detection on HAdV disease severity. Methods Children admitted to the hospital or seen in the emergency department with fever and/or respiratory symptoms <14 days duration were enrolled at 7 sites across the US, from 12/01/2016 through 08/31/2023, as part of the CDC-sponsored New Vaccine Surveillance Network (NVSN). Respiratory specimens were systematically obtained and tested for HAdV and other common viral etiologies of ARI. Demographics, clinical characteristics, and disease severity (hospitalization and in-hospital oxygen use) were compared among children with HAdV single detection, HAdV co-detection with other respiratory viral pathogens, and single detection of a non-HAdV virus. Results Of 68,004 children enrolled with a respiratory specimen tested, 4,292 (6.3%) were positive for HAdV; 1,779 (41.4%) of these were HAdV single detections. Human rhinovirus/enterovirus (HRV/EV) (43.1%), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) (14.7%), and parainfluenza virus (PIV) (7.6%) were the most common viruses co-detected with HAdV and selected for further analysis. HAdV co-detection with these 3 viruses was associated with increased odds of hospitalization and in-hospital oxygen use when compared to HAdV single detection. However, the odds of hospitalization and in-hospital oxygen use with HRV/EV, RSV, and PIV single detection were also increased compared to HAdV single detection. Conclusion HAdV co-detection with HRV/EV, RSV, or PIV was associated with increased disease severity when compared to HAdV single detection. However, HRV/EV, RSV, and PIV single detections were also associated with increased severity in comparison to HAdV single detection with these pathogens. Additionally, the increased odds of severe disease seen in HRV/EV, RSV, and PIV single detections was often greater than the increase seen with HAdV co-detection with HRV/EV, RSV, or PIV. This could suggest that the overall severity of these ARIs is being driven primarily by the co-detected viruses, HRV/EV, RSV, and PIV. These results could help guide interpretation of viral testing by clinicians, when multiple viruses are detected. Further research involving asymptomatic and mild HAdV ARI cases, as well as longitudinal studies to determine timing of co-infections, are needed to fully understand the role of HAdV in pediatric ARI of mixed viral etiology.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the impact of co-detection of Human Adenovirus (HAdV) with other respiratory viruses on disease severity in children with acute respiratory infections (ARIs). The research aimed to understand how the presence of multiple viruses affects the severity of HAdV infections. The study was conducted across 7 US sites from 2016 to 2023, involving 68,004 children. HAdV was detected in 6.3% of participants, with 41.4% of these cases being single detections. The most common co-detected viruses were human rhinovirus/enterovirus (HRV/EV), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and parainfluenza virus (PIV). The results showed that co-detection of HAdV with HRV/EV, RSV, or PIV was associated with increased odds of hospitalization and in-hospital oxygen use compared to HAdV single detection. However, the severity of HRV/EV, RSV, and PIV single detections was often greater than that of HAdV co-detection. The findings suggest that the overall severity of ARIs may be driven more by the co-detected viruses than by HAdV itself. These results could inform clinical interpretation of viral testing in cases of multiple virus detection. The study's evidence strength is moderate due to its observational nature and lack of causality.

title_zh: 人类腺病毒联合检测对急性呼吸道感染儿童疾病严重程度的影响
source_body_en: Abstract Background Human Adenovirus (HAdV) is frequently identified as a cause of acute respiratory infections (ARIs) in children and often co-detected with other common respiratory viruses. However, the effect of co-detection on disease severity is not well understood. This study aimed to describe the spectrum and frequency of other respiratory viruses co-detected with HAdV and define the impact of co-detection on HAdV disease severity. Methods Children admitted to the hospital or seen in the emergency department with fever and/or respiratory symptoms <14 days duration were enrolled at 7 sites across the US, from 12/01/2016 through 08/31/2023, as part of the CDC-sponsored New Vaccine Surveillance Network (NVSN). Respiratory specimens were systematically obtained and tested for HAdV and other common viral etiologies of ARI. Demographics, clinical characteristics, and disease severity (hospitalization and in-hospital oxygen use) were compared among children with HAdV single detection, HAdV co-detection with other respiratory viral pathogens, and single detection of a non-HAdV virus. Results Of 68,004 children enrolled with a respiratory specimen tested, 4,292 (6.3%) were positive for HAdV; 1,779 (41.4%) of these were HAdV single detections. Human rhinovirus/enterovirus (HRV/EV) (43.1%), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) (14.7%), and parainfluenza virus (PIV) (7.6%) were the most common viruses co-detected with HAdV and selected for further analysis. HAdV co-detection with these 3 viruses was associated with increased odds of hospitalization and in-hospital oxygen use when compared to HAdV single detection. However, the odds of hospitalization and in-hospital oxygen use with HRV/EV, RSV, and PIV single detection were also increased compared to HAdV single detection. Conclusion HAdV co-detection with HRV/EV, RSV, or PIV was associated with increased disease severity when compared to HAdV single detection. However, HRV/EV, RSV, and PIV single detections were also associated with increased severity in comparison to HAdV single detection with these pathogens. Additionally, the increased odds of severe disease seen in HRV/EV, RSV, and PIV single detections was often greater than the increase seen with HAdV co-detection with HRV/EV, RSV, or PIV. This could suggest that the overall severity of these ARIs is being driven primarily by the co-detected viruses, HRV/EV, RSV, and PIV. These results could help guide interpretation of viral testing by clinicians, when multiple viruses are detected. Further research involving asymptomatic and mild HAdV ARI cases, as well as longitudinal studies to determine timing of co-infections, are needed to fully understand the role of HAdV in pediatric ARI of mixed viral etiology.

title: Letter to the Editor on: "Nosocomial Respiratory Virus Infections in Hematologic Malignancies: Risk Factors for Progression to Lower Respiratory Tract Infection".
abstract: This Correspondence responds to Oh and colleagues' study on nosocomial respiratory virus infections in hematologic malignancies and risk factors for progression to lower respiratory tract infection. We raise three methodological concerns: (1) the landmark analysis used to evaluate URTI-stage ribavirin therapy excludes patients who progressed or died before landmark time points, introducing selection bias by conditioning on a collider; (2) antiviral therapy analyses are severely underpowered (only 15 PIV and 9 RSV treated patients), with wide confidence intervals precluding definitive conclusions and substantial Type II error risk; and (3) combining glucocorticoid exposures from different indications (short-course pulse vs. prolonged therapy) may mask heterogeneous effects on immune function and viral progression. We commend the authors' risk stratification framework while urging cautious interpretation of antiviral efficacy data and recommending future prospective studies with adequate sample sizes and refined corticosteroid characterization.

elements_zh.methods: 作者强调了原始研究中的方法学问题,包括使用 URTI 阶段利巴韦林治疗的标志性分析、动力不足的 抗病毒药物 治疗分析以及异质糖皮质激素暴露分类。
elements_zh.main_results: 该信函报告称,抗病毒药物 治疗分析的效力严重不足,只有 15 名副流感病毒 (PIV) 和 9 名 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 治疗的患者,导致置信区间过宽,并且存在 II 型错误的巨大风险。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者赞扬了原始研究的风险分层框架,但由于方法学的限制,敦促谨慎解释 抗病毒药物 疗效数据,建议未来进行具有足够样本量的前瞻性研究。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调需要改进研究设计,以准确评估 抗病毒药物 的疗效以及呼吸道病毒感染免疫功能低下患者病情进展的危险因素。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据强度受到原始研究中方法学缺陷的限制,包括标志性分析的选择偏差、动力不足的 抗病毒药物 治疗分析以及异质性糖皮质激素暴露分类,需要进行低置信度评估。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The letter critiques a prior study on nosocomial respiratory virus infections in patients with hematologic malignancies, focusing on methodological limitations that may affect the interpretation of antiviral efficacy and risk factors for progression to lower respiratory tract infection.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The original study by Oh and colleagues evaluated nosocomial respiratory virus infections in patients with hematologic malignancies, including those with upper respiratory tract infections (URTI) and risk factors for progression to lower respiratory tract infection.
analysis_en.methods: The authors highlight methodological concerns in the original study, including the use of a landmark analysis for URTI-stage ribavirin therapy, underpowered antiviral therapy analyses, and heterogeneous glucocorticoid exposure categorization.
analysis_en.main_results: The letter reports that antiviral therapy analyses were severely underpowered, with only 15 parainfluenza virus (PIV) and 9 respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) treated patients, leading to wide confidence intervals and substantial risk of Type II error.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors commend the risk stratification framework of the original study but urge cautious interpretation of antiviral efficacy data due to methodological limitations, recommending future prospective studies with adequate sample sizes.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings emphasize the need for improved study designs to accurately assess antiviral efficacy and risk factors for progression in immunocompromised patients with respiratory virus infections.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is limited by methodological flaws in the original study, including selection bias from landmark analysis, underpowered antiviral therapy analyses, and heterogeneous glucocorticoid exposure categorization, warranting a low confidence assessment.

title_zh: 致编辑的信:“血液系统恶性肿瘤中的院内呼吸道病毒感染:进展为下呼吸道感染的危险因素”。
source_body_en: This Correspondence responds to Oh and colleagues' study on nosocomial respiratory virus infections in hematologic malignancies and risk factors for progression to lower respiratory tract infection. We raise three methodological concerns: (1) the landmark analysis used to evaluate URTI-stage ribavirin therapy excludes patients who progressed or died before landmark time points, introducing selection bias by conditioning on a collider; (2) antiviral therapy analyses are severely underpowered (only 15 PIV and 9 RSV treated patients), with wide confidence intervals precluding definitive conclusions and substantial Type II error risk; and (3) combining glucocorticoid exposures from different indications (short-course pulse vs. prolonged therapy) may mask heterogeneous effects on immune function and viral progression. We commend the authors' risk stratification framework while urging cautious interpretation of antiviral efficacy data and recommending future prospective studies with adequate sample sizes and refined corticosteroid characterization.
abstract_zh: 本通讯回应了 Oh 及其同事关于血液系统恶性肿瘤中的院内呼吸道病毒感染以及进展为下呼吸道感染的危险因素的研究。我们提出了三个方法学问题:(1)用于评估 URTI 阶段利巴韦林治疗的里程碑分析排除了在里程碑时间点之前进展或死亡的患者,通过对撞机的调节引入了选择偏差;(2) 抗病毒药物 治疗分析的效力严重不足(仅 15 名 PIV 和 9 名 RSV 治疗患者),置信区间宽,无法得出明确的结论,并且存在大量 II 型错误风险;(3) 结合不同适应症(短程脉冲治疗与长期治疗)的糖皮质激素暴露可能掩盖对免疫功能和病毒进展的异质性影响。我们赞扬作者的风险分层框架,同时敦促谨慎解释 抗病毒药物 疗效数据,并建议未来进行具有足够样本量和精细皮质类固醇特征的前瞻性研究。

title: Changes in Lung Sounds During the Acute Stage of RSV Acute Bronchiolitis in Infants.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Changes in the respiratory function over time in respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)-induced acute bronchiolitis were evaluated by a lung sound analysis. METHODS: We retrospectively examined changes in lung sound parameters over time in 54 children (median age, 7 months) diagnosed with RSV acute bronchiolitis. We evaluated the power of inspiratory and expiratory sounds using a conventional method and analyzed the frequency characteristics of inspiratory sounds using new automated analysis software program. We examined changes in these lung sound parameters over time during and after hospitalization and compared these data with those of age-matched healthy children. RESULTS: In 138 lung sound samples from 54 infants, the power of inspiratory and expiratory sounds was greatest within 4 days after the onset and improved over time. In contrast, the greatest changes in inspiratory sound parameters were observed at 5 to 10 days after the onset of RSV acute bronchiolitis. Some lung sound parameters in patients with RSV acute bronchiolitis did not return to normal even by 14 days after the onset. CONCLUSIONS: This finding is considered a characteristic of RSV acute bronchiolitis in infants and is meaningful in terms of post-treatment management.
journal: The Tokai journal of experimental and clinical medicine

title_zh: 婴儿 RSV 急性 毛细支气管炎 急性期肺音的变化。
source_body_en: OBJECTIVE: Changes in the respiratory function over time in respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)-induced acute bronchiolitis were evaluated by a lung sound analysis. METHODS: We retrospectively examined changes in lung sound parameters over time in 54 children (median age, 7 months) diagnosed with RSV acute bronchiolitis. We evaluated the power of inspiratory and expiratory sounds using a conventional method and analyzed the frequency characteristics of inspiratory sounds using new automated analysis software program. We examined changes in these lung sound parameters over time during and after hospitalization and compared these data with those of age-matched healthy children. RESULTS: In 138 lung sound samples from 54 infants, the power of inspiratory and expiratory sounds was greatest within 4 days after the onset and improved over time. In contrast, the greatest changes in inspiratory sound parameters were observed at 5 to 10 days after the onset of RSV acute bronchiolitis. Some lung sound parameters in patients with RSV acute bronchiolitis did not return to normal even by 14 days after the onset. CONCLUSIONS: This finding is considered a characteristic of RSV acute bronchiolitis in infants and is meaningful in terms of post-treatment management.
abstract_zh: 目的:通过肺音分析评估 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 诱导的急性 毛细支气管炎 呼吸功能随时间的变化。方法:我们回顾性检查了 54 名诊断为急性 RSV 毛细支气管炎 的儿童(中位年龄为 7 个月)肺音参数随时间的变化。我们使用传统方法评估吸气和呼气声音的功率,并使用新的自动分析软件程序分析吸气声音的频率特性。我们检查了住院期间和住院后这些肺音参数随时间的变化,并将这些数据与年龄匹配的健康儿童的数据进行了比较。结果:在 54 名婴儿的 138 个肺音样本中,吸气音和呼气音的力量在发病后 4 天内最强,并随着时间的推移而改善。相比之下,RSV 急性 毛细支气管炎 发病后 5 至 10 天观察到吸气音参数的最大变化。RSV急性毛细支气管炎患者的一些肺音参数即使在发病后14天也没有恢复正常。结论:这一发现被认为是婴儿 RSV 急性 毛细支气管炎 的一个特征,对于 毛细支气管炎 后的管理具有重要意义。

title: Durability of RSV Prefusion F Vaccine Protection across Two RSV Seasons
abstract: BACKGROUND: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is an important cause of hospitalization and death among older adults. Although first-season vaccine effectiveness against RSV-related hospitalization has been demonstrated for the bivalent RSV prefusion F protein-based vaccine (RSVpreF), data regarding the durability of protection beyond a single RSV season are lacking. METHODS: In a pragmatic, open-label trial with individual randomization, participants 60 years of age or older were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive RSVpreF vaccine or no vaccine during the 2024-2025 winter season. Participants were followed through the 2025-2026 winter season to evaluate protection across two consecutive RSV seasons after a single vaccine dose. The primary endpoint was RSV-related respiratory tract disease (RTD) hospitalization. Secondary endpoints included RSV-related and all-cause lower respiratory tract disease hospitalization, all-cause respiratory hospitalization, all-cause cardiorespiratory hospitalization, and all-cause mortality. RESULTS: Of 131,379 participants who underwent random assignment, 130,991 were included in the intention-to-treat population during the second season. During the second RSV season, the incidence rate of RSV-related RTD hospitalization was 0.11 events per 1000 person-years in the RSVpreF group and 0.25 events per 1000 person-years in the control group, corresponding to a vaccine effectiveness of 56.2% (95% confidence interval [CI], -12.4% to 84.8%), as compared with 83.3% (95% CI, 42.9%-96.9%) during the first season. Across both seasons, the corresponding incidence rates were 0.11 and 0.37 events per 1000 person-years in the RSVpreF and control groups, respectively, with a vaccine effectiveness of 70.6% (95% CI, 39.1%-87.0%). There was no apparent difference in all-cause respiratory and cardiorespiratory hospitalization outcomes in the second season among those randomly assigned to vaccine or no vaccine in the first season. CONCLUSIONS: Among adults 60 years of age or older, the RSVpreF vaccine was associated with a lower incidence of RSV-related respiratory tract disease during a second RSV season as compared to no vaccine. Vaccine effectiveness estimates appeared to be lower in the second season compared to the first. (Funded by Pfizer; ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06684743.).

METHODS: In a pragmatic, open-label trial with individual randomization, participants 60 years of age or older were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive RSVpreF vaccine or no vaccine during the 2024-2025 winter season. Participants were followed through the 2025-2026 winter season to evaluate protection across two consecutive RSV seasons after a single vaccine dose. The primary endpoint was RSV-related respiratory tract disease (RTD) hospitalization. Secondary endpoints included RSV-related and all-cause lower respiratory tract disease hospitalization, all-cause respiratory hospitalization, all-cause cardiorespiratory hospitalization, and all-cause mortality. RESULTS: Of 131,379 participants who underwent random assignment, 130,991 were included in the intention-to-treat population during the second season. During the second RSV season, the incidence rate of RSV-related RTD hospitalization was 0.11 events per 1000 person-years in the RSVpreF group and 0.25 events per 1000 person-years in the control group, corresponding to a vaccine effectiveness of 56.2% (95% confidence interval [CI], -12.4% to 84.8%), as compared with 83.3% (95% CI, 42.9%-96.9%) during the first season. Across both seasons, the corresponding incidence rates were 0.11 and 0.37 events per 1000 person-years in the RSVpreF and control groups, respectively, with a vaccine effectiveness of 70.6% (95% CI, 39.1%-87.0%). There was no apparent difference in all-cause respiratory and cardiorespiratory hospitalization outcomes in the second season among those randomly assigned to vaccine or no vaccine in the first season. CONCLUSIONS: Among adults 60 years of age or older, the RSVpreF vaccine was associated with a lower incidence of RSV-related respiratory tract disease during a second RSV season as compared to no vaccine. Vaccine effectiveness estimates appeared to be lower in the second season compared to the first. (Funded by Pfizer; ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06684743.).

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the durability of protection provided by the bivalent RSV prefusion F protein-based vaccine (RSVpreF) across two consecutive RSV seasons in adults aged 60 years or older. The trial, conducted during the 2024-2025 and 2025-2026 winter seasons, found that vaccine effectiveness against RSV-related respiratory tract disease hospitalization was 56.2% in the second season, compared to 83.3% in the first. However, the effectiveness was lower in the second season, and there was no significant difference in all-cause respiratory and cardiorespiratory hospitalization outcomes. The study's limitations include potential bias due to its open-label design, and the evidence strength is moderate. These findings suggest that while the vaccine offers some protection, its efficacy may wane over time, highlighting the need for further research on booster strategies.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 是老年人住院和死亡的重要原因。缺乏有关 RSV 单个季节之后的保护持久性的数据。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在一项采用个体随机化的务实、开放标签试验中,60 岁或以上的参与者以 1:1 的比例分配,在 2024-2025 年冬季接受 RSVpreF 疫苗 或不接受 疫苗。对参与者进行了整个 2025-2026 年冬季的跟踪,以评估单次 疫苗 剂量后对连续两个 RSV 季节的保护作用。
elements_zh.methods: 主要终点是 RSV 相关呼吸道疾病 (RTD) 住院治疗。次要终点包括RSV相关和全因下呼吸道疾病住院、全因呼吸系统住院、全因心肺住院和全因死亡率。
elements_zh.main_results: 在131,379名参与随机分配的受试者中,130,991名在第二季度被纳入意向性治疗人群。在第二呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)流行季,RSVpreF组的RSV相关下呼吸道疾病(RTD)住院率为每1000人年0.11例,对照组为每1000人年0.25例,对应的疫苗有效率为56.2%(95%置信区间[CI]:-12.4%至84.8%),而第一季度为83.3%(95% CI:42.9%至96.9%)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 与没有 疫苗 的情况相比,RSVpreF 疫苗 与第二个 RSV 季节期间 RSV 相关呼吸道疾病的 发病率 较低相关。与第一季相比,第二季的 疫苗 效率估计似乎较低。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,RSVpreF 疫苗 在第二个季节为老年人提供了一些针对 RSV 相关住院的保护,尽管其有效性可能会随着时间的推移而减弱。这表明需要进一步研究 疫苗 的耐久性和潜在的助推器策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是一项务实的、开放标签的试验,具有个体随机化,这可能会引入偏差。由于研究的观察性质和潜在的混杂因素,证据强度中等。

title: Infection-triggered neurological deterioration and immunodeficiency in a case of RNU4ATAC-opathy
abstract: RNU4ATAC-opathy is a rare autosomal recessive disorder characterized by a wide clinical spectrum, including brain anomalies, seizures, strokes, immunodeficiency, and cardiac defects. Other manifestations include ophthalmologic, dermatologic, renal, gastrointestinal, auditory, and endocrine involvement. Here, we report the identification of pathogenic RNU4ATAC variants through whole exome sequencing in an infant presenting with microcephaly, growth failure, and immunodeficiency. We describe an 11-month-old infant who had been followed since 4 months of age for growth failure and developmental delay. During follow-up, the patient experienced episodes of neurological deterioration triggered by febrile illnesses associated with SARS-CoV-2 and respiratory syncytial virus infections (RSV) at 9 and 11 months of age, respectively. title: Detection Patterns and Temporal Dynamics of Multiple Pathogens in Wastewater Using a TaqMan Array Card
abstract: Background: Wastewater-based surveillance (WBS) complements clinical surveillance by capturing community-level circulation of infectious diseases, including asymptomatic infections.However, most multipathogen WBS studies have focused on pathogen detection and detection frequency, with limited evaluation of temporal changes using semi-quantitative Ct values.Objectives: This study aimed to characterize multipathogen detection patterns in wastewater using a customdesigned TaqMan Array Card (TAC) and explore temporal changes using semi-quantitative Ct values.Methods: Weekly influent samples (500 mL) were collected from two wastewater treatment plants in Cheonan and Asan during weeks 21~52 of 2025 (64 total samples).The TAC targeted 31 pathogen analysis groups encompassing respiratory, enteric, and selected high-concern pathogens, along with seven antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs).Pathogen occurrence was evaluated based on week-based detection status and detection frequency, while Ct values were interpreted as a semi-quantitative indicator for exploratory assessment of temporal changes.Samples failing the predefined quality control criteria were re-extracted and reanalyzed, and all samples were ultimately included in the final analysis.Results: Ten pathogens, including SARS-CoV-2, norovirus, adenovirus type F, and human rhinovirus, were detected in 100% of the study weeks.Influenza A virus and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) showed increased detection during winter, with influenza A/H3 and RSV type B predominating among their respective subtypes.Semi-quantitative Ct values showed no consistent increasing or decreasing trend for SARS-CoV-2, but they declined during winter for norovirus and influenza A. In contrast, RSV showed increased winter detection without a corresponding decrease in Ct values.bla_KPC, bla_NDM, and vanA/B/ C were detected in all study weeks, and mecA and bla_OXA also showed high detection frequencies.Conclusions: TAC-based WBS enabled simultaneous characterization of multipathogen detection patterns, antimicrobial resistance gene detection, and exploratory assessment of temporal changes using semiquantitative Ct values.These findings support TAC-based WBS as an integrated tool for community-level infectious disease surveillance.
journal: Korean Journal of Environmental Health Sciences

title: Reactive Infectious Mucocutaneous Eruption Following a Respiratory Infection in an Adolescent: A Case Report
abstract: Reactive infectious mucocutaneous eruption (RIME) is a recently defined mucocutaneous manifestation associated with respiratory infections, most commonly reported secondary to Mycoplasma pneumoniae.The core diagnostic criteria of RIME involve greater than or equal to two mucosal areas with erosive mucositis, minimal cutaneous lesions, a recent infectious prodrome, and exclusion of drug-induced etiologies.RIME presents with acute mucositis involving the oral, ocular, and genital mucosa, with presentations similar to other mucocutaneous disorders such as Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS), erythema multiforme (EM), and multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) secondary to SARS-CoV-2 infection.This case report describes a unique presentation of RIME secondary to a Mycoplasma infection, highlighting diagnostic challenges and therapeutic approaches.A 16-year-old male, previously healthy with no significant past medical history, was accepted for transfer to our hospital for evaluation of persistent fever, worsening left lower lobe pneumonia, oral mucositis, and conjunctivitis.On examination, extensive erythema and inflammation throughout the oral cavity, exudative pharyngitis, clear ocular discharge with conjunctival injection, and sloughing of the scrotal skin were noted.The patient's medical history and clinical examination raised initial suspicion of Kawasaki disease or possible MIS-C.Lab studies showed elevated CRP, ESR, and B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP), indicating extensive systemic inflammation; however, the PCR was negative for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), influenza A and B, and SARS-CoV-2.Further investigations revealed a positive Group A Streptococcus PCR on throat swab, felt to be colonization, and elevated Mycoplasma pneumoniae IgG titers suggested previous or recent exposure; however, acute infection could not be confirmed due to negative PCR and IgM.The patient improved over the following several days after initiation of azithromycin, continuation of clindamycin, and wound care for scrotal and oral mucosal lesions.Differentiating RIME from other mucocutaneous disorders is vital to prescribing proper treatment and preventing further systemic effects.This case underscores the importance of considering Mycoplasma as a potential etiology in patients presenting with mucocutaneous lesions and conjunctivitis following a previous respiratory infection.

title: Sociodemographic and Clinical Factors Related to Admission to the Pediatric Intensive Care Unit in Patients Hospitalized with COVID-19: A Post-Pandemic Study
abstract: Abstract Background The impact of COVID-19 on children has varied over time. title: Mortality rate and predictors of mortality of pediatric sepsis and septic shock in a Moroccan tertiary care center
abstract: Background Sepsis is the leading cause of child mortality worldwide. Pediatric sepsis-related mortality in Africa is estimated to be as high as 40%. We aimed to assess sepsis-related mortality and to identify predictors of mortality in pediatric sepsis. Methods We conducted a retrospective observational study of children admitted to the PICU for sepsis or septic shock. Statistical analysis was performed using Jamovi version 2.3.28. Continuous variables are expressed as mean ± standard deviation (SD) and categorical variables as frequencies and percentages. The Mann–Whitney U test assessed the association between the pediatric sequential sepsis-related organ failure assessment “pSOFA” score and mortality. Logistic regression was used to identify mortality predictors. Model performance was assessed based on discrimination and calibration. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. Results We enrolled 130 patients. The mean age was 32.5 months (SD: 47.12, range: 1–180). The identified infection sites were pneumonia (53.1%), central nervous system (23.8%), gastrointestinal tract (15.4%), bloodstream (4.5%), bone and joint (2.3%), and urinary tract (0.8%). Biological assessment showed the following mean values: 14,076 E/mm 3 for leukocytes (SD: 9,162, range: 350–59,100), 349 x 10 3 E/mm 3 for platelets (SD: 214, range: 10–939) and 111 mg/L for C-reactive protein “CRP” (SD 122, range:1–480). The median pSOFA score was six (range: 2–18). A microorganism was isolated in 32.3% of cases, including SARS-CoV-2 (5.2%), Streptococcus pneumoniae (3.7%), respiratory syncytial virus (3%), and Pseudomonas aeruginosa (2.3%). The overall mortality rate was 50%. Statistical analysis showed an association between the pSOFA score and mortality ( p < 0.001). Lower platelet count, vasopressor use, and mechanical ventilation were independently associated with mortality. The logistic regression model performed well with a p -value < 0.001 and a McFadden R 2 of 0.415. The area under the ROC curve was 0.888. The sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy were 88.9%, 85.1%, and 87.0%, respectively, with acceptable calibration. Conclusion Our research assessed pediatric sepsis in Morocco, a lower-middle-income North African country. Mortality rates were higher compared to high-income countries. The pSOFA score was effective in predicting severity and mortality. Lower platelet count, vasopressor use, and mechanical ventilation were identified as independent predictors of mortality.

title: 23 | Impact of educational interventions in childbirth classes on uptake of recommended vaccinations during pregnancy in the metropolitan area of Palermo, Sicily
abstract: Maternal immunization represents an effective public health strategy for the prevention of vaccine-preventable infections during pregnancy and in the first months of life [1]. Despite the recommendations introduced by the Italian Ministry of Health in 2018, vaccination coverage during pregnancy remains suboptimal [2]. In this context, vaccine counselling provided during childbirth classes may improve both knowledge and vaccine uptake. Materials and Methods. Between January 2025 and March 2026, an observational study was conducted among pregnant women attending childbirth classes at three hospitals in the metropolitan area of Palermo. Participants completed an anonymous Google Forms questionnaire assessing knowledge, attitudes, and vaccination practices. An educational intervention on maternal immunization, the cocoon strategy, and childhood vaccinations during the first year of life was subsequently delivered by physicians from the University of Palermo. Vaccine uptake was evaluated 30 days later through telephone or email follow-up. Among the 132 pregnant women enrolled, uptake of the dTpa vaccine reached 92% (relative post-intervention increase - PII: 55%), influenza vaccination uptake was 43% (PII: +26%), and COVID-19 vaccination uptake was 5% (PII: +3%). Previous influenza vaccination was strongly associated with vaccine uptake during pregnancy, both for influenza vaccination (OR:30.61; 95%CI:6.84–136.97; p-value=< 0.001) and COVID-19 vaccination (OR:5.6; 95%CI:1.177-26.748; p-value=< 0.05). Furthermore, vaccine-related knowledge was significantly associated with the uptake of at least one recommended maternal vaccine, including awareness of the correct timing of influenza vaccination (OR:6.1; 95%CI: 2.378-15.682; p-value=< 0.001), knowledge of the recommendation for Tdap vaccination during pregnancy (OR 10.09; 95%CI:2.524-40.343; p-value= <0.01) and its administration during every pregnancy (OR: 7.8; 95%CI:0.970-64.217; p-value= <0.05), and awareness of RSV (OR: 14.87; 95%CI:1.824-121.206; p-value= <0.01). Vaccine counselling interventions delivered during childbirth classes appear to be effective in improving uptake of vaccinations recommended during pregnancy. The systematic integration of these strategies into regional maternity care pathways is desirable in order to increase vaccination coverage and strengthen maternal and infant health prevention.

title: A decade of maternal RSV vaccine trials: what remains unresolved and why it matters
abstract: “A lot of work is still needed to prioritize which vaccines pregnant women should receive, which will differ depending on region and disease burden.”Ashling Cannon, Editor, Vaccine Insights , speaks with Shabir Madhi, Dean of the Faculty of Health Sciences and Director, South African Medical Research Council Vaccines and Infectious Diseases Analytics Research Unit (Wits VIDA), University of the Witwatersrand) about the questions a decade of maternal respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccine trials has raised but not resolved: why efficacy diverges markedly between trial sites, what the unexplained preterm birth signal that led to early termination of the GSK maternal RSV program means for the field, and why no validated correlate of protection for infant RSV disease has yet been established. Madhi also addresses the design of the RSV_IMPACT study, which is powered to investigate both the prematurity signal and the correlate question, the ALIVE program’s progress in building vaccinology research capacity across Africa, and why combination vaccines represent the single systemic advance that would most accelerate maternal immunization uptake over the next decade.

title: Early-life respiratory infections and their association with chronic lung disease: an expert perspective
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Early-life respiratory infections may disrupt lung development during critical fetal, neonatal, and infant windows, when alveolarization, airway and vascular maturation, and immune programming remain active, potentially causing effects beyond the acute illness. AREAS COVERED: This narrative review examines prenatal and postnatal respiratory infections and long-term respiratory outcomes, with emphasis on chorioamnionitis, fetal inflammatory responses, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, respiratory syncytial virus, and other pathogens. Literature was identified through targeted searches of biomedical databases and reference lists using terms related to early-life infection, lung development, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, wheeze, asthma, lung function, COPD, and respiratory mortality. Priority was given to systematic reviews, meta-analyses, longitudinal cohorts, mechanistic studies, and relevant reports. Proposed pathways include impaired alveolar and vascular growth, epithelial injury, immune dysregulation, trained immunity, airway remodeling, and reduced peak lung function. Epidemiological evidence linking early lower respiratory tract infection with recurrent wheeze, asthma, impaired lung function, COPD-like trajectories, and respiratory mortality is appraised. EXPERT OPINION: Early respiratory infections likely contribute to chronic morbidity through interactions among pathogen, timing, host susceptibility, prematurity, and environmental exposures. Causality remains difficult to establish. Newly available respiratory syncytial virus prevention strategies may clarify whether preventing severe infection improves long-term lung health. Standardized outcomes and longitudinal follow-up are essential.

The central question is whether RSV infections during critical developmental stages contribute to long-term respiratory outcomes such as wheeze, asthma, impaired lung function, and respiratory mortality.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The evidence base includes biomedical databases and reference lists, with searches using terms related to early-life infection, lung development, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, wheeze, asthma, lung function, COPD, and respiratory mortality. Priority was given to systematic reviews, meta-analyses, longitudinal cohorts, mechanistic studies, and relevant reports.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that early-life RSV infections likely contribute to chronic respiratory morbidity through interactions involving pathogen, timing, host susceptibility, prematurity, and environmental exposures. However, causality remains difficult to establish due to the complexity of these interactions.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There is heterogeneity in the evidence, with conflicting findings on the causal relationship between RSV and chronic lung disease. The review highlights the need for standardized outcomes and longitudinal follow-up to better understand the long-term effects of RSV infections. analysis.research_and_practice_implications: New prevention strategies for RSV may provide insights into whether reducing severe infections can improve long-term lung health. It highlights the biological and epidemiological evidence suggesting that RSV may contribute to respiratory outcomes such as wheeze, asthma, and impaired lung function. It also identifies gaps in the evidence, including the need for standardized outcomes and more detailed mechanistic studies. The implications suggest that RSV prevention strategies could offer valuable insights into improving long-term respiratory health, and further research is needed to clarify the underlying mechanisms and confirm causal relationships.

title: Upper-airway organism detection profiles in children with respiratory tract infection assessed by targeted next-generation sequencing: a single-centre descriptive study in Changzhou, China, August 2022 to March 2024
abstract: Respiratory tract infection (RTI) is among the commonest reasons for children to seek medical care, and the spectrum of organisms detected in the airway may shift with epidemic-prevention policies and with the epidemic cycles of individual organisms. This study describes the profile of organisms detected in throat swabs from children presenting with RTI in Changzhou, China, between August 2022 and March 2024, a period that spans the abrupt relaxation of China’s COVID-19 prevention policies in December 2022. In this single-centre, retrospective, descriptive study, 2049 throat swab samples from pediatric respiratory tract infection patients of Changzhou Children’s Hospital from Aug 2022 to Mar 2024 were collected and detected by targeted next-generation sequencing technology that can simultaneously detect 107 organisms. Patients were stratified by age (< 1, 1 to < 3, 3 to < 7, 7 to < 13, and 13 to < 18 years) and by season (spring, March-May; summer, June-August; autumn, September-November; winter, December-February). Proportions are reported with 95% CIs; groups were compared using chi-square or Fisher’s exact tests followed by pairwise proportion tests with Bonferroni correction. Among 2049 RTI samples tested by targeted next-generation sequencing, the overall positivity rate was 98.00% (2008/2049). Haemophilus influenzae , Streptococcus pneumoniae and Mycoplasma pneumoniae were the most frequently identified organisms. Co-detection of two or more organisms occurred in 81.97% (1646/2008; 95% CI: 80.23%-83.59%) of samples with at least one organism detected. Age- and season-specific heterogeneity in the positivity rate was found. Notably, respiratory syncytial virus detection patterns changed during the study period. Rhinovirus and Streptococcus pneumoniae continued to be detected during strict prevention measures. Positivity rates of the most frequently detected organisms, except Mycoplasma pneumoniae , increased during the three months after relaxation. tNGS of throat swabs revealed frequent organism detection and co-detection, with marked age- and season-related variation, in children presenting with RTI during the post-pandemic transition.

Proportions are reported with 95% CIs; groups were compared using chi-square or Fisher’s exact tests followed by pairwise proportion tests with Bonferroni correction. Among 2049 RTI samples tested by targeted next-generation sequencing, the overall positivity rate was 98.00% (2008/2049). Haemophilus influenzae , Streptococcus pneumoniae and Mycoplasma pneumoniae were the most frequently identified organisms. Co-detection of two or more organisms occurred in 81.97% (1646/2008; 95% CI: 80.23%-83.59%) of samples with at least one organism detected. Age- and season-specific heterogeneity in the positivity rate was found. Notably, respiratory syncytial virus detection patterns changed during the study period. Rhinovirus and Streptococcus pneumoniae continued to be detected during strict prevention measures. Positivity rates of the most frequently detected organisms, except Mycoplasma pneumoniae , increased during the three months after relaxation. tNGS of throat swabs revealed frequent organism detection and co-detection, with marked age- and season-related variation, in children presenting with RTI during the post-pandemic transition.

title: Immunity Interrupted: Links Between SARS-CoV-2 And the Tripledemic Of 2022
abstract: One hypothesis for the tripledemic and RSV surge of 2022 is possible viral-viral interaction and immune suppression following SARS-CoV-2 infection. Our objective was to compare the risk of viral re-infection and concurrent infections in children with and without SARS-CoV-2 infection. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using electronic health record data from pediatric emergency rooms in a health care system with numerous locations throughout the state. We included children under the age of 18 yrs. diagnosed with a viral upper respiratory infection between January 1st, 2021, and December 31st, 2023. The comparison groups were children with (a) SARS-CoV-2 alone, (b) SARS-CoV-2 and another respiratory virus, and (c) with viral infections excluding SARS-CoV-2. The primary outcome was viral re-infection in the subsequent 15 to 120 days. The secondary outcomes were the frequency of concurrent viral infections as well as clinical outcomes (i.e., oxygen use, length of stay, etc.). We included data from 37,116 patients. The cohorts consisted of 4,004 with SARS-CoV-2 alone, 1,678 with SARS-CoV-2 + another virus, and 31,434 with non-SARS-CoV-2 viruses. When comparing the SARS-CoV-2 only group (a) by ICD 10 code to the other two groups the odds of having a re-infection were higher in the other groups. The odds ratio (OR) in Group C was 1.42 and the OR was 1.38 in Group B with a reinfection rate of 4.4%, 6.0%, and 6.1% respectively in Groups A, B, and C. For the lab confirmed infection rates, the OR of having a recurrent infection in the other 2 groups compared to the SARS-CoV-2 only group was 1.44 with a re-infection rate of 2% compared to 2.8% in the other groups. Indicating viral re-infection was less common in those with SARS-CoV-2. The most common viruses seen in re-infection in all three groups were RSV, SARS-CoV-2, and Influenza. In group A these made up 37.7% (n=26), 33.3%(n=23), and 23.2% (n=16) respectively. In group B they made up 29.3% (n=12), 39.0% (n=16), 29.3%(n=12) and in C 32.4% (n=231), 29.2% (n=208), and 26.6% (n=190) respectively. Among those with lab confirmed re-infection, rates of having multiple viral infection at once on re-infection were low at 0.4% (n=13), 0.3% (n=4), and 0.3% (n=69) in groups a,b, and c. There was no increased risk of viral re-infection or concurrent infection in children with SARS-CoV-2 infection within 4 months. Re-infection with multiple viruses at once in any group was rare. Finally, the most frequently seen infections during the study period were SARS-CoV-2, RSV, and Influenza with RSV being the most prevalent overall.

title: Clesrovimab in prevention of RSV lower respiratory tract disease: a profile of its use in infants
abstract: Clesrovimab (ENFLONSIATM, clesrovimab-cfor), a long-acting monoclonal antibody that targets the respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) fusion protein, is a useful addition to prophylactic options for RSV-associated lower respiratory tract (LRT) disease in neonates and infants born during or entering their first RSV season. As demonstrated in the phase 2b/3 CLEVER clinical trial, a single 105 mg dose of clesrovimab, irrespective of body weight, provides durable protection against RSV-associated medically-attended lower respiratory infection (RSV-MALRI), and reduces RSV-associated hospitalizations in neonates and infants born during or entering their first RSV season. Pharmacokinetic data from the phase 3 SMART trial supports the efficacy of clesrovimab in infants and children at increased risk of severe RSV disease. Clesrovimab was generally well tolerated, with low reactogenicity, and had a similar adverse event profile to placebo (CLEVER) and palivizumab (SMART). Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a significant cause of infant hospitalizations and deaths. Clesrovimab (ENFLONSIATM), a novel long-acting monoclonal antibody (mAb) that binds a highly conserved site on the RSV fusion protein, was recently approved in the USA and the EU for the prevention of RSV-associated lower respiratory tract (LRT) disease in neonates and infants born during or entering their first RSV season. As demonstrated in clinical trials, clesrovimab, administered as a single 105 mg dose regardless of body weight, provides durable protection against RSV disease in neonates and infants born during or entering their first RSV season. Data from a phase 3 clinical trial supports the efficacy of clesrovimab in infants and children aged < 2 years at increased risk of severe RSV disease. Clesrovimab is well tolerated, with low rates of adverse events. As the second long-acting mAb approved for prevention of RSV disease, clesrovimab represents a useful addition to treatment options for neonates and infants born during or entering their first RSV season.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates clesrovimab, a long-acting monoclonal antibody targeting the RSV fusion protein, as a prophylactic option for RSV-associated lower respiratory tract disease in neonates and infants during their first RSV season. The phase 2b/3 CLEVER trial demonstrated that a single 105 mg dose of clesrovimab provides durable protection against RSV disease and reduces hospitalizations. Pharmacokinetic data from the phase 3 SMART trial further supports its efficacy. Clesrovimab was well tolerated with a low reactogenicity profile and similar adverse events to placebo and palivizumab. The findings suggest that clesrovimab represents a novel and effective treatment option for RSV disease in high-risk infants. However, the evidence is based on clinical trials, which may limit generalizability, though the results are robust and indicate moderate confidence in its efficacy.

title_zh: Clesrovimab 预防 RSV 下呼吸道疾病:其在婴儿中的应用概况
source_body_en: Clesrovimab (ENFLONSIATM, clesrovimab-cfor), a long-acting monoclonal antibody that targets the respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) fusion protein, is a useful addition to prophylactic options for RSV-associated lower respiratory tract (LRT) disease in neonates and infants born during or entering their first RSV season. As demonstrated in the phase 2b/3 CLEVER clinical trial, a single 105 mg dose of clesrovimab, irrespective of body weight, provides durable protection against RSV-associated medically-attended lower respiratory infection (RSV-MALRI), and reduces RSV-associated hospitalizations in neonates and infants born during or entering their first RSV season. Pharmacokinetic data from the phase 3 SMART trial supports the efficacy of clesrovimab in infants and children at increased risk of severe RSV disease. Clesrovimab was generally well tolerated, with low reactogenicity, and had a similar adverse event profile to placebo (CLEVER) and palivizumab (SMART). Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a significant cause of infant hospitalizations and deaths. Clesrovimab (ENFLONSIATM), a novel long-acting monoclonal antibody (mAb) that binds a highly conserved site on the RSV fusion protein, was recently approved in the USA and the EU for the prevention of RSV-associated lower respiratory tract (LRT) disease in neonates and infants born during or entering their first RSV season. As demonstrated in clinical trials, clesrovimab, administered as a single 105 mg dose regardless of body weight, provides durable protection against RSV disease in neonates and infants born during or entering their first RSV season. Data from a phase 3 clinical trial supports the efficacy of clesrovimab in infants and children aged < 2 years at increased risk of severe RSV disease. Clesrovimab is well tolerated, with low rates of adverse events. As the second long-acting mAb approved for prevention of RSV disease, clesrovimab represents a useful addition to treatment options for neonates and infants born during or entering their first RSV season.

title: PIWIL4 regulates gene expression and piRNA levels in RSV-infected airway epithelial cells
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of acute lower respiratory tract infections with significant morbidity and mortality in young children, the elderly and immunocompromised hosts. Despite its clinical burden, no effective RSV vaccine or therapy exists for infants, only prophylactic treatment. Small non-coding RNAs have emerged as important regulators of host-pathogen interactions. PIWI-interacting RNAs (piRNAs) are a distinct class of small non-coding RNAs known for maintaining the genome complexity and integrity in gonadal cells. However, there is growing evidence of their role in controlling gene expression in somatic cells. The biogenesis and function of piRNAs is associated with P-element Induced Wimpy testis (Piwi) proteins, whose function in the respiratory epithelium in response to infections remains largely unexplored. Here, we characterize the expression and function of the Piwi-like protein PIWIL4 in the context of RSV infection. We found that PIWIL4 is expressed in both primary and immortalized small airway epithelial cells and is significantly induced at the mRNA and protein levels following RSV infection or poly I:C stimulation, a proxy of viral infection. Immunofluorescence microscopy revealed that PIWIL4 was primarily nuclear in uninfected cells but translocated to the cytoplasm upon RSV exposure. While siRNA-mediated knockdown of PIWIL4 did not significantly affect RSV replication, it led to decreased secretion of several cytokines, chemokines and growth factors, indicating a role in modulating host innate immune responses. Transcriptomic analysis of PIWIL4-silenced iSAE cells showed significant changes in gene expression both in basal conditions and upon RSV infection. Ingenuity Pathway analysis of differentially expressed genes underscored the role of PIWIL4 in modulation of interferon signaling, cytokine production, stress and metabolic responses, as well as airway remodeling pathways. Silencing of PIWIL4 also resulted in global alteration of piRNA expression both in uninfected and infected cells. However, the predicted targets of the differentially expressed piRNAs had limited overlap with the differentially expressed genes identified by transcriptomics, suggesting a function of PIWIL4 in regulating airway epithelial cell responses at least in part independent of piRNAs. Taken together, our study uncovers an important role for PIWIL4 in somatic cells and position it as a key regulator of airway epithelial innate immunity. A better understanding of the mechanisms by which PIWIL4 affects host cells responses following a pathogen exposure may identify novel therapeutic strategies for RSV, as well as other viral respiratory infections.

analysis.study_design_and_population: The study characterized the expression and function of the Piwi-like protein PIWIL4 in the context of RSV infection. It focused on primary and immortalized small airway epithelial cells, examining both baseline and infected conditions.
analysis.methods: The study used siRNA-mediated knockdown of PIWIL4 to assess its impact on RSV replication and host immune responses. Transcriptomic analysis was performed to evaluate gene expression changes in PIWIL4-silenced cells, and immunofluorescence microscopy was used to observe PIWIL4 localization.
analysis.main_results: PIWIL4 is expressed in both primary and immortalized small airway epithelial cells and is significantly induced at the mRNA and protein levels following RSV infection or poly I:C stimulation. Immunofluorescence microscopy revealed that PIWIL4 was primarily nuclear in uninfected cells but translocated to the cytoplasm upon RSV exposure.
